|---|---|---|---|---|
| repo-safety, shell-check, source-block, and house-style's table | none of their tables' messages | each runs `tests/hooks/guard-cases.sh`, the guard crate's case tests, whose environment is the test thread's own (`shared::env`, 451 T32), so the `L7R_MESSAGE_CORPUS` that `hookrun.sh` exports never reached `protocol::keep` | `case_tables::drive` names the process's corpus in the thread's (`kept`), so each case goes `cli` -> `protocol::run` -> `keep`, the hook path | 28: repo-safety 3, shell-check 12, source-block 2, house-style 11 |
| guard-file | the root Makefile's and the roster's Read notices | its "another guard's Read keeps the generic context" case read the root Makefile, which takes its own notice | the case reads a guard script, `scripts/hooks/make-only-hooks.sh` | 1, the generic Read notice |
| set-down | its builder-slot, parked-stage and next-task blocks | the next-task block's two other forms were in no fixture | section 4b: a `[perf]` task named first; every task waiting, none named | 2 |

Two runs of the tables gave the same 28 keys (`/tmp/t174/keys1`, `keys1b`, a `diff` empty), measured 2026-11-23.

**THE CORPUS FILES STILL EMPTY, measured 2026-11-23** (`find .git/hooks-test/messages -empty` after the closing checks' `make hooks-test`, read against `.claude/settings.json`'s hooks and each guard's `decide`): T170's census less the 3 suites filled above leaves 14; today's corpus holds 61 files, 15 of them empty, and none of the 15 is a message a guard says to a session:
- 13 are suites of scripts no hook runs: claims-gate, closing-checks, cohort-gate, entry-gate, l7r-gate (3 parts), land-tooling, plan-gate, review-gate and sync-with-main, and parts (2 parts, `tests/hooks/parts.sh`, the suites' parallel runner). The one hook command in `.claude/settings.json` is `scripts/hooks/l7r-hook`, which calls none of them. Their output reaches a model as a command's result, which the check, held at `protocol::keep`, does not read; sync-with-main's reaches a session only through clone-sync's notice, which its own suite renders (`clone-sync-hooks.sh.jsonl`, 14,783 bytes, measured 2026-11-23 (`find -printf '%s'`)).
- 2 are guards that never answer: event-log's `decide` records its line and returns no answer, and stall-watchdog's starts its loop and says nothing (neither file builds an `Answer`).

**THE TASK LINE'S PREMISE, RESTATED** (measured 2026-11-23): finished-run's and set-down's Stop blocks do not bypass `protocol::run`. ### T182 (observed 2026-11-23, 451 T177 and `ask:guard-wordings-sleep-and-slot`: a round-arbiter tooling fix built in Rust inside the task being landed could not be settled - `make arbiter-fix-done` wanted its test on main, `LAND=` goes through `make land-tooling`, which rightly refuses `rust/`, and the task's own `make land` was refused by `fix_hold` until the fix was settled)

- **Approach**: `make arbiter-fix-done ID= NOTE= TEST= LANDING=<task> FILES="<the fix's files>" [F=<feature>]` checks that the fix is done with its test, that its files and test are committed in the clone as they stand, and that the task is an open task of F (by default the fix's own feature). It then writes no done row. It keeps the fix pending in the clone's git directory (`arbiter-fix-landing.json`, the reviews crate's `closing/landing.rs`), which both the arbiter and the task and land crates build on. The land's first pass reads its tasks' hold with the fixes pending on them left out (`fix_hold_landing`, through the tick's `Ask.landing`). `make land` writes each pending fix's done row into its home's `arbiter.jsonl` BEFORE the ticks, adds those logs to the tick commit, and forgets the entries once the push lands. DECISION: before the ticks, not after (the order the handoff drafted): the closing check at a feature's last tick reads the open fixes too, so rows written after would refuse a landing that closes its feature. A refused tick puts the logs back (`Settled::undo`), and a failed push's revert takes the rows out; the fix stays pending either way. A plain `make tick` is still held. `ENGINE=1` settled a fix committed here at once, so its done row reached main ahead of its code while the landing was still refused; `LANDING=` replaces it. `fix_hold`'s message and the on-main refusal name the route.

| step | figure | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| before | T177's fix reached main in another landing's push (`efcf9c44b7`, 449's), was settled by hand in a commit of its own (`4c52cd244e`), and T177 ticked in a third (`545a462773`), its landing refused until the settling; on HEAD's code the new tests: the task crate 86 passed, 1 failed (the first pass held by the fix its landing carries), the land crate 90 passed, 4 failed (each landing refused at its first pass), the arbiter crate 34 passed, 1 failed (no `LANDING=`), measured 2026-11-23, method: a detached worktree at HEAD with the new tests copied in, `make rust-test` per crate | no route carries a Rust fix and its task's tick together |
| after | one push: the land's tests show the fix's done row in the tick commit, in its home's log (this feature's or another's), a landing that closes its feature carrying its fix, and a refused tick or failed push settling nothing, measured 2026-11-23, method: `make crate-checks` over the reviews, task, land and arbiter crates | fix and tick reach main in one push, or neither does |

### T165, T166, T172 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A builder's engine edit in the clone waits on no review that reads its own tree (T175, kept); `make verify` warns of undeclared occasions only when the bundle it verifies declares none, whatever another builder's task-start or set-down did to the clone's mark; the guard wrapper's suite fails only when a call waits on another's build.

**The idle-check mechanism and its evidence** (the hooks reference, `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md`, read 2026-11-23, and the claude-code-guide agent's reading of the scheduled-tasks, tools and plugin pages): a cron's fire "submits a prompt" - always a turn, no "only if non-empty" mode; `Notification` `idle_prompt` "can't block or modify notifications" and cannot inject; a Stop hook's `additionalContext` still continues the turn; a plugin monitor is model- or plugin-started, with no settings route. One documented mechanism stays silent: a command hook with `asyncRewake: true` "runs in the background and wakes Claude on exit code 2", and "an `asyncRewake` hook that exits with code 2 wakes Claude immediately even when the session is idle". So the idle check is a second Stop entry, `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/scripts/hooks/l7r-hook Idle` (asyncRewake, timeout 420 s, a CONVENTION: above the wait's 300 s GUESS), which runs `l7r-guard --idle-check`: silent at once for a sub-agent's stop or a Stop whose `background_tasks` (the harness's own list: shell, subagent, monitor, workflow) names anything; else it waits `L7R_IDLE_CHECK_SECS` (a GUESS of 300 s, the GM's "every 5 minutes"), is silent where the transcript gained a `user` or `assistant` record since (the session was active, and that turn's Stop arms the next check), and otherwise says the set-down block on stderr with exit 2. Periodic by construction: every idle stretch begins at a Stop, and each Stop arms one check.

**Holds** (`set_down_hooks/holds.rs`): the feature's newest `ask:set-down-...` ruling in its own `arbiter.jsonl`, ruled `continue` or `accept`, whose `what` says no new, other or further task starts, or sets the feature down (a CONVENTION: the arbiter's prose is read; matched against every set-down ruling on record - the 7 holds read as holds - the pilot's `4. Then set down. The work resumes from the GM's reply` (ask:set-down-449-pilot) among them, its set-down holding T171 and the rest of 449 (MODE 4 round 2, D11) - and the 8 go-ons, a bare do-not-start clause and the mid-landing waiver do not, pinned in `tests/idle.rs`). Only a later set-down ruling ends a hold, never a task-start (T183 itself was started under the 451 hold); a task-start's own refusal never reads a hold. **A task a ruling holds by name is never the idle check's next** (MODE 4, D6): the same newest ruling's do-not-start clause (`Do not start T150-T158`, the pilot's form) holds each task it names, a range each member and never a task named elsewhere in the ruling; on record every such clause stands beside a set-down (the pilot's, `Set feature 449 down now and do not start T83`, `Set 444 down now; do not start T19's build`), so the feature hold covers those too, and the clause alone holds its tasks under a ruling that sends other work on; with only held tasks open the check is silent, and a later set-down ruling ends it as it ends a feature's (`holds::named`, pinned in `tests/idle.rs`; `make task-start`'s picker does not read it, so a start the GM approved is never refused).

    stay `settle_quotes`', which already settles one whose quoted words and claim did not change and re-owes one whose quoted words
    changed, whoever changed them (a claim change). The categories, decided:
    - wording (never re-owes): modal-form (its contract: "A replacement only rewords"), record-format (VOCABULARY, SESSION NOTE,
      HISTORY: how a reader meets the words), record-style (presentation), intro-check (a question's opening), modal-depiction LINKS
      (a pointer to a drawing page, no fact stated).
    - factual (may re-owe and cascade): modal-research ACCURACY, REFERENCES (what a statement rests on) and GAPS (a statement added);
      modal-depiction COVERAGE and TRUTH; quote-check, source-reader, translation-check and entry-drift findings; and any EDIT whose
      check or category is untold - so a mislabel costs a round, never a skipped review.

    `### The change since round <n> (451 T189)`: every run of lines of the subject's files that differs from what the last round was
    bundled - an EDIT's or a hand edit's alike - its whole old and new text paired. What each round was bundled is kept when its

    dispatch overwriting it, rounds before the last dropped); a subject whose last round was bundled before the keeping gets no change
    section, so its round reads the whole unit, unscoped as before - the judge-only instruction is given only where every change since
    the last round is paired. Each comes with the instruction to judge ONLY whether the change made something wrong, the
    unit in the bundle for context, nothing it did not touch re-opened; the ten record and pop-up check contracts' Earlier rounds
    paragraph says so.
  - T190, SETTLED CHOICES STAY SETTLED: `apply_edits/settled.rs` reads the check state's other rounds' EDITs and refuses, before
    anything is applied, an EDIT whose new text is an earlier EDIT's old and whose old is its new, unless its finding carries
    `REVERSES round <n>:` and an `evidence:` quoting the words or naming the page, and its check's category is factual; the refusal
    names that form. The ten contracts say it beside their existing `REVERSES round <n>:`.

### T185 (the GM 2026-11-23, request.md 'the convergence talk': "as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page where the full information can be found, then nothing needs to cascade simply because a split occurs")

- **Approach**: a split leaves a pointer of one marked form on its source page, `<a class="moved" href="NNNN-<slug>[.drawing].html">` (`triage/change.rs`'s `POINTER`; the site build's link reader takes an attribute before `href`, `site_links.rs`, so it builds as any question link). A pop-up's checks read the pages its `Entry:` and `Drawing:` name and the pages their pointers name (`modals::followed`: in its fingerprints, its owed rows, the triage's pages and the research and depiction bundles), so a later edit of a moved block on its new page re-owes the pop-up. The triage counts a removed block that stands verbatim on a page the pop-up reaches as moved, a new block that stood on a page it reached at its last check as moved in, and a block carrying only the pointer (no note mark, no figure, at most `POINTER_WORDS` words beside the link, a GUESS knob) as no claim; the claims triage drops the same moves and pointer blocks. The record checks needed nothing: `units.rs` indexes the base's blocks and notes across every page, so a block moved verbatim already owes no record check (measured on the fixture: none owed for the moved block). A move with no pointer stays a removal, and the MANIFEST tells the session the pointer's form. Measured 2026-11-23: no page carries the form yet (`grep -rlE '<a\s+class="moved"' research/questions`: 0), so every pop-up's fingerprint and owed row stands as it was.

### T184 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** No research page loses a claim to fit the size cap: a page over it is split with a pointer, or, one indivisible topic, carries an audited limit of its own.

Constitution XII (citations verbatim). Other builders' files (T188-T190) untouched.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: request.md 2026-11-23. R: docs/research-record-rules.md. O: the word diff and the real-commit run above.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the guard was run on the real trim commit and on the repaired pages (the delta run green on the working tree).
5. **The order.** The page sessions first (they were queued before the guard was built), the guard then run over their pages as the green fixture.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T184 F=451` green, the record checks of the page sessions recorded, `make question-sizes` naming none. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.

8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST above; after: `make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/checks` 159 passed (a plain link refused, the `moved` form kept), 2026-11-23 (`/tmp/t184/item4-green.log`); the delta check green on the restored and split pages.

11. **Before fitting things into room.** Room first: a split gives each topic its own page.
12. **Before any fix.** A reader of 0009 and 0059 met weakened claims (a qualifier gone, a source's restatement cut to a pointer at its footnote, a question's date gloss gone): wrong outcomes, fixed.

**Found and left?**
- The guard also names 0097 on cce80ca436 (qualifiers `none`, `not`): not a defect - both claims stand restated, observed 2026-11-23, method: `grep` of the dropped sentences' words over 0097 and 0331 as they stand now. "None gives a count of the staff or says who else lived inside" stands on 0331 as "No page we read counts who lived inside one, or says whether all its staff did"; "a Beijing courtyard house lodged its servants not in a rowhouse but in one of the ranges of rooms around its courtyard" stands on 0097 as "A Beijing courtyard house lodged its servants in the south range, one of the ranges of rooms around its courtyard", in the paragraph opening "China shows the other form, several rooms behind one door" - a correction to the range the source names, not a cut. The escape `SIZE_EDIT_OK` is the route for such a correction.

### T193 (the GM 2026-11-23, the task line; observed 2026-11-23: 451 T184's builder `a676c53072fd7258b` waited from 20:27:39Z to 21:35 on a watch that had ended, and the idle check said nothing)

- **What happened, measured 2026-11-23** (the coordinator's transcript `c6fd72d1-...jsonl`, its `subagents/` directory, 451's event log `.git/l7r-events/451-*.jsonl`): the builder ended its turn at 20:27:39 waiting on its Monitor `bx5gtybg3` ("Waiting for the follow-ups session"); the coordinator's Stops listed `bx5gtybg3` in `background_tasks` through 20:39:12 and never after, so the watch ended then; its notice reached the builder's transcript only after the coordinator's message (record 846, stamped 20:39:12, written after record 842, stamped 21:35:26). The one Stop of the window with an empty list (21:04:56) reached `verdict`, which returned at 451's hold (`ask:set-down-451-gm-stop-for-convergence-talk`, "451 starts no new task") before anything read the builder; every other Stop of the window returned at the idle check's first test, a run listed. And the transcript reader did not know a Monitor's launch at all (its result opens `{"taskId": ..., "timeoutMs": ...}`, 214 of them in the transcripts of 2026-11-22 and 23, no other result opening `taskId`).
- **Approach**: a new `set_down_hooks/stalls.rs`. A builder (`builder_brief`: the session's own dispatch, its description opening with a feature number) that the session's transcript reads as running, whose task is still open in `tasks.md`, counts as running only while it has live work - the Stop's `background_tasks` names it, or a run or sub-agent its own transcript launched, or a sub-agent of its own wrote within the bound - or its own transcript (file mtime: records are not written in time order) moved within `STALL_SECS`. One with neither is STALLED. `idle_check` (idle.rs) now waits on every main-session Stop, not only one with an empty list; after its wait, where the session did not turn and the Stop gave its list, it names each stalled builder - its id, description, silent-since time, last line and `SendMessage to <id> "..."` - ahead of the hold and the open-task block (a hold holds new tasks, not a started builder's wake); each builder once while its line is unchanged (`once`, key `stalled <id>`), so a builder named a day ago is not said again beside a new one. A list naming a run still waits that run out for the open-task block, as before. `LAUNCHED` reads a Monitor's launch (set_down_hooks.rs). With no list (a harness before the field), no builder is named: live work cannot be told.

- **Approach**: Each of the three readers now refuses a reply holding a line it cannot read. The refusal names the line and the expected form, and nothing is recorded or applied.
  - **The pop-up triage** (`rust/gate/crates/owed/src/record/triage.rs`, `read_reply`): the reply is read whole before `record` writes anything. It refuses any of these: a non-blank line that is neither `NONE` nor in the form; a uid that is not of this triage (before this, that was a message and exit 0, with the rest cleared); an empty reply; `NONE` beside a TOUCHES line.
  - **The claims triage** (`rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/triage.rs`, `refused`): the same rules, called by `claims triaged` before `record_triage`, so `save_index` never runs on a refused reply. `record_triage` itself is unchanged for its callers that pass `""` (the tool's clear and the forced claims), observed 2026-11-23, method: `grep -rn "record_triage("` over the crate. Its unknown-key message is unreachable now and was removed. A claim key may hold spaces, so a non-ASCII dash with a later ` - ` reads as an unknown key and is refused.
  - **EDIT** (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/reply.rs`, `unread_edits` and `EDIT_FORM`): finds each line shaped as an EDIT header, or as a `<<<` fence, that stands in no block the parser reads. A header is a line whose first word, past any bullet, quote or bold, is `EDIT` (not `EDITS`). `record apply-edits` refuses on such a line before any block is applied or settled. The guard's own readers, the round state (`rounds.rs:856`, `freeze.rs:88`) and the bundles' displays, keep the parse. The refusal sits at the one reader that writes, observed 2026-11-23, method: `grep -rn "reply::blocks\|categorized("` over `rust/`, each caller read; the others are the round state and the arbiter and check bundles' displays, and only `record apply-edits` (`apply_edits.rs:417`, `apply_edits/settled.rs:59`) applies or settles a block.
  - **The agent files.** `modal-triage.md` now asks for `NONE` when nothing is touched; before, it asked for an empty reply, which is now refused. `claims-triage.md` says a line outside the form is refused.

### T197 (the gap audit of 2026-11-23, item 9: `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh` builds from the clone's working tree, so triage and apply-edits answers were judged with other builders' uncommitted code and landed with no build id, T184's first two triage runs on T185/T186's unlanded code; the 81 stale TOUCHES marks on T184's 21 pop-ups stand under `ask:t184-stale-triage-marks`, and no withdrawal verb is built, `ask:t197-rejudge-verb`)

- **Approach**: Three parts.
  - **(1) The build's id.** After each build, the launcher writes `$BIN.build.json` beside the binary: `{"commit": <HEAD>, "dirty": {<path>: <blob id or "deleted">}}`. The dirty set is the uncommitted files the binary builds from: its `SOURCES`, `rust/guard`, the Cargo files and `.cargo/config.toml`, untracked files included. Scoped that way, a clean build in a busy clone is not marked dirty by unrelated edits. The id is written at build time and not on each run, because a binary run under `L7R_GATE_STALE_OK` or `L7R_GATE_FRESH` does not match the tree. Every run exports it as `L7R_GATE_BUILD`, empty for a binary built before T197. `rust/gate/crates/core/src/build.rs` reads it (`current`, `landing`, `mixed`, `same`).
  - **(2) Answers carry their build.**
    - `owed`'s `write_answer`, the one writer of the triage, `record-checked` and `apply-edits` answers, keeps `builds: {fingerprint: build}`.
    - A settled answer keeps its judge's build, not the settling run's, since nothing judged it again. A pending settle takes its answer's build, and an adopted sibling answer brings its build along.
    - A claims-triage clear (`record_triage`) records `build` only where the build was dirty, so the tracked `dev/claims-index.json` moves only then. A clean build removes it.
  - **(3) A landing alone re-owes a mixed answer.** Under `L7R_LAND_ALONE`, `unanswered_in` and the claims `owed` owe again an answer whose build held an uncommitted file whose blob is not the landing's `HEAD:<path>`, naming the files. That is the other builders' code, or the builder's own older edit. A file deleted then and absent now counts as landed. An answer with no build, recorded before T197, stands as it always did. Refusing those would refuse every landing in every clone.

| step | figure | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| before | an answer's record holds no `builds`, measured 2026-11-23 (`/tmp/t195/red-build.saved.log`, "no entry found for key") | the answer cannot say what judged it |
| after | the launcher's sidecar matches the binary's `L7R_GATE_BUILD`, and every uncommitted source is at its `git hash-object` blob, measured 2026-11-23 (`tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.1.sh`, the "build id" cases, run on this clone with the other builders' files dirty) | the id names exactly the uncommitted code built |

### T207 (`make_only_hooks::tests::an_escape_is_recorded_with_its_reason` red under the coverage run and green alone, three times on 2026-11-23; the last `landbig2.log` line 143)

- **Approach**: The lead was the log writer dropping a record when its lock wait timed out. Measuring refuted it. `log::place` takes no lock: it makes the directory, writes a temporary and renames it. `tool.rs`'s `flock_within` is not on its path. The cause, measured on 2026-11-23:
  - **Reproduced.** The guard's test binary ran 8 suites side by side, each in its own `TMPDIR`, measured 2026-11-23 (`.git/t207/loop.sh`). The test failed 9 of 120, 7 of 80 and 10 of 80.
  - **The record was written.** A temporary print in `place` showed the test's record written and renamed into place in every failing run. The test's later read found 2 to 147 files in the log, measured 2026-11-23 (the test's own print of the directory).
  - **The log was emptied under it.** inotify on one loaded run (`.git/t207/watch.sh`, `.git/t207/inotify.txt`, excerpt `inotify-excerpt.txt`) caught the deletion. The record was renamed in at line 1039 and deleted at line 1286, among every other record. The directory was then removed and made again (line 1382), and a second pid wrote into it at once.
  - **The second pid is a child.** It is a hang pin's child run of the same binary (`guards::passes_in_time`, `current_exe()`; the make-only, readme and no-poll in-time tests). Its tests call `log::quiet()`, whose `Once` is the child's own. `tempdir::beside_binary("guard-tests-log")` then emptied the directory it inherited through `TMPDIR` and `GUARD_LOG_DIR`, while the parent's tests were still reading it. The same child could empty the log under `repo_safety_hooks`' and `scratch_sweep_hooks`' log reads.
  - **The fix (1), in `shared/src/log.rs` `quiet()`.** A process that inherits this run's own path (`<temp dir>/l7r-test-scratch/guard-tests-log`) as `GUARD_LOG_DIR`, with the directory there, keeps it. Any other inherited value is replaced as before, a session's real log among them. `beside_binary` is unchanged: no hang pin's child reaches another shared fixture.
  - **The fix (2): the test owns its state.** `log::dir()` reads the test thread's own `GUARD_LOG_DIR` first (`env::opt`), then the process's. The escape test names its own `TempDir` log and asserts its one record. The `env.rs` header says so. A normal build's `env::opt` is the process's variable, so its answer is unchanged.
  - **Fixed here, (3).** `scratch_sweep_hooks::tests::a_day_passes_between_sweeps_and_one_sweep_holds_the_lock` failed 3 times in the same 280 loaded runs, at its last assert: the 40-day mark was missing from the plan. The test set the mark's time through an open descriptor. A child forked by another test copies every open descriptor until it execs, and the plan, reading `/proc`, keeps a file a live process holds. That is inferred, not caught. The mark's time is now set by path (`touch -m -d @<secs>`), so no descriptor of it is open in the process.
  - **A decision, not a change: a failed write stays silent.** The brief asked that a record is never dropped silently: either it waits or it fails closed. That premise was the lock lead, and no write failed in any measured run. The drop was test-only: `quiet()` and `beside_binary` are built only under `test` or the `test-env` feature, which only `rust/guard`'s dev-dependency turns on (every `Cargo.toml` under `rust/`, grepped 2026-11-23). A real escape's record was never at risk this way. `log.rs`'s recorded rule stands: "A write that fails is silent: an entry must never cost the guard its answer." It costs this: a disk-full or permission failure loses a record with no word. Making `fire` refuse on a failed write was considered and rejected: it would turn a log fault into a refusal of correct work. That choice is MODE 4's to overrule.

| step | figure | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| red | `log/tests.rs` `a_child_run_of_the_tests_keeps_its_parents_log` ("the child emptied its parent's log") and `a_test_names_its_own_log` failed on the unfixed code, 2026-11-23 (`.git/t207/red.log`) | the child's wipe, pinned without load |
| before | 26 of 280 loaded suite runs red on the escape test (8 side by side, `.git/t207/loop.sh`) | the flake, reproduced |
| after | 104 of 104 loaded suite runs green, no test of any kind red (13 rounds of 8 side by side, the fixed binary, 2026-11-23, `.git/t207/proof.log`) | the flake and the sweep test's gone |

### T201 (451 T193's MODE 4 round 2, 2026-11-23: a builder whose live work outlasts the idle check's wait, the session silent, is named only at the session's next Stop)

- **Approach**: the idle check's looks ended at `WAIT_SECS` (600 s, a GUESS) past its first, under the Idle hook entry's `timeout` (960 s, a CONVENTION), so a builder whose own run (a Monitor, up to its 30-minute cap; a background shell, unbounded) ended after that, with no Stop after, was never named. Now `WAIT_SECS` is a Monitor's cap and the bound after it (`MONITOR_SECS` 1,800 + `STALL_SECS` 600 = 2,400 s), the Idle entry's `timeout` 2,760 s (the two waits and 60 s for the reads, a CONVENTION pinned by `the_hook_timeout_holds_both_waits`), so a watch that runs its full 30 minutes and ends unheard is named within one check. Live work still going at the deadline is HANDED ON (`idle::handed_on`): the check exits with one short notice, `IDLE CHECK: N builder(s) still working past its wait. End the turn; the next Stop re-arms the check.`, each builder's id and description under it. It is said every time, not once, because each wake is a new check. A detached successor cannot do this: only the hook's own exit 2 wakes the session (hooks reference, "Run hooks in the background", read 2026-11-23). The cost is one short turn every `IDLE_SECS` + `WAIT_SECS` (45 minutes, a CONVENTION: the sum of the two) while a builder's run outlasts the wait.
- **The cap, measured 2026-11-23** (Claude Code 2.1.330): a nested interactive session in tmux (`/tmp/t201m/proj`, `proj2`), its Stop hooks `asyncRewake`, each sleeping past or short of its `timeout` and logging its start, its SIGTERM or its end to `/tmp/t201m/hook*.log`. A 10 s timeout was killed at 10 s and a 1,200 s timeout at 1,200 s, past the old 960 s, so the timeout is enforced as set (measured 2026-11-23 (`hook.log`: start 1795477556, `C10s30 term` +10, `A1200s1500 term` +1,200)). A 2,400 s timeout with a 2,000 s sleep ran to its end and exited 2, and the pane showed the rewake ("hook B2400s2000 woke after 2000 s") (measured 2026-11-23 (`hook.log`: `B2400s2000 done` at +2,000)). A 3,000 s timeout with a 2,900 s sleep ran to its end and exited 2, and the pane showed the rewake (measured 2026-11-23 (`hook2.log`: start 1795478162, `D3000s2900 done` at +2,900)), so the 2,760 s timeout stands. A 4,000 s timeout with a 3,700 s sleep ran to its end and exited 2, and the pane showed the rewake (measured 2026-11-23 (`hook2.log`: start 1795478162, `E4000s3700 done` at +3,700)). The docs: "Claude Code still enforces `timeout` on a hook you run with `asyncRewake`", and they name no maximum (the claude-code-guide agent, hooks reference, 2026-11-23). The binary: the background hook's limit is `e.timeout?e.timeout*1000:Wp`, with no clamp found (`strings` of the 2.1.330 binary). `MEASURED_TIMEOUT_SECS` (2,900, the test's constant: D's sleep, the shortest run measured past the new timeout, with E's 3,700 s also run, measured 2026-11-23 (`hook2.log`)) holds the Idle entry's timeout under a figure measured to run.
- **The in-progress rule** (the coordinator's live false positives, 2026-11-23): the landed T193 rule named 451 T51's builder and 449 T158's at a Stop because both tasks were open. T51 was at its cap on 2026-11-22, its line `(waits: T138 lands)`, T138 open. T158 was done 2026-11-22 07:33 and parked: started 2026-11-22T06:12:24Z, with 449 set down at 2026-11-23T10:34:24Z, both read from `.git/task-starts.jsonl` and `.git/set-downs.jsonl`. `stalls::in_progress` names a builder only while its task is in progress, which needs all of these:
  - its box is open;
  - it was started since its last landing: a `task-starts.jsonl` row later than the feature event log's last land `end` for it, or the active mark naming it;
  - `waits` (the reading the nothing-running refusal shares) does not hold it;
  - no binding ruling holds it by name (`holds::named`);
  - its feature was not set down at or after its last start (`active`'s test).
  A ruling that holds NEW work (`holds::held`) does not hold a started task: it holds the tasks not yet started (T183). T184's builder, started 2026-11-23T19:22:55Z under 451's hold and after a page session's 451 set-down at 11:06:29Z, is still named, as T193 was built to do.

**Found and left?**
- The idle check named builders of tasks that were open but not in progress: waiting, set down since their start, held by name, landed, or never started. Fixed here, observed 2026-11-23, method: the coordinator's two live cases, and each of `verdict`'s holds read against `stalls.rs`'s single test of an open box.
- Not a defect (an accepted cost, no wrong outcome): while a builder's run outlasts the wait, the session wakes once every 45 minutes (a CONVENTION: `IDLE_SECS` + `WAIT_SECS`) to a one-line hand-on. Priced against waiting silently, the cost of no wake is a builder never named; a detached successor cannot wake the session. Chosen by this task's builder; the GM may cut it.
- Not a defect (a check's reach): the hand-on notice is outside the suites' message corpus, as T193's idle words are (`protocol::keep` runs only in `protocol::run`), so `make guard-messages` never names it. It was judged by `message-check` on a hand-built bundle (`/tmp/t201m/msg/MANIFEST.md`, 2026-11-23). FIDELITY passed. BREVITY's cuts were applied: the header shortened, and each builder's line cut to its id and description.

**Performance work?** Yes. It is the builders' loop: a builder parked or waiting is no longer named, so no wake goes to it, and a builder whose watch runs its full 30 minutes (`MONITOR_SECS`, measured 2026-11-23 (every Monitor launch's `timeoutMs`)) is named about 10 minutes after the watch ends (`STALL_SECS`, a GUESS) instead of never.

### T202 (observed 2026-11-23: three landings refused on plan.md and arbiter.jsonl conflicts, each resolved by hand; T195+T197's landing refused on T198's Makefile lines)

- **What happened, measured 2026-11-23** (the landings' logs `~/.claude/jobs/c6fd72d1/tmp/land*.log`, the clone's reflog, the coordinator's transcript):
  - Step 7, the take, gave up twice. On T187+T191's landing (`land191b.log`, tip d601eee011) it gave up on "the piece '<!-- plan-archive: T188 to T190 ...', changed otherwise on both sides". On T184+T196's (`land196.log`, tip 74b68e3644) it gave up on the T186 mark the same way. Both exited 4 ("the clone could not take").
  - The clone then never held main's tick. The next landings' pushes from the worktree conflicted on plan.md, and were merged by hand at 17:07 and 17:47 (the reflog's `Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'`) and at 22:07 (the coordinator's transcript, record 86613: a `git merge origin/main` conflicted on plan.md after T187+T191's take failed). The arbiter.jsonl conflict came in the same hand merges.
  - Replayed through land-alone's own `merge_pieces` on the real files (`/tmp/t202/try.py`): base, the clone's HEAD; ours, the coordinator's saved `plan451.dirty*.md`; theirs, the tip. The clone's only change to each mark piece was one blank line after the mark, before its next new section. The tick had rewritten that piece (`T196 to T186`, `T191 to T186`).
- **Approach**:
  - **Blank lines.** A piece the clone changed only in its blank lines is no change of the clone's (`merge_pieces`, `unblank`). Both real shapes then merge clean: the clone's T193 section kept, the archived T184 and T196 sections and the rewritten mark taken from main.
  - **Append-only logs.** An append-only `.jsonl` (the arbiter's log) that both sides appended to keeps both sides' new lines, the clone's first and then the tip's it does not hold (`merge3`'s `union`). A line rewritten on both sides still conflicts, named.
  - **Where main comes back.** The take, step 7 of land-alone, is where `make land` brings main back into the clone. It already leaves every uncommitted file untouched or merged. These two shapes were what kept it from finishing, so no second merge is added after it.
  - **Net-zero edits.** Step 3 counts a file as the task's own only where its edits leave a change of their own (`leaves_change`). Some hunk of the file's uncommitted diff must hold a line one of the task's Edits wrote (`new_string`) or removed (`old_string`): a whole line of the string, the string within the line (an edit inside one line), or the string's cut first or last line. Each Edit's call is read from its agent's transcript by its tool-use id (`edit_inputs`; the event line carries only digests). A file whose task edits are all put back is listed `putback`, left uncommitted, not refused. A `replace_all` Edit's flag is read with its strings; its one-line string is one the file repeats, so another task's line holding it is no line the edit wrote, and it counts only as one of its replacements - the line with the string put back on the hunk's other side (fixed here, MODE 4 round 1's D8). A Write, a Bash call's write, or an Edit whose call cannot be read counts as own: this fails toward the refusal, never a landing short of the task's edit.
  - **The Makefile shape.** T197's builder added the REJUDGE= lines (`ae254c4a94e079a98`, 23:05:56Z) and took them out (`a912d0a50ffb8b015`, 23:30:39Z). The two edits' strings cut mid-line differently, so no digest or line count of the edits could tell; only the diff could.

### T192 (the GM 2026-11-23, request.md: "Yes please tag the rest of the record before resuming our port"; filed by T187, which tagged one page, 0218)

- **Approach**: measured first, 2026-11-23. A tag-only edit on HEAD: one GUESS tag added to 0090's drawing page owed 12 pop-ups a triage (`make record-owed`: `modal-depiction` rows, "a page its Drawing: names moved"), no page check and no claim; a written-out Guesses bullet turned into a `{NNNN#id}` reference owed its pop-up form and research (T187's compound-shrine). So the strip came first, red first: `modals.rs`'s `page_words` drops every well-formed item tag (`items::strip`, a malformed one left visible), and what owes a pop-up reads its Guesses as its reader meets them, each reference filled from its tag's `data-guess` whatever the label (`modals/refs.rs`), found as the registry finds it at build (T200's `Pages::locate`: its own question first, else the one other question tagging the id): the base's references filled from the base's pages, the tree's from the tree's. A bullet made a reference to a tag carrying its words verbatim owes nothing; a referenced `data-guess` reworded owes the pop-up its checks (without that, stripping the tag would have hidden a rewording of the text a pop-up shows); a relabel owes nothing (T187). The bulk is a script (`.git/t192/tag.py`, the clone's, not tracked): it matches each pop-up bullet to the block of a cited drawing page sharing at least 0.6 of its content words and, where that block is a GUESS, tags it with the bullet verbatim and makes the bullet a reference; it tags a block stating a convention or deviation in a fixed form; it lists the rest for a page session. Coverage over the whole record (2026-11-23, `tag.py propose` over every drawing page): 1056 labeled blocks untagged, 225 GUESS tags by bullet (247 bullets of 160 pop-ups made references), 188 convention or deviation tags in fixed form, 643 left to sessions (496 GUESS blocks no bullet repeats, 100 attested, 39 convention or deviation not in fixed form, 8 with two labels); a hand-read of 12 bullet matches found 10 in the right block. Claims: 223 claims point at a drawing page without an item (88 GUESS, 11 DEVIATION, 124 plain), `.git/t192/claims.py` proposes each one's item by overlap with the same-label tags.

**The route, restated 2026-11-24: the cheap route** (the GM, request.md: *"please proceed with that as the way forward rather than the really expensive one that frankly seems kind of pointless for the purpose of what we are trying to accomplish"*). The mechanical route ran whole first: `tag.py` over every drawing page placed 225 GUESS tags by bullet (247 bullets made references) and 188 fixed-form tags, 36 page sessions of at most four questions confirmed them (391 confirmed, 18 moved, 13 removed with their bullets restored, 0 checks owed after every batch: `make record-owed`, `make claims-owed` and the registry's real-tree test green, `.git/t192/ledger.tsv`). At about 8 min a batch, 3 min of session and 5 of `make record-owed` (measured 2026-11-23 (the ledger's times and the gate logs' mtimes)), the 624 blocks left would have taken 50 more sessions, about 7 h (measured 2026-11-23 (`briefs.py p2`'s batch count times that rate)); measured instead: every one of them names its label in its own words (the 457 one-GUESS and 21 many-GUESS blocks by `GUESS`, written in capitals by the record's convention; 39 by convention or deviation; 8 by two labels; 100 by attested or accurate), so a script (`.git/t192/cheap.py`) tags each with an id and its label and no bullet: 476 GUESS, 32 CONVENTION and 27 DEVIATION tags, a convention or deviation beside the GUESS where one block holds both. Two findings make that enough (observed 2026-11-23, method: reading every reader of an item tag in `rust/`). (1) A tag's `data-guess` is read only where a pop-up references the item (`registry::items::bullets`, `owed`'s `modals::refs`; `restated` skips a bullet under three words), so it is owed from the first reference: the page check (`research::record::items::faults`) no longer asks it, and the registry refuses a reference to a GUESS tag without one, with its fix - the referencing pop-up's author writes it from the block. (2) Nothing reads an ATTESTED tag but a claim naming the item (`claims::item_labels`; the registry drops a non-GUESS reference, and an untagged block reads as unknown, never attested; grep of `"ATTESTED"` over `rust/`, 2026-11-24), and the classed claims anchored here name no ATTESTED item, so the 100 attested blocks stay untagged until a claim names one. Page sessions took only what the script could not decide (measured 2026-11-23 (`cheap.py propose`'s left list and the ledger)): 9 blocks on 9 questions in 3 sessions (a negated or back-referring convention or deviation word, and 3 whose label sits in a nested list's outer item, where the registry reads the inner item as the block), 7 tagged. Claims: an `opus` judge read each of the 94 classed claims still unanchored (83 GUESS, 11 DEVIATION) against its page's same-label tags, and 72 name their item now (`claims.py apply`), 0 owed after T204; 22 cite a page on which no tagged block states their decision, left as they were (listed in `.git/t192/claims-verdicts.json`).

### T204 (451 T192's sample, 2026-11-23: naming the item of 12 GUESS or DEVIATION claims citing 0090's and 0196's drawing pages owed all 12 impl-drift as `code changed`, while a plain pointer flipped to `GUESS ...#id` owed none; method: `make claims-owed` after `.git/t192/claims.py apply`)

- **Approach**: A claim recorded before it named its items stored its class word. `Claim::normalized` drops the class once the claim names an item (T187), so the claim no longer matched its row. Three places read it that way, all in the claims crate, and each now also takes the claim with its anchors left out and its class word kept (`grammar.rs`: `Claim::unanchored`, `anchors_free`, `same_but_items`).
  - **(1) A Rust unit's claim** (`index.rs` `relabeled_only`): the stored `claim` is read against `unanchored()` as well as `normalized()`.
  - **(2) A doc section's claim** (`index.rs` `owed_one`, `units.rs` `Unit::code_unanchored`): such a row stores no `body` and no `claim`, and its `code` is the claim alone. So the stored `code` is read against the code of the unanchored claim too. Without this arm, 77 of the 94 still owed. The advisor predicted it before the first fix, and the measurement found it.
  - **(3) The stale-figure check** (`stale.rs`): a constant's doc that only named the item, class kept, is no change. This is a bug found in the work: the same asymmetry in `label_free` flagged 24 stale figures on the 94 anchors. Fixed here.
  - A class changed with the naming (`GUESS p` to `DEVIATION p#id` or to a plain `p#id`), or an account changed, still owes. The brief says "its class word staying the same". The tag's agreement with the class stays with the label check (`item_labels.rs`), which refuses a landing on its own, so `owed` does not repeat it.

3. **What do you expect it to save, and why?** For the bulk, about 1050 tags and 247 references (275 with the sample's 28) on 226 pages and 160 pop-ups that would each have owed a triage or a pop-up's checks, measured 2026-11-23 (`tag.py propose ALL`); after the bulk, each relabel's pop-up and claim reviews (T187).
4. **How does the work grow with the settlement?** It does not: record tooling; a pop-up's references read each question's pages once.
5. **What did the before and after show, and under what conditions?** Before (HEAD's code): one tag owed 12 triages, and the two new owed tests failed. After: the sample's 55 tags and 27 references owed nothing; measured in this clone, 2026-11-23. The bulk, measured 2026-11-23 (`.git/t192/ledger.tsv`, the gate logs): the projected 60 write sessions (6-10 h) became 36 confirming sessions (about 8 min each, run before the restatement), one script run of seconds for 535 tags, and 3 sessions for 9 blocks; the 50 sessions the cheap route did not run were about 7 h at the measured rate (measured 2026-11-23 (the batch count times 8 min)). 0 checks owed throughout.

### T210 (the cascade test's 147 claims forced after a generated doc's rows were regenerated)

- **Approach**: the root cause is that a procedure section's snapshot kept only its blocks' digests (`dev/claims-pages.json`), while its words were sought only in git's history, so a snapshot of words that never reached a commit - round 2's `claims-checked` over a hand edit of two generated rows, then `make building-programs` putting HEAD's words back - left `gather_section` (rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/triage.rs) no removed block to show, and it forced every claim of the section. A section's words are now kept as a page's are (feature 375 T04's blob map, `.git/claims-page-blobs.json`, key `section:<core>`): each bundle that snapshots a section writes its words beside the snapshot (`section_texts`, `SECTION_TEXTS`, in the impl-drift bundle's `blocks.json`, `bundle.rs`, and the triage's `triage.json`), and every record of a snapshot keeps them (`keep_sections`: `claims-checked`, the tool's clear, the all-forced record, `claims-triaged`, and `claims backfill-sections`; `commands.rs`, `commands/backfill.rs`), so they are the words as judged, not the tree's at record time. `section_words` reads the kept words first, then the history. The regenerated row then shows as a pair (hand edit -> HEAD words) and T191's filter judges it per claim, as it does any edit. `gather_section` now reads each section's edit once, its claims sharing it (`Gathered::section_lost`): the history search ran once a claim. `keep_texts`' blob writing is shared (`keep_blobs`). The kept texts and the removed-words search move to `triage/kept.rs`, and the backfills to `commands/backfill.rs` (constitution X clause 13's bar; observed 2026-11-24, method: `check file-scale` in the closing checks named triage.rs at 1017 lines and commands.rs at 1006), re-exported under their old paths. THE ONE FORCE LEFT, kept on purpose: a removed block whose words neither the kept snapshot nor the history holds (a snapshot recorded before T210 kept words, or recorded in another clone - the blob map is per clone - of words no commit holds, or older than the history the search reads): an echo of the new words cannot see a claim that repeated only the lost ones, and a full impl-drift is the one check that needs no old words, so its claims are owed in full (pinned by `a_change_that_only_removes_shows_none_new_and_a_lost_block_owes_in_full`). A change with nothing claim-bearing left is already cleared by the tool (T191). Also left forced, unchanged: `gather_code`'s empty hunks (a code fingerprint moved with no hunk of the unit's diff to show - a constant it reads changed elsewhere, `reads`): the code did change and nothing shows how, so forcing is the only safe answer there too. Priced and not taken: refusing `claims-checked` while a generated doc is stale against its generator (`make quick` already reds on it, `building-programs --check`): it covers generated rows only, not any section snapshotted with words later reverted, and the claims crate does not build on `mode_a`.

### T214 (the cascade test's review-fixed refusal on a sheet with no carried verdict)

- **Approach**: the GM 2026-11-24, request.md's last section: *"Yes let's fix all 6 of those before we resume."* Measured first
  (2026-11-24, this clone, read-only): why the three tools disagreed on the round-trip sheet. `reviews owed` (so `make verify`) and
  `reviews snapshot` both read the delta's occasions, and a notes-only edit is none (feature 294); the push's review gate
  (`review-gate.sh`) asks only owed units, so it owed nothing too. `make review-fixed` (`prereq/scoped.rs`' `declare`) was the one that
  disagreed, for three reasons. (a) `UNIT=ochiba-roundtrip-test`, the sheet's bare name, was looked up as a unit with no verdict record,
  refused as "no PASS or NEEDS-WORK verdict to carry: a full round is owed". (b) It took the unit's sheet from `unit_folder`, which
  prefers the review tree's snapshot, and `.git/review-snapshot/building-review--ochiba-roundtrip-test/` was still on disk from
  2026-11-23 11:01, a delta that had landed, so a unit no delta owed read as owed. (c) That verdict was written at 11:06, before T199
  landed (22eb592bad, 18:55), so no `.reviewed` copy was kept, and one let-else printed "was not kept: a full round is owed" for all of
  not owed, not kept and kept-but-different. So `declare` now:
  - reads a bare sheet name as its `building-review--<sheet>` unit (`unit_of`), and prints that slug when it declares;
  - takes owed from `unit_sheet`, `reviews owed`'s own list, before any snapshot (`unit_folder_on`, the sheet asked once). A unit the
    delta does not owe gets the answer the other tools give, with exit 0: not owed by this delta, no round full or change-scoped, the
    last verdict left on file as it is. A name with no pool sheet is refused as that, and never read as not owed;
  - keeps the full round for an owed unit with no PASS or NEEDS-WORK on file (a sheet never reviewed: its first round is the full one);
  - finds the sheet as reviewed again where no copy was kept (`scoped/recover.rs`): every version of the drawing and the notes that git
    holds (`DEPTH`, 200 commits back at most: observed 2026-11-24, method: `git log` of the round-trip sheet's notes, 15 commits over seven weeks), plus the drawing as it reads now, since a generated compound's drawing is never committed. These
    are hashed by `files_key`, the bytes half of `folder_key`, so the hash is the verdict's own. The match is written to the kept
    copy and the change-scoped prompt pairs it as before. With no match, the full round is owed, and the message says the sheet as
    reviewed is neither kept nor in git history. Measured: on the real sheet, the drawing as it reads now with the notes at
    03cc1514d1 hashes to its verdict's `9b7b9464d35cc002`.
  The rest of T199's rule is unchanged: a named non-nitpick, an open error or questionable finding, an unchanged sheet.
  Replayed on the real sheet after the fix (`l7r-gate reviews prereq fixed`, both names): exit 0, "is not owed by this delta ... no
  round is owed", which agrees with `reviews owed --units` (no round-trip unit).

### T215 (the GM's question 2026-11-24: T210's kept section words lived in each clone's .git, so another clone forced its sections)

- **Approach**: T210 kept a procedure section's words as git blobs in the clone's `.git/claims-page-blobs.json` (`section:<core>`), so a snapshot of words no commit holds - recorded in one clone - was unreadable in any other, and a fresh clone forced every claim of the section (measured 2026-11-24, the replay in item 9: 147 forced). The words now live in the repository, `dev/claims-section-words.jsonl` (`SECTION_WORDS`, rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/triage/kept.rs): one line a block, `{"block": its digest, "words": its words}`, sorted by digest, keyed by block rather than by section snapshot because `dev/claims-pages.json` already maps each snapshot to its blocks' digests and the triage seeks only the missing digests - so a regenerated row adds its new block's line and drops its old one, never a whole section re-written. `keep_sections` adds a bundle's `section_texts` (the words as judged, T210's property kept) and prunes the file to the blocks of the snapshots the saved index's rows name (`section`), written only when it changes. Every record of a snapshot writes it through one path: `save_recorded` (rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/commands.rs) - the index's live rows, the snapshots, the words - for `claims-checked`, the tool's clear, the all-forced record and `claims-triaged`; `claims backfill-sections` writes it after saving (commands/backfill.rs). Observed 2026-11-24, method: every `save_store(` and every write of a row's `section` in the crate (`rg 'save_store\(|"section"'`): the five sites above record section snapshots, each with words; the other two `save_store` writers record page snapshots only (`claims-triage`'s page-move clear, `clear_page_moves`, and `claims backfill`); `reply.rs`'s and `triage.rs`'s copies of `section` and `bundle.rs`'s carry a core a bundle read, recorded through those sites. `section_words` reads the file, then the history; a line that does not parse or whose words do not hash to its digest is not read. The per-clone section path is dropped (`kept_section` and the `section:` keys deleted): no case needs it - the clone's blob store held 20 sections, and the file written by `make claims-backfill-sections` resolves all 257 blocks of the 20 snapshots the index names (each named core is the tree's current one); a stale `section:` key in a clone's blob map is ignored. Page texts stay per clone (git's history holds a page's). The file merges by `merge=union` (`.gitattributes`): a line is its block's alone, so two clones' edits never conflict; a union may keep a pruned line or leave the order unsorted, which the reader tolerates and the next write re-sorts and prunes. It is registered where `dev/claims-pages.json` is: the push's claims gate judges it (`cohort` crate, `push::judges`), and the gate's preflight counts it a claims record no phase reads (`measure` crate, `preflight::RECORDS`). Clippy's `unnecessary_wraps` then named `section_words` and `gather_section` (they no longer fail), so both return plainly.

### T216 (the GM 2026-11-24: builders were sent with `model: opus` under a Fable 5.2 session; an ad-hoc agent that judges or builds runs on the session's model)

- **Approach**: `agent_model_hooks` (rust/guard/src/guards/agent_model_hooks.rs, its rule text agent_model_rule.txt) refused an ad-hoc dispatch with no model and passed ANY named one, and the rule it printed said `opus` for anything that judges - so every builder was named `opus` while the GM's session ran Fable 5.2 (measured 2026-11-24, `make guard-log GUARD=agent-model`, the `model-named` rows dated 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-24: 415 on opus, 16 on sonnet, 1 on fable). The rule as built, decided in this order: a fork passes (unchanged); a DEFINED type (a file under `.claude/agents/`) passes whatever it names - this check moved ahead of the model's, since a defined agent is out of scope; a named `sonnet` or `haiku` passes (`model-named`); any other named model is refused (`judging-model-named`), the message naming the model and saying to omit it; no model and a line of the prompt `SESSION_MODEL: <what it judges or builds, two words or more>` passes (`session-model`, the reason in the guard log) and inherits the session's model; no model and no such line is refused (`no-model`), as before. `workflow_hooks` (rust/guard/src/guards/workflow_hooks.rs) holds a script's ad-hoc `agent()` call to the same rule - it only tested that `model:` was present - reading the model's literal (`NAMED`, a computed model refused as `?`), the marker anywhere inside the call's text (its prompt or a comment), a marked call recorded `session-model`; an omitted `model` in `agent()` inherits the session's model (the workflow-authoring reference, read 2026-11-24: "the agent inherits the main-loop model"). No default subagent model is configured (measured 2026-11-24: `grep -i subagent` over `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `~/.claude/settings.json` and the environment, no hit), so an omitted model does inherit here.
- **Decision (a), the carrier: a line of the prompt, `SESSION_MODEL: <reason>`.** The Agent tool's input is a closed schema (description, prompt, subagent_type, model, isolation, effort), so the statement rides in the description or the prompt. The description's head and the prompt's FIRST line are already read for the task a dispatch serves (`set_down_hooks/builders.rs` `builder_brief`, `check_bundle_hooks/own.rs`), so the marker is a line of its own anywhere in the prompt, matched at a line's start so a sentence that mentions the token is not the decision. It carries a reason held to the escapes' floor (`shared::escape::enough`: two words, eight characters), as `GP_OK` and `DECIDE_OK` do, and the reason is the log's detail - so `make audit` shows what was sent to the session's model. It is a compliant form, not an escape: the guard has none.
- **Decision (b), any named model but `sonnet` or `haiku` is refused - the session's own included.** The T216 line says the guard refuses "a named opus or fable that is not the session's". Built stricter: a named `opus` under an Opus session is refused too. Why: the GM asked that the agent follow the switch ("if I switch back to Opus 5.5, then I would want them to use that"; "inheriting the parent session model"), and a name that equals the session's model today stops following at the next switch; the compliant dispatch (omit the model, add the line) is always available and costs one line. The allowed names are a list rather than `opus` and `fable` being a denied one, so an alias the harness adds later is refused until its tier is decided. Cost: no ad-hoc dispatch can be pinned to a judging model other than the session's; none was asked for, and a defined agent's file still pins any tier.
- **Decision (c), a named `sonnet` beside the line passes as sonnet.** The named model is what runs, and it is the cheaper tier; the line is then inert.
- **Decision (d), the unmarked dispatch with no model stays refused** (the brief's design, the GM 2026-11-24: "that ruling from before is something that I still want with regards to enforcing that Sonnet should be used to read, fetch, translate, or extract"): were it allowed, reading work would land on the session's model by omission, the defect the 2026-09-19 ruling answered (docs/guards.md's row for this guard records feature 251's census of it).
- Restated with the rule (observed 2026-11-24, method: `grep -rn 'for anything that judges'` and `grep -rn 'names its .model'` over the tree outside `.git`): the root CLAUDE.md's clause and the suite's check of it (its clauses and the `SESSION_MODEL: <` line), docs/guards.md (the guard's row, and the escape table's rows for this guard and for `workflow_hooks.rs`), docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md, docs/research-doctrine.md (the ad-hoc agent's row), scripts/container/page-session-rules.md, rust/guard/CLAUDE.md's index lines for the guards. Left alone (observed 2026-11-24, the same method): the defined checks' pinned tiers ("judgment is on Opus", `agent_models.rs`) - the GM's ruling is about ad-hoc agents - and the spec directories of features 252 and 293, which are history.

### T217 (probed 2026-11-24: a built-in type's own definition sets its model, so a marked `Explore` was recorded `session-model` and ran Opus)

- **Approach**: T216's `agent_model_hooks` (rust/guard/src/guards/agent_model_hooks.rs) passed a model-less dispatch carrying the prompt line `SESSION_MODEL: <reason>` on ANY ad-hoc type. The probe on the T217 task line (measured 2026-11-24, method: a Fable 5.2 session dispatched each type and asked the agent to state its own model; this builder did not rerun it and cites the task line): `general-purpose`, `Plan` and `claude` with no `model` ran Fable 5.2, `Explore` with no `model` ran Opus 5.5 - its built-in definition's - and `Explore` with `model: sonnet` ran Sonnet 5.5. The rule as built: a new list `INHERITS` (`general-purpose`, `Plan`, `claude`), the measurement and its date in the comment beside it, matched exactly. After the fork, defined-type and named-`sonnet`/`haiku` passes (unchanged, so `Explore` naming `sonnet` still passes), a dispatch of a type NOT on the list is refused whatever else it carries - marked (`type-not-inheriting`), unmarked (`no-model`) or naming another model (`judging-model-named`) - with one message of its own that names the two routes: `model: "sonnet"` to read, a `general-purpose` dispatch with no model and the line to judge or build. A listed type is judged as T216 built it, its messages unchanged. `workflow_hooks` (rust/guard/src/guards/workflow_hooks.rs) reads the same list: an ad-hoc `agent()` call naming an unlisted `agentType` and no reading model is refused (verdict `PINNED`, its own message with the same two routes), and so is a call naming NO type unless it names a reading model - Decision (c).
- **Decision (a), a list of what was measured to inherit, not a list of what was found pinned.** The task line: "the line passes only on a type measured to inherit (a list with its measurement beside it)". So the unprobed built-ins (`web-fetch`, `claude-code-guide`, `statusline-setup`) and any type the harness adds later are refused until someone probes them. Cost: a judging dispatch cannot use those types; `general-purpose` has every tool they have.
- **Decision (b), every refusal of an unlisted type prints the one new message, not the rule text.** The rule text (agent_model_rule.txt) says "Re-send the SAME dispatch" with the line added; on an `Explore` that route is now refused, so an unmarked `Explore` and an `Explore` naming `opus`, which got the rule text before, would be sent into a second refusal. They get the new message instead, and the rule text is unchanged. The task line asks for the refusal on the marked dispatch; the other two are the same wrong route closed.
- **Decision (c), a workflow `agent()` call with NO `agentType` is held as an unmeasured type: it reads, on `sonnet` or `haiku`, or is refused.** The task brief: verify from the workflow reference rather than assume. Found (the workflow-authoring reference, read 2026-11-24): `opts.agentType` "uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent - resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool", and `opts.model`: "Default to omitting it - the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model)". So a typed call resolves as an Agent dispatch does and is held to the list; an untyped call is the default workflow subagent - NOT `general-purpose` - and nobody probed what it runs on. The reference's sentence is a document, not the measurement the list asks for, so the untyped call gets the standard `web-fetch` gets (spec-fidelity MODE 4, round 1, ruled passing it a narrowing): marked, unmarked or naming another model, it is refused (`PINNED`, the message saying it "is not measured to run on the session's model" and naming `agentType: "general-purpose"` with the line), and the `UNTYPED` refusal now says a `GP_OK` stage may only read. Cost: a workflow stage that judges names `agentType: "general-purpose"`, which already passed without `GP_OK`; the route into the list is the same probe run on an untyped call. This builder has no Workflow tool, so the probe was not run here.
- Restated (observed 2026-11-24, method: `grep -rn SESSION_MODEL` over the tree outside `specs/` and `.git`): docs/guards.md (the guard's row and the escape table's rows for both guards), docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md, docs/research-doctrine.md row 55, scripts/container/page-session-rules.md, rust/guard/CLAUDE.md's index line, both modules' doc comments, both suites. Left alone: the root CLAUDE.md's clause - its two clauses (sonnet to read; no model and the line for anything that judges or builds) do not change, and the type list is the guard's message to give.

| the `SESSION_MODEL:` line passes only on `general-purpose`, `Plan`, `claude`; any other ad-hoc type refused with the two routes | `tests/hooks/test-agent-model-hooks.sh` (red first on the unchanged guard, 2026-11-24, `/tmp/t217-red-first.txt`: a marked `Explore` rc=0, a marked `web-fetch` rc=0, the routes, the types and the record absent - 6 failed; 40 of 40 green on the new guard); `agent_model_hooks::tests::the_line_passes_only_on_a_type_measured_to_inherit` | none: guard tooling | none | n/a |

### T218 (the restatement audit, 2026-11-24: "the cited pages do not say it" filed from the bundle alone where the record says it)

- **Approach**: impl-drift reads only the pages its claims cite, so its "none of the cited pages says it" was filed as if the record were silent: 449's found row 210 (452 T22) said no page gives the kitchen door "often at the rear", and `research/questions/0107-kitchens-daidokoro.html`, which the section did not cite, says the door "was often tucked away at the rear". The search is the tool's, at `make claims-checked` (`rust/gate/crates/claims/src/claims/silent.rs`, called from `commands.rs` before the reply is vetted), not the bundle builder's: a claim judged IN-STEP costs nothing, and the lines under OUTSIDE THE CHANGE, which row 210 was, are covered. A finding line that says the pages are silent - a VERDICT other than IN-STEP that is NEEDS-RESEARCH, ends `[§]` or uses a silence phrase ("none of the pages", "the page does not say/give/attest", "gives no", "silent on"), or an OUTSIDE THE CHANGE line with such a phrase that names its effect (one that names none is dropped unfiled by T219, so nothing is searched for it) - is HELD: taken out of the reply, so neither recorded in the index nor filed as a row, its key still owed and the command exiting 3, while any of the record's three nearest pages for its words is not in the bundle. The message names the missing pages and the call that adds them (`make claims-bundle UNITS=... PAGES=... REASON=...`; `PAGES=` already existed). Judged again with those pages in the bundle, the line is recorded as written, so a finding the record is truly silent on is still filed, after one more reading; where a page says it, impl-drift.md now tells the check the finding is the missing citation (`fix: claim`, naming the page) or nothing, and that "the pages do not say it" speaks of the cited pages, never of the record. The nearest pages are ranked by words alone - each question and drawing page (notes and originals are no pages) by its best block, a block by the share of the line's words it holds, a word weighing more the fewer blocks hold it; the words are the claim's text and the note for a VERDICT, the block and the finding for an outside line. No score separates silent from said, so there is no threshold: the rule is "read the nearest three, then file" (the number three is a knob, `silent::NEAREST`, a GUESS: the one recorded case ranks its page first). One hold a search: the pages a hold named are kept in the clone's `.git/claims-searched.json` under the claim's key (an outside line's file), and the next reply on that key is passed once those pages are in the bundle, whatever its new words rank, then the entry is forgotten - so a reworded second reply cannot be held again and the round ends. What it costs: every NEEDS-RESEARCH and every silent finding whose nearest pages the claim does not already cite is judged twice; and a pass is not searched, so a GUESS judged IN-STEP because its cited pages are silent, where another page answers it, is still missed (no filing comes of it; not built here).

- **Approach**: the stale rows of `dev/claims-index.json` were read beside their claims at HEAD, measured 2026-11-24 (the index rows printed, the source lines grepped). Two mechanisms. (1) The shrine-tree trio (`grounds.rs::shrine_tree`, `fixtures.rs::tree`, `layout.rs::TREE_ROOM`) were judged citing 0218's drawing page as a finding and relabeled `GUESS <page>#shrine-tree`; a claim on a tagged item leaves its class word and anchor out of its fingerprint (T187), so the stored claim and code read the same before and after and nothing saw the relabel. (2) `audit/palette.rs::ROLE_NAMES#the palette's table` was told three of its rows need claims of their own; they were written beside it, the judged claim unmoved. The fix, in `rust/gate/crates/claims`: a FINDING's row now keeps the claim as it was said, class word kept and anchors dropped (`said`), and its unit's claim labels, fingerprinted (`siblings`); `bundle.rs` writes both to `units.json`, `reply.rs` copies them onto finding rows only, measured 2026-11-24 (`make claims-report`'s first line: 17 findings of 3,557 claims). `index::relabel_answered` reads the backing from `said`, so a relabel the fingerprint cannot see answers its MISLABELED verdict as any relabel does (385 T23 D45, T213: the account word for word, the body unchanged); `index::answered` is the one reading the push's carry, the report and the clean gate's `open_lines` share. `make claims-report` counts an answered finding as `ANSWERED` and leaves it off the list (`ALL=1` lists it), so the list is what stands. A finding whose unit's claim labels changed since it was judged is owed impl-drift again (`index::SIBLINGS`), never hidden: whether the new claims answer it is a judgment. A row recorded before T221 keeps neither field: it is answered only where its stored claim differs from the claim both with and without its anchors, and otherwise stands until judged again - the rows named here are such rows and are re-judged in T220's claims round. - **Approach**: instructions only, in the two agent files the task names. `building-review.md` told the reviewer the notes' "deliberate choices and the Review log are settled" and nothing about what a dated entry is, and 449 T380's review (452 T015) reported that Hayakawa's log entries T276, T299 and T312 "still give the armory at the west end" with no pointer to T367, which mirrored the row afterwards: each entry was true when written and says when. The file now says a dated entry of a sheet's notes - a Review log line, a line under a dated heading, an entry naming the feature or task that made it - is history: it is not held to the sheet as it stands, an older entry a later change overtook is no finding, and it owes no "since superseded" pointer; only the notes' present-tense text (the choices, the program, a Result or summary paragraph that states the sheet as it is) is held to the drawing. `record-format.md`'s HISTORY rule stays whole - the GM's rule that a research page carries no history of itself - and gains one sentence: a dated entry is history by its form, ruled on as HISTORY (what is useful kept, the rest proposed for removal), and never reported as a statement the page makes today that is stale or contradicted; this permits no change log on a research page. No recorded record-format case of the kind was found (the audit's case is building-review's), so its sentence is stated on the rule alone and said so here.

### T224 (the round arbiter's `ask:mixed-build-53-record-answers`, 2026-11-24, continue with a tooling fix: a landing was refused at the push and 53 record answers owed again by T197's rule, when for 49 of them the uncommitted files were the claims crate's and a Markdown doc)

- **Approach**: A landing alone counts a build's uncommitted file against an answer only where that file's code can run in building the answer's bundle or recording it. The rule is one function, `runs_in`, in `rust/gate/crates/core/src/build.rs`, over a table per kind of answer; `mixed` takes the table.
  - **(a) A record answer's table, `RECORD`.**
    - The `owed` crate: it records the answer (`record-checked`, the modal triage, `write_answer`).
    - The `bundle` crate: it builds the bundle the agent read (`check-bundle`, `modal-bundle`).
    - Their path dependencies: core, pool, registry, research and `rust/guard/shared`. Observed 2026-11-24, method: `cargo tree` (`/home/agent/.claude/jobs/c6fd72d1/tmp/cargo-tree-owed-bundle.txt`) and the walk of the `Cargo.toml` files the new test makes.
    - `rust/gate/src`: `l7r-gate` is one executable, and its `lib.rs` dispatches `record`.
    - The `record` crate: it dispatches each `record` verb, holds `apply-edits` (which settles an answer through `write_answer`), and holds `html5_entities.tsv`, which `rust/guard/shared` includes.
    - Left out: the `record` crate's other dependencies (archive, downloads, pages, semantic, trials, uncited). They are linked into the executable, and no verb that builds a check bundle or records its answer calls them. Observed 2026-11-24, method: every caller of `write_answer` and `write_judged` listed with grep (the `owed` crate, and `record/apply_edits/round.rs`), and the crates `apply_edits` names (bundle, core, owed, research).
  - **(b) Files that are not code.**
    - A Markdown file outside the table's crates never counts: it cannot run. `rust/gate/CLAUDE.md` is the measured case.
    - A Markdown file inside a crate of the table counts. The `plan` crate includes Markdown fixtures by `include_str!`, so "Markdown cannot run" is not true inside a crate. Observed 2026-11-24, method: the new test failed on the first draft's blanket rule, naming three such files.
    - A `tests.rs` or `tests/` file inside a crate of the table counts. Whether a file is test-only is its `mod` line's `cfg`, not its name, and `core` holds test helpers the `testkit` feature also compiles. The measured case does not need the exclusion: its tests files were the claims crate's.
    - A `Cargo.toml` anywhere, `rust/Cargo.lock` and `.cargo/config.toml` always count: a manifest can turn on a feature of a shared crate.
    - A path the rule does not know counts.
  - **(c) The claims side.** Narrowed the same way, with its own table, `CLAIMS`: the `claims` crate, its path dependencies (core, owed, plan, pool, registry, research, reviews, tree, `rust/guard/shared`), `rust/gate/src`, and the one included file of the `record` crate. Every claims reader of a mixed build goes through `Landing::paths` in `claims/index.rs` (`landing.rs` calls it twice), so the one call is the whole change. Observed 2026-11-24, method: grep of `build::mixed` and `Landing` in the claims crate.
  - **The table follows the tree.** `build::closure::gaps` walks the `[dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]` path entries from the table's root crates, and the `include_str!` and `include_bytes!` lines of each crate reached. It names a crate reached and not in the table, a table entry nothing reaches that is not listed beside it with its reason, and an included file the table does not count. Core's test runs it on the real tree for both tables. Core's `Cargo.toml` declares those crates as what its tests read, so `make rust-test` runs the test again when one of their manifests moves.
  - **The message is unchanged.**

| the landing's record answers (`L7R_LAND_ALONE=1 make record-owed UNANSWERED=1`, read only, 2026-11-24) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| listed as answered by a mixed build | 49 | 0 |
| quote-check | 28 | 0 |
| source-reader | 10 | 0 |
| translation-check | 7 | 0 |
| source-applicability | 3 | 0 |
| intro-check | 1 | 0 |

  Before is the clone at `1b064aa0de` with no edit (`/tmp/t224/before.txt`); after is the same tree with this task's edits uncommitted (`/tmp/t224/after.txt`: "no record check is owed"). The task line's 53 included 4 guest-quarters modal answers, re-run by the ruling before this task began. `L7R_LAND_ALONE=1 make claims-owed` after: no claim is owed.
