### T225 (the round arbiter's `ask:stamp-reads-committed-code-as-mixed`, 2026-11-24, continue with a tooling fix: each of the day's three gate fixes re-owed the answers recorded before it - 241 claims, 53 record answers, 191 claims and 49 record answers, and the landing was refused each time - because the mixed-build rule compared a build's stamped blobs with HEAD alone)

- **Approach**: A landing alone reads a build's uncommitted file as another builder's only where no commit holds the blob the build stamped for it. The reading is one type, `Own`, in `rust/gate/crates/core/src/build.rs`; `mixed` asks it, and the two readers (`Judged` in `owed/answers.rs`, `Landing` in `claims/index.rs`) each hold one `Own` in place of their own HEAD lookups.
  - **(a) The ruling's rule.** A stamped blob is the landing's own committed code where it is its path's blob at HEAD, at a commit of the landing's delta, or at the delta's base. A stamped `deleted` is the landing's own where one of those commits holds no such file.
  - **(b) How the delta and its base are found.** The base is `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`, the base `make land` already diffs from (`origin/main...HEAD` in `land.rs`). The delta is `base..HEAD`. The landing worktree is a worktree of the clone, so it resolves `origin/main` as the clone does. A merge of main into the clone moves the base to main's tip and leaves the clone's own commits in the delta. Where no base is found (no `origin/main`, no shared history) the delta is empty and a blob is held to HEAD: the rule before this task.
  - **(c) A blob no commit holds still reads mixed.** That is the real case the rule exists for: another builder's work in progress, changed before it was committed or never committed. Observed 2026-11-24, method: a script over every `builds` entry of the clone's `.git/record-checks/*.json` (302 entries) and every `build` of `dev/claims-index.json` (205 rows): one answer holds blobs no commit holds, `modal-form:sheet/guest-quarters` at its superseded fingerprint `e22e938665b5` (a build of `07aac2b99c` with 24 dirty files, 15 of them never committed in that form). It is not the unit's current answer, so nothing reads it.
  - **(d) Since the build: a decision this task adds to the ruling's words.** The stamp names the commit its binary was built at. A file committed unchanged after the build is at a commit of `<stamp commit>..HEAD`, wherever the landing's base stands, so a blob held there is committed code too. Why it is needed: the ruling's rule holds for one landing. Observed 2026-11-24, method: a script over `dev/claims-index.json` comparing each stamped blob with this tree: 189 rows carry a stamp of `1b064aa0de` with seven dirty files, and this task's own commit edits five of them. Once this landing is pushed, its commits are behind the next landing's base, and every one of those rows would read mixed at the next landing of any clone, the loop the ruling ends run once more. With (d), observed 2026-11-24, method: the same script: 0 of the 205 stamped rows, and 0 of the 302 record entries but the one in (c), hold a blob that no commit since its stamp holds. It is asked last, after HEAD, the delta and the base miss, so a landing whose answers are its own pays nothing for it. A stamp commit git does not know adds nothing.
  - **(e) The cost.** A blob HEAD holds: one `rev-parse` a path, as before. The first blob HEAD does not hold: one `merge-base` and one `git log --raw` over the whole delta, kept for every later path and answer; then one `rev-parse` of the base a path. For (d): one `git log --raw` a stamp commit. The `git log` took 0.08 s for 106 commits (932 lines), 0.03 s for 65 and 0.01 s for 27, measured 2026-11-24 (`/usr/bin/time` on it in the clone).
  - **(f) The stamp is refreshed at use.** `build::current()` hands the stamp on without each dirty file whose stamped blob is the one HEAD of the launcher's tree (`L7R_GATE_TREE`) holds now: one `git ls-tree` a call, none for a clean stamp. This is the ruling's second clause on the writing side. An answer recorded by a binary whose sources were committed unchanged since its build carries a clean stamp, and a triage clear by it stamps no row of the tracked index. The reading side already read such a stamp as clean, blob by blob.
  - **The messages are unchanged.**

| the landing as the clone stands (`L7R_LAND_ALONE=1`, read only, 2026-11-24) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `make record-owed UNANSWERED=1`: units listed as answered by a mixed build | 49 | 0 |
| `make claims-owed`: claims owed | 0 | 0 |

  Before is the clone at `764f15e3d2` with no edit (`/tmp/t225/before-record.txt`, `before-claims.txt`); after is the same tree with this task's edits uncommitted (`/tmp/t225/after-record.txt`: "no record check is owed"; `after-claims.txt`: "no claim is owed"). The claims row proves nothing by itself: every claim stamp equals HEAD until this task is committed. The claims half rests on the script in (d) and on the claims crate's fixture.

- **Approach**: D12 in `no_poll_hooks`. Held: `rust/guard/src/guards/no_poll_hooks.rs` (`make guard-edit` first). Red first: R4's
  observed `(make static > /tmp/t225-static.log 2>&1; echo END >> ...) & sleep 1` refused naming `run_in_background`; `nohup make
  rust-test` refused; `for c in git setsid make; do ...` passes (a word, not a command); `make static > log 2>&1 & wait $!` passes;
  `make static & echo wait` refused (a `wait` that is a word); `make static & sleep 5 & wait $!` refused (`$!` names the sleep); `make
  static & P=$!; wait $P` refused (a saved pid, D12); `make static & (wait)` refused (another shell's wait); `make static & false &&
  wait` refused (a conditional wait); `make static & wait &` refused (a backgrounded wait); `(make static > log) & make decide F=449
  T=T121 | tail -40; wait` passes (R4's observed bare form); `sleep 30 & make static & wait %2` passes (`%2` names the make job,
  the sleep no make or cargo); `setsid make static` refused; `make static & disown` refused; `make static & disown; wait` and `make static & disown;
  wait $!` refused, each going red when the disown check is deleted (the covering wait would pass them); `make static & disown -h;
  wait` and `make static & disown %1; wait` refused; `{ make static; } &`, `VAR=x make static &` and `env X=1 make
  static &` each refused (D1's detector reads the target past `{`, `VAR=` and `env`); `make static` with `run_in_background` passes; `DETACH_OK="..."` passes and is
  recorded. A compound that runs in another shell - a pipeline's part (`for t in a b; do make $t & done | cat; wait`, `{ make x & }
  | cat; wait`), a `( )`, a backgrounded loop, one in `$( )` - is refused, since a later `wait` covers none of its jobs; a bare `wait`
  after a loop, `if` or `case` body run in the same shell covers it (the plan review's ruling, LEGITIMATE, 2026-11-20).
- **The shared readers, fixed here** (T30 folded in; the plan review of 2026-11-20 ruled leaving them NOT LEGITIMATE). Held also:
  `rust/guard/src/shared/shape.rs`, `rust/guard/src/shared/make.rs` (`make guard-edit` first). Each red first in its own tests:
  `strip_heredocs` takes a heredoc whose opener line goes on past its delimiter (`cat <<'EOF' > f`), keeping those words;
  `strip_quotes` keeps a quoted string only after an interpreter's `-c`, its flags joined too (`bash -lc`, `sh -ec`, `python3 -c`),
  never `grep -c` or `git -c`, and blanks the strings quoted inside a kept one; `invoked` reads `setsid [opts]` as a word that runs
  what follows, `make;` as a call, and a goal-less make as `.DEFAULT_GOAL` (a goal it cannot read, `make $T`, still names none).
  `no_poll_hooks` reads through them, its own heredoc and quote readers retired. Every guard reading them is replayed on the frozen
  corpora before and after, each moved verdict named.

### T236 (the GM 2026-11-25, request.md "a research backlog": of eight hamlet searches in two days two changed what is drawn; "yes please" to UNRESEARCHED as a fifth label and a backlog in place of a search before every guess)

- **Approach**: UNRESEARCHED (not yet searched) becomes a fifth label beside accurate, deviation, convention and guess (searched, silent), on the pages as in the claims grammar, where it already was. ### T238 (page session P12, 2026-11-25: its correction to 0006's drawing page from a search pass, b75ade5b7e, read as a SIZE EDIT at 21,792 bytes against the 20,000 cap while `make question-sizes` listed no page over 20,000 bytes of prose, measured 2026-11-25 (the refusal and the report as the landing printed them); the landing needed SIZE_EDIT_OK)

- **Approach**: The two measures are in one file, `rust/gate/crates/checks/src/checks/question_size.rs`.
  - **What each counted.** The cap and `make question-sizes` (`--report`) read `size`: the page's bytes with each money mark unwrapped to its words (feature 413) and each item tag removed (`items::strip`, 451 T192). The size-edit rule (`size_edit_refusal`, 451 T184) handed `is_size_edit` `old.len()` and `new.len()`, the raw file: item tags, money markup and all. Comments, footnote marks and other markup count in both; only the item tags and money marks differ.
  - **The case.** Raw: 19,539 bytes before, 21,792 after, measured 2026-11-25 (`git show` of the page at `b75ade5b7e~1` and `b75ade5b7e`, `wc -c`). Prose: 17,558 before, 19,513 after, measured 2026-11-25 (the same two texts, money marks unwrapped and item tags stripped by the check's two patterns, `wc -c`). The edit removed 171 bytes of words, measured 2026-11-25 (the refusal's own figure, `l7r-gate check question-size --base b75ade5b7e~1`). By prose the page was under the cap before, after, and with the removed words put back (19,684), so it was no size edit; by the raw file its after-plus-removed was over, so the rule fired and refused the correction's dropped `not` and `without`.
  - **The fix.** One function, `prose(text)`, is the measure. `size(path)` reads the file and calls it; `size_edit_refusal` calls it on the base and the new text and hands those to `is_size_edit`. Its refusal prints "bytes of prose". `is_size_edit` keeps T184's rule (over before, or the removed words putting it back over: the add-then-trim of one session), now by that one measure. `make question-sizes`'s help line said "question + notes"; it counts the question's prose alone, and now says so.

### T237 (the GM 2026-11-25, request.md: "sounds good please do that ASAP": five 449 code builders and the 451 T218-T222 builder hit the 300k context cap and handed off, the claims round the part that ran them out; the brief template half landed as `scripts/container/builder-brief.md`)

- **Approach**: The enforcement half, in the context-cap guard (`rust/guard/src/guards/context_cap_hooks.rs`, which already tells a builder from the main session and a defined agent, D8, and reads its own transcript, D9), a new submodule `context_cap_hooks/split.rs`.
  - **Who is a code builder.** A builder whose brief - the first row of its own transcript, the prompt it was dispatched with - holds a line opening `STOP POINT`, and does not itself open `Run the claims round` (the claims round's own dispatch, which may quote the brief). The main session (no `agent_id`) and a defined agent are never read. Any read that fails passes.
  - **The measurement**, 2026-11-25, method: every subagent transcript of this session (c6fd72d1, 579 builders) read for its first row and its own Agent calls. The 12 builders whose brief held a line opening `STOP POINT` (449 T431-T435, 451 T230-T240, from 06:21Z on) dispatched 0 `claims-triage` or `impl-drift`: the split held by brief alone, and the rule refuses none of their calls. The 6 claims-round dispatches (prompts beginning "Run the claims round for feature ...") carry no such line, nor do the 131 claims dispatches the main thread made itself (no `agent_id`): none would be refused. The builders before the brief (449 T426, T427, T429/T430 and T430's finisher) did dispatch claims agents themselves (5, 1, 4 and 3), so "held by brief alone" is true of briefed builders only. What the guard adds: a backstop for a briefed builder that drifts; it is silent where the brief is omitted.
  - **Why the marker, not every builder** (spec-fidelity MODE 4 round 1, 2026-11-25, asked for the count). Of the same 579 builders, 85 with no `STOP POINT` line, the claims-round dispatches aside, dispatched a claims agent themselves, measured 2026-11-25 (their first rows, descriptions and Agent calls): 52 code or landing builders, 19 record or pop-up bundles, 11 page-session cascades and 3 claims rounds worded otherwise ("Claims round: arch claim re-check", "Finish 449 T430's claims round"). Since the split's first brief (06:21Z) there was ONE: the page session P15 cascade ("Run the cascade of page session P15 (feature 449 T436)"), whose claims round is its own correct work. So the wider test - every builder but a prompt opening `Run the claims round` - would have refused correct work on the split's first day, and every page cascade and record bundle after it; a guard that fires on correct work is worse than none (root CLAUDE.md, "What is enforced"). No test the transcripts hold separates a code builder from a record bundle or a cascade but its brief, so the brief carries the mark: the template (`scripts/container/builder-brief.md`) is the coordinating session's standing order for every code builder's dispatch, the guard enforces the split on every builder it sets, and an unmarked builder passes, as D8 passes what it cannot tell.
  - **What is refused.** A code builder's `Agent` call of `claims-triage` or `impl-drift`, or a `Workflow` naming either as an `agentType` (args, a unit's `then` step, or a script literal: a wave of 4 or more runs through `check-wave`, whose units no Agent hook of the builder sees, since `workflow_hooks` replays them without `agent_id`). The refusal names the agent, the brief's STOP POINT (`make claims-triage` and stop), and what to report (the claim keys, what `make claims-owed` lists, the paths to commit). Escape: `SPLIT_OK="<reason>"` in the prompt, recorded (`split-ok`); a firing is recorded `builder-split`.
  - **The handoff names the split.** The cap's refusal, for a code builder only, adds one line: it hands off at its STOP POINT and does not run the claims round. A claims-round dispatch past its cap is not told that.
  - **The brief** (`scripts/container/builder-brief.md`) says the guard keys on its `STOP POINT` line, so the marker is one the brief sets.

### T237 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A code builder stops at its stop point; the coordinating session runs the claims round as its own dispatch. A builder that drifts is refused its claims dispatch, and told what to report instead.
2. **The constraints.** The root CLAUDE.md "What is enforced": a guard that fires on correct work is worse than none, so the rule must refuse none of the coordinating session's claims rounds. The escape states a two-word reason, recorded. The message names the compliant action.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: request.md, "sounds good please do that ASAP". O: this session's 579 builder transcripts, 2026-11-25 (above). The task line: "enforced, not remembered: the context-cap guard's handoff names the split".
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the 12 briefed builders made no claims dispatch, and the 6 claims-round dispatches and the 131 main-thread dispatches carry no mark, measured 2026-11-25 (this session's subagent transcripts, their first rows and Agent calls).
5. **The order.** After the brief template (on main). No other task depends on it.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T237` and the suite. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25: the suite on HEAD's guard gave 34 passed, 8 failed (cases 8 and 9); on the fix, 42 passed, 0 failed. Fires-proof: HEAD is the rule deleted, and case 8 goes red there.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: the split was remembered (in the brief), not enforced. No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- `workflow_hooks` replays a `check-wave` unit through the Agent hooks without the caller's `agent_id`, so no builder-keyed rule sees a builder's wave. Effect here: a code builder's wave of claims checks would pass. Fixed here for this rule (the split reads the `Workflow` call itself); the replay itself is left as it is: adding `agent_id` there changes what the event log and the checks' records book, a wider change than this task, and no other builder-keyed Agent rule exists today.

**Performance work?** no: it refuses a dispatch; nothing runs faster or slower.

### T237 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

1. **Where does the time go?** <the stage and the loop: its counted operations, `make work-budget` (a hamlet stage) or `make budget-sheets` (a Mode A stage)>
2. **Removes work, or only moves it?** <fewer candidates, a screen, a kept result, an index, an early stop, a better algorithm,
   a loop into C - or an inlining, a merge, a builtin written out: never the goal, only where the time evidence shows a gain>
3. **What do you expect it to save, and why?** <a share of the stage's profiled time>
4. **How does the work grow with the settlement?** <the growth exponent between sizes, and whether this bends it>
5. **What did the before and after show, and under what conditions?** <the counted operations before and after, and any wall
   time with the host's load - evidence, not a pass>
6. **Did any map move, and does it still keep the research?** <`make maps-moved`, the cohort>

### T226 (page session P7's cascade, 2026-11-24: 0097's drawing page gained the GUESS items `barracks-length-ceiling` and `row-of-48-ft`, and nothing on sheet/barracks' Guesses or Depiction tab says the map draws no row past 145 ft; P15, 01549f3828, the same with 0057's new UNRESEARCHED `toe-shoulder-past-corner` against hamlet/marsh)

- **Approach**: a labeled item new on a drawing page now owes `modal-form` of each About-form pop-up whose `Drawing:` names the page, through the triage, with the item shown to both agents.
  - **The cause, read in the code 2026-11-25.** A moved `Drawing:` page owes a pop-up `modal-depiction` alone (`modals::owed_row`), whose contract is the Depiction tab's COVERAGE, TRUTH and LINKS. The figure the map draws as a guess is a Guesses bullet (dev/modals.md M8, M11), which is `modal-form`'s. Its bundle held no drawing page, so even owed for another reason it could not see the item: in P7 it was owed by the research EDITs and left the 145 ft gap as a NOTE "for the session", observed 2026-11-24, method: p7-cascade.md, stage 2.
  - **A second cause, found on the P15 pair.** The item reader (`l7r_gate_research::record::items`, its TAG) read only an EMPTY token. P15's tag held `<!-- 449 T432, 2026-11-25 -->` inside it, so no reader saw `toe-shoulder-past-corner`: not the owing, not `make research-backlog`, not the claims' item labels. It was the only such tag in `research/questions/`, measured 2026-11-25 by a count of `<span class="item"` against the tags read on every page. The fix: a comment inside the token is read as part of it, and `items::faults` names any item tag the reader still cannot read, with the form to write.
  - **The rule** (`rust/gate/crates/owed/src/record/modals/labeled.rs`):
    - An item owes when its tag is new on a drawing page since the merge base, or its label changed, AND its label is GUESS, UNRESEARCHED, DEVIATION or CONVENTION, AND its block's words did not stand on the page before (`items::blocks`). A tag added to standing words is T192's tagging, which owes nothing, and its test `a_page_gaining_a_tag_owes_no_pop_up` stays green. A relabel rewrites its block, since `items::faults` holds the prose to the label word.
    - It owes each About-form pop-up whose `Drawing:` names the page, split pointers followed, unless its Guesses tab references the item as `{NNNN#<id>}`. That bullet is filled from the tag, so it cascades by regeneration (T187).
    - The unit is `modal-form:<uid>`, with the occasion "a page its Drawing: names gained a labeled item (<page>#<id> <LABEL>, ...)". It is owed only where the pop-up's own text did not already owe its form check.
    - The occasion opens "a page its ", so `make modal-triage` comes first (feature 375 FR-001).
    - Its fingerprint is the form fingerprint plus the items, so its answer covers those items. With none owed, it is the form fingerprint unchanged, so no earlier answer is moved.
  - **Which check owns it.** `modal-form`: M8 and M11 (the drawn figure as a Guesses bullet) and M13 (a deviation in About) are its rules, per its agent file's "What you judge". A CONVENTION is the Depiction tab's, so the form contract leaves it to `modal-depiction`. All four labels still owe, as T236's line asks. `modal-research` judges a bullet's truth against the Entry pages and never reads a drawing page.
  - **The triage** (`triage.rs`):
    - A form unit reads its pop-up's `Drawing:` pages (`pages_of`).
    - The tool's filter may not clear a page carrying an item the unit is owed for (`Unit::held`). The filter reads what a pop-up states, and the item is what it does not state.
    - The MANIFEST lists each such item under its page.
    - The contract gains rule (D): a labeled figure of the pop-up's own thing that its Guesses tab does not hold. An item about another kind on the same page is not (D).
    - A `D:` reply line marks the form unit alone, and an `A:`-`C:` line the other checks (`record`).
  - **The form bundle** (`bundle/modal.rs`):
    - It writes `drawing-items.md`: each such item's reference, label, page, block and bullet.
    - Its `unit:` line carries the fingerprint that owed it.
    - The contract tells it to add the `{NNNN#<id>}` bullet as an M11 FIX.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |

### T243 (the GM 2026-11-25, tasks.md T243 and its amendments (a)-(g) and (i)-(l): a task time breakdown across features, each bucket's minutes and blocking minutes with both percentages, nothing hidden in "other")

- **Approach**: a new command, as the GM approved it (request.md, "2026-11-25: the task time breakdown (451 T243)": the session proposed `make task-time` on `make where-time`, and he answered "that sounds great. Yes, let me know when that's ready."), `make task-time [SINCE=24h|<N>h|<ISO>] [UNTIL=] [F=]` (`rust/gate/crates/measure/src/measure/task_time.rs`, `task_time/book.rs`, `task_time/program.rs`), on `make where-time`'s reader: its runs with their ends and phases (`columns::runs`), its agents and their spans (`columns::flight`, `spent::clip`), its transcript pass (`columns::read_subagents`, which now also keeps each Bash call's command, the session's and its subagents').
  - **One table across features.** Every clone's every event log (and the mirror's, the clones' parent) is read once, each line tagged with its log's feature; a task is keyed (feature, task), since task ids collide across features. This replaces where-time's "another feature" column (361 min of 449's, measured 2026-11-25 (`make where-time F=449 SINCE=2026-11-24T13:20Z`)) and the two reports stitched by hand.
  - **Which tasks.** A task LANDED in the window is one a landing's `end` phase with `landed: true`, inside the window, names in its `tasks` - the landing log. `F=` narrows to one feature's landings. The window's other time is one more section, "the rest of the window" (tasks not landed in it, and `-`), so the window's percentages reconcile. A landed task's tables carry its WHOLE time, not only its time inside the window: in the GM's sentence the 24 hours picks which tasks ("the tasks that have landed over the last 24 hours"), and "the time that was spent" is the time spent on them (round 2 of this section's review). The command reads `BACK=` hours before the window (default 48h, a GUESS and a knob: two days covers most tasks' start), books the task's whole time from there, and prints beside its tables its time inside the window and that share; a landed task whose first start in any tree's `task-starts.jsonl` precedes the read-back, or that has no start recorded, is named in its heading ("started <time>, before the read-back: its time before <read-back> is not in its tables", or "no start recorded: its time before <read-back> may be missing") and on the report's "Cut at the read-back" line (`none` when nothing is cut), so the cut is never silent (round 3 of this section's review; `BACK=` reads further; the round arbiter's ruling on trigger `round:spec-fidelity|plan:451-time-retro-and-efficiency#T243@4`, CONTINUE, recorded in its log, let round 4 judge the knob so named, and round 4 ruled it LEGITIMATE); the window's own tables, the rest and the whole window, stay clipped to the window, so their percentages still sum to 100. Each hour read back costs about 1.3 s, measured 2026-11-25 (`make task-time` took 55 s for SINCE=24h and 238 s for SINCE=168h). Reading back also corrects the window's own figures: a wait begun before the window needs its `Stop` read, and with nothing read back the test's window lost 3.0 of its 3.8 blocking minutes, measured 2026-11-25 (`a_landed_task_carries_its_time_before_the_window`).
  - **Minutes** (amendment (b): machine time, overlapping): every main session's and builder's own time, every review agent's span, every Bash run (foreground and background, its phases split out as where-time splits them), every page-session phase. Percent of minutes is of the summed minutes.
  - **Blocking minutes** (amendment (b)): each main session's wall clock inside the window, each second once per task it blocks, walked: its own turns and calls are its own; a wait - between turns on work (the `Stop`'s `inflight`), or a wait loop - is booked at each instant, for each task its work in flight blocks, to that task's thing in flight that ends LAST (its critical one), and into a builder it descends the same way: the builder's turns, its foreground commands, its waits on its own background runs and agents (a wait loop, or a turn that ends after its own background work did: the turn up to that end is the wait). A review agent's piece is its kind's. Each piece is booked to the task it BLOCKED (amendment (l), below), and a piece that blocked no task is named apart; the tasks' sum and the blocking-no-task time together reach each session's clock or pass it (the booking tests pin the identity, `>=`, and exactly the clock on their one-task worked days), and the window's blocking is the sum over tasks, which passes the clock where tasks ran side by side, in one session or across clones - the header says so. Every blocking percentage is of that sum (less the GM's, amendment (i)), never of the clock, so the window's tables still sum to 100 over the working time and a task's share reads as its part of all tasks' blocking. The clue's reading and the window's sweeps sit in `task_time/book/clue.rs` and `book/window.rs` (book.rs passed the 1,000-line bar).
  - **Model turns** (the task line's first fix): the gap from an actor's line to its next call is booked by the tool that call is - Read/Grep/Glob reading code, Edit/Write writing code, Bash running a command, Agent dispatching, other tools by name, a gap ending at a `Stop` its reply - the main session's and the builders' apart, a tool's own run joined to its turn's category.
  - **Agents never pooled** (amendment (f)): a review agent's whole span books to its kind - plan review (spec-fidelity, -verify), claims round (claims-triage, impl-drift), record and pop-up checks (the guard's `RECORD_CHECKS`, modal-triage, source-filter, size-exception), arbiter, the GM's filter (escalation-check), research and page sessions (research-pass and the page sessions' phases), map and building reviews (the guard's `REVIEW_CHECKS`), other review agents (work-budget, message-check) - by the guard's `agent_category` where it has a row, no third table. Every other kind is a builder.
  - **Review by kind** (amendment (e)): the review bucket's commands split by target into plan review (decide, plan-delta, plan-verdict), claims round (claims-*, impl-check), record and pop-up checks (check-bundle, modal-bundle, record-owed, modal-triage(d), modal-prepass, translation-owed, record-checked, record-prepass, style-prepass, quote-verbatim), arbiter (arbiter-*), and review's other commands; each kind's "commands" row sits beside its "agents" row.
  - **Per make target** (amendment (g)): a table of every target and program run - runs, minutes, blocking, both percentages, the category it books to - beside the category table, for each landed task, the rest and the whole window. A Bash call with no booked target is listed by its program (`program.rs`): the classes are the measured ones (next item). A make target is read from the command only by `shared::make::invoked`, the guards' one detector, which counts a call at a command position and never a mention: a line that logged no target (a past log) whose command runs one the table books is booked by the table, as a logged one is. Before this rule a loose `make <word>` pattern read prose in a commit message or a grep pattern as a run (`make the`, `make sure`, `make charcoal` rows), and a `make rust-test` its log line did not name was listed as unbooked, measured 2026-11-25 (`make task-time SINCE=24h`, a probe printing each such run's id, `makes` and bucket). Nothing is booked "other": a target the guard's table does not book is listed by name, under the category "Makefile targets the guard's table does not book".
  - **The 610 minutes, measured** (the task line's second fix): measured 2026-11-25 (a scratch reader over every clone's logs, each command joined from the transcripts) from 2026-11-24T13:20Z to 2026-11-25T13:20Z, the unbooked Bash calls were 6,481 runs and 1,640 machine minutes (610 of them in 449's and 451's logs, two runs still open at the window's end, 990 and 553 min, left out, since an open run's end is the window's, not its own, measured 2026-11-25 (the scratch reader below)): the main session's `until grep -q '^ALL DONE' .../page-sessions/run-*.log` waits 1,247 min (24 runs), builders' `until [ -s ... ]`/`sleep N` waits 71, shell reads and file edits 96, `for` loops over `pdftotext`, `make apply-edits` and `make reserve` 72, the builders' scratch `run.sh` cohort sweeps 32 (each runs `make cohort` several times in parallel), `python3` 12.5, `git` 6.3, and targets the table does not book (`source-pages` 12.7, `research-search` 11.9, `crate-checks` 8.8, `apply-edits` 5.3, `source-outcome` 4.2, `reserve` 3.1, ...), measured 2026-11-25 (a scratch reader over the logs, each command joined from the session's and its subagents' transcripts, a background run ended as `columns::runs` ends one). The classes named sum to about 1,583 min, the rest small `for` loops and program classes, measured 2026-11-25 (the classes above, summed). `task-time` joins `where-time` in the docs row; no other row moves, since the breakdown books by its own categories ("Generating maps" below), and every target the table leaves unbooked is listed by name.
  - **A page session is not a main session.** A detached page session is a `claude` session of its own and logs as one (its `Phase` lines' `name` is its session id): its turns and runs are its phases' minutes, under "research and page sessions", and its clock is nobody's blocking. Before this rule the first 24-hour run booked its sessions' turns 393 min of "main session" blocking, measured 2026-11-25 (`make task-time SINCE=24h`, then a session id of a page phase's `name` found as a `sid` in 449's log).
  - **Generating maps** (the GM's "generating maps", beside compiling, tests and landing): one category, `map generation`, holds the map and sheet targets' runs (`map`, `hamlet`, `compound`, `sheet-render`, `maps-moved`, which the guard's table books tests, and `cohort`, `cohort-landing`, which it books gate), the phases where-time already books that column (`map`, `cohort`, the gate's `seeds` and `reference`), and a builder's scratch `run.sh` sweep (it runs `make cohort` several times). The breakdown's categories are its own: the guard's table and where-time keep their buckets, so no row of the guard's file moves. `crate-checks`, which the table leaves unbooked, runs a crate's tests, lint and cover, so it books to tests. The research and page targets the table leaves unbooked (`source-pages`, `research-search`, `apply-edits`, `source-outcome`, `reserve`, ...) fit no category the GM named, so each is listed by name under `Makefile targets the guard's table does not book`.
  - **Wait loops** do no work: their minutes are the time each was held open, named "wait loops (held open, no work)" (or "on page sessions"), and their blocking is booked to what they waited on - a page-session wait to the page sessions' phases running then.
  - **Nothing silent** (amendment (c)): what cannot be booked is named in its own row and the footnote - a wait with nothing in flight (`waiting: nothing in flight - <class>`, amendment (j)), a monitor with no page session running (`waiting: a monitor alone`), a builder's time inside its span no line of its accounts for, a command no transcript holds, the Bash calls refused before running and the phases tied to no run (counted, minutes stated), and each landed task whose time is cut at the read-back (the "Which tasks" item).
  - **The biggest blocking and parallelism** (amendment (d)): the five biggest blocking categories are listed first, each with its share that was a foreground run in its actor - which could have run in the background beside other work - and the rest already in the background and waited on; a model's turn, an agent's span or a wait is "serial in its actor: parallel only across more actors". A measured proxy, labeled so in the report.
  - **The name where timings are gathered** (the task line's last item, "everywhere that we're gathering these timings"): the root CLAUDE.md (one line under "Verification and iteration"), the Makefile help of `task-time` and `where-time`, `docs/efficiency-tooling.md` (section 6's table), and a comment at each gatherer. The gatherers were found by search from the function each kind of timing is written or computed through, observed 2026-11-25, each command's hits listed (tests left out), the name at every hit or the reason it is not a gatherer:

1. **The goal, in the world.** One command answers where a day's time went per landed task: what we spent, what we waited on, and whether the biggest waits could run in parallel, with no percentage math left to the GM.
2. **The constraints.** T243's task line and amendments (a)-(g) and (i)-(l) ((l), the GM's definition of blocking, replacing (k)'s reading); FR-005's reader (one reader: where-time's runs and agents, not a copy); D2's one category table; the guard's agent kinds.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's amendments of 2026-11-25 (tasks.md T243). O: the measurement of the unbooked minutes above; `make where-time F=449` of 13:20Z.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the fixture day is worked second by second, its blocking summing to its session's clock, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/measure`); the 24-hour run over the real logs is in the handoff.
5. **The order.** After T08-T11 (the reader it builds on). No task waits on it.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T243 F=451`. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.

11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.

### T244 (the GM 2026-11-25, tasks.md T244: "I would like to essentially defer all of it until at least tomorrow ... will our current procedures end up inadvertently kicking off a bunch of research tasks ... If so, then what can we do about that?")

- **Approach**: a `research` switch in `dev/switches.json`, beside `claims` and `port`, and the three places research starts read it.
  - **The switch.** `research` is `open` (the default, the shipped rules) or `deferred`. It is thrown like the others, with a reason recorded with who and when: `make research-deferred REASON="..."` and `make research-open REASON="..."` through `_switch`, which commits it. `make switches` shows it, and `l7r-gate switches state research` prints it. Its one reader is `l7r_shared::switches::research` (new, `rust/guard/shared/src/switches.rs`), which the guard, the tick and the switches tool all call. The guard cannot build on a gate crate (`check guard-deps`), and the task crate does not build on `ci`. A missing file or entry reads `open`. A malformed entry also reads `open`, with MALFORMED in its why. That is the label of this decision: `open` is the state in which the research rules bind, as `clean` is for claims, so a broken file never silently defers research. **A defect fixed on the way:** `switches::write` serialized only `claims` and `port`, so any later `make claims-*` or `make port-*` would have dropped a third axis. It now writes all three, pinned by a test (set research, then claims; research survives).
  - **(1) The box answer.** While deferred, a `research: physical` task's boxes may be answered `deferred: UNRESEARCHED` instead of by a pass. The literal text goes on the box line itself, after its box(es): `- [ ] research pass  deferred: UNRESEARCHED`. It goes on the box line because the tick keeps only box lines below `verify:` (feature 315), so an answer on a line of its own would be cut. Every box on an answered line is answered, and any of the five boxes may take the answer. An answered box stays `[ ]`, and `BOXES=1` does not tick it, because a tick would say a pass ran. At tick and land (`tick/text.rs::boxes_refusal`, the one rule both ask), an answered open box is no refusal while the switch is `deferred`. While the switch is `open`, an answered box is refused with or without `BOXES=1`, and the refusal names the switch. The standing rule over every tasks file (`research_boxes.rs::violations`) accepts an answered box whatever the switch's state, so a task ticked while deferred stays green once the switch reopens; its answer is the history. The tick does not check that `make research-backlog` lists the decision. The backlog is keyed by claim and page item, not by task, so the check would need each task to name its items, a form no task has. The answer's text and the refusal's wording name the backlog instead (GUESS: the cheaper route, taken where the record is silent).
  - **(2) A port stage's end.** No tool enforces "each port stage's end searches the ones it touched"; it is prose in the root CLAUDE.md's Research bullet and `docs/research-doctrine.md` (the T236 restatement, and the citation-rules paragraph). Both are restated to say that while the switch is `deferred`, a stage's end LISTS what it touched (`make research-backlog STAGE=<stage>`) and does not search it. While deferred, the exception that still searches first ("other code builds on it or a guess is likely visibly wrong") goes through `RESEARCH_OK` too, because the GM deferred "all of it". The `research-backlog` target's help line says the same.
  - **(3) The guard.** New `research_switch_hooks.rs` (PreToolUse, `Agent|Bash`). While the switch is `deferred` it refuses:
    - an Agent dispatch of `research-pass`. A check-wave unit is covered too, because `workflow_hooks` puts each unit through the Agent hooks.
    - a Bash call that invokes `make page-session`, read by `shared::make::targets` (an invocation, not a mention).
    The refusal names the switch, its reason, who threw it and when, and the compliant steps: label the decision UNRESEARCHED onto `make research-backlog`, or `make research-open REASON=` once the GM turns to research. `RESEARCH_OK="<reason>"` is the escape, in the prompt or the command, and is logged `escaped`. A bare token is refused (`shared::escape`). Each refusal is logged `blocked`. While `open`, the guard is silent. The switch is read from the session's clone, else the mirror. Its tests run on fixture trees (open, deferred, missing, malformed), never the live file. It is registered in `guards.rs` and `lib.rs`, with the suite `tests/hooks/research-switch-hooks.sh` -> `guard-shim.sh` and `test-research-switch-hooks.sh`. Its messages go through `make guard-messages`.
  - **Not built:** impl-drift's NEEDS-RESEARCH verdicts already stay listed and refuse nothing while claims stand at `report` (feature 445), so the T244 line's last clause needs no code.

### T244 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** No map changes. While the GM defers research, no procedure of this repository starts a search pass or a page session unasked. A physical task lands with its decision drawn UNRESEARCHED onto the backlog. Reopening is one `make research-open REASON=`.
2. **The constraints.** The T244 line. The switches' form (`docs/switches.md`: reason required, recorded who and when, an unknown key ignored). The guard doctrine (root CLAUDE.md "What is enforced": match invocations, not mentions; the escape checked first; proven to fire). T236's backlog rule.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM 2026-11-25 (tasks.md T244). R: `docs/research-doctrine.md` T236's restatement. O: the code read 2026-11-25 (`ci/switches.rs` writes two axes; `tick/text.rs::boxes_refusal`; `research_boxes.rs::violations`).

### T242 (451 T238's landing, 2026-11-25: its tick left staged, the push refusing the dirty clone, the revert refused; T238 reached main only with T240's landing)

- **Approach**: `rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/writers.rs`, new, called from `land.rs` and `cheap.rs`.
  - **What happened, measured 2026-11-25** (the clone's 451 event log, its reflog, the T240 builder's transcript). T238's `make land` ran in the clone `/diagram/.clones/diagram-backlog`, clean at its start (12:28:20), so it did not land alone (451 T88). T240's builder was dispatched into the same clone at 12:28:29. Its first Edit came at 12:32:44, after the landing ended. The push step failed with exit 1 at 12:29:21. The reflog holds no commit between the escape records (12:29:13) and the tick commit made by hand at 12:29:39. So the landing's `git commit` of the tick made nothing. `tick_and_push` never read that commit's exit (`self.run(..)?` stops only on a spawn failure). It then read HEAD, the escape-record commit, as the tick's. `sync-with-main.sh done` refused the dirty clone (its `die`, exit 1). The revert, aimed at that wrong commit, was refused by the staged tick. On a scratch repository a staged change refuses `git revert` with the incident's own words ("your local changes would be overwritten by revert"), observed 2026-11-25. Why the commit failed is NOT measured. A held `index.lock` (exit 128, what was added left staged, observed 2026-11-25 on the scratch repository) is a hypothesis: the builder's calls in that second ran grep and sed.
  - **The rule as built.**
    - (1) **In the first pass** (`cheap.rs`), the refusal "uncommitted changes - commit them first" becomes `writer_refusal`. It lists the clone's `git status --porcelain` lines that are not the landing's own, the first six and a count of the rest. The landing's own escape records are committed before it asks (feature 408). Where an open builder handoff names the clone, the refusal names that handoff too. The handoff is `<git common dir>/l7r-handoffs/T<n>-<agent>.md`, and it counts when:
      - its text names the clone's root as a whole path (`<root>-t235` does not count);
      - its task is not one being landed;
      - its task is open (`- [ ] T<n>`) in some `specs/*/tasks.md`. A ticked task is a closed handoff, as the context-cap guard reads a resume;
      - it was written in the last 24 hours (`HANDOFF_FRESH_S`, a CONVENTION knob). Task numbers repeat across features. Measured 2026-11-25 (a script of this rule over the clone's handoff directory): of 538 files, 26 named the clone with a task open in some other feature's tasks.md, all 2 to 5 days old, and with the bound none is named.

      A handoff is named only beside changes, never a refusal on its own.
    - (2) **The same check runs again at the push step's start**, before the ticks. A refusal there means nothing is ticked and nothing pushed.
    - (3) **The tick's own `git add` and `git commit` are read** (`commit_tick`). A commit refused for `index.lock` is tried three times, 500 ms apart (`COMMIT_TRIES`, `COMMIT_POLL_MS`, a CONVENTION knob). Where the add or the commit fails, the ticks are put back (`put_back`): the tick's paths are unstaged and the feature's directory is checked out from HEAD. The archives a tick created are removed, the fixes' rows are pending again, and the tick's own escape record is committed. Nothing is left staged. The refused-tick branch shares `put_back`.
    - (4) **The revert after a failed push now always names the tick's own commit** (its id is read only from a successful commit). Where another writer's edit blocks that revert, the tick commit stands, committed and never staged, with the message that already says so.
  - **Where it sits beside landing alone (451 T88, T101).** A clone dirty at `make land`'s start still lands alone, unchanged: `alone_owed` is asked before the first pass, and `land-alone.sh` step 3 already sorts the clone's files into the task's own, another task's and unnamed. This refusal reads the tree the landing ticks in. That is the clone on a direct landing, which was clean when it started, so dirt there arrived since. In the landing worktree's own run (`L7R_LAND_ALONE`), nobody else writes. Refusing a dirty clone outright before `alone_owed` would reverse T88, so it is not done.
  - **A writer arriving during the gate.** The claims wait, before the push step, already waits up to 20 min (`CLAIMS_WAIT_S`, 405 T50's knob) for a clean tree and then refuses with nothing ticked (a pin, `a_writer_arriving_during_the_gate_ticks_nothing`). It waits rather than refuses because the session commits the claims round's records beside the gate. Check (2) covers the seconds between that wait and the ticks. It also keeps (3)'s put-back from taking another writer's edit of the feature's files: they held none just before.
  - **A builder's worktree.** Today's parallel trial builds in linked worktrees and carries commits into the clone by cherry-pick. A worktree's uncommitted work bears on none of this. Its files and index are its own, never in the clone's `git status`, and its handoff names the worktree, not the clone. A landing from the clone with a dirty worktree and that handoff lands (`a_builders_worktree_bears_on_nothing`).

### T242 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A landing never leaves a tick staged. When another writer's changes are in the clone, it says so before anything long runs and again before the ticks, naming the changes and that writer's handoff. When its push fails, the tick is committed or put back.
2. **The constraints.** 451 T88 and T101: a dirty clone at the start lands alone, so the refusal must not reverse that. Feature 408: the landing's own escape records are its own. CLAUDE.md: never rewrite history, so the put-back is a checkout and the failed-push undo a revert, never a reset of a commit. The task's line: a fixture remote, never the real one, and no live fetches.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task's line in tasks.md (filed from T238's landing). O: the handoff directory's count, 2026-11-25. O: the 451 event log, the clone's reflog and the T240 builder's transcript, 2026-11-25. O: the scratch repository probes of `index.lock` and `git revert`, 2026-11-25.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes, measured 2026-11-25 (above). The incident's commit failed while the clone held no other writer's file. So the fix that answers it is (3), and (1) and (2) answer the task's named refusal, measured 2026-11-25 (the event log's Edit lines and the reflog).
5. **The order.** No dependency. T235 is built beside this in its own worktree and touches no file of the `land` crate.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T242`. Red: what failed is recorded and the task set down, and a claim that it cannot be done is ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/land`, logs in the session scratchpad `t242-red.log` and `t242-green.log`). HEAD's behavior was restored in place: the pre-tick check disabled and the add and commit unread. With it, four of the new tests failed: the pre-tick refusal, the failed commit, the lock held once and the failed add. Each is a landing that reported landed with its tick staged, or ticked past a foreign change. With the fix, 107 passed and 0 failed.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: the landing left a tick staged, and its revert named the wrong commit. A revert that had succeeded would have undone the landing's escape records and reported "its ticks reverted". No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- The failed push's revert named HEAD whatever the tick's commit did. Effect: a tick commit that failed sent the revert at the commit before it. Fixed here by (3).

**Performance work?** no: a `git status` and a directory read in the first pass and at the push.

### T235 (the Stop hook's QUESTION UNFILTERED fired on statements, `Nothing is waiting on you.` and `That lets you see, for example, whether ...` among them, each costing an escalation-check run that kept the reply as information; the GM asked 2026-11-25 for efficiencies in that check (request.md, "the escalation check's cost"), and the session's reply named a mechanical pre-filter as T235's shape)

- **Approach**: `escalation_hooks::classify` is narrowed where it read statements as asks, and keeps every ask and offer it read before.
  - **The corpus.** Every QUESTION/OFFER UNFILTERED refusal in the main-session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/*/`, paired with the final message it read (the refusal's quoted line checked against the rule's first ask; 4 pairings that read another record dropped), deduplicated: 112 messages, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-25, observed 2026-11-25, method: a scan of every transcript record that opens `Stop hook feedback` and the last assistant text before it. Each was labeled by hand, observed 2026-11-25, method: the session's reading of each flagged line in its message: T (it puts a question, decision or offer to the GM) 74, B (borderline: a pointer to a question already kept, or a decision deferred to a later report) 8, F (a statement) 30. The corpus stays in the session scratchpad, not the repository, which is public and the messages are the GM's sessions; the task's own named statements are the committed cases.
  - **Where the false firings came from** (each alternative's firings, alone and in all, on the corpus, 2026-11-25, method: the rule's alternatives one at a time over the labeled messages). `which (one|of|would|do you)` fired on 18 F messages and no T that another alternative did not also catch: it read relative clauses (`which of them give wrong answers`, `which would mean`, `which one clone holds`). `waiting (on|for) (you|your)` fired alone on 9 F, 6 T and 2 B: negated (`Nothing is waiting on you`), a measure (`442 minutes of waiting on you`, `the time spent waiting on you`) or a measure's name (`**Waiting on you** is still reported`, `| Waiting for you to answer | 0.5 | 1% |`), against the label form (`**Waiting on you:** the removal command ...`). `needs your` and `ask you` fired on 3 F, each negated (`Nothing needs your decision`, `didn't ask you anything`).
  - **The rule.** `ASK` keeps a question's own words, `which` only as the interrogative (`which (one |of these|those|them|the two )?(do you|would you|should I|shall I)`). The alternatives that STATE a decision is his (`your call`, `for you to decide`, `ask you`, `needs your ...`, `waiting on you`, `yours to decide`) move to `STATED`, an ask unless the text before it negates it in its clause (`nothing`, `none`, `nobody`, `neither`, `no one`, or `not`/`never`/`-n't` within two words, with no `but`, `except`, `without`, `until`, `unless`, `besides` or `than` between, and no `but`, `except`, `besides`, `other than` or `apart from` after it in the clause), it follows `of` or `spent` (a measure), or a `waiting ...` opening its sentence is a measure's name: the subject of `is`/`was`/`were` (`**Waiting on you** is still reported`), or a table row's first cell with no `:` in it (`| Waiting for you to answer | 0.5 |`; a later cell, `| T26 | Waiting on your budget answer |`, is an ask). With a colon it is a label and an ask, and with neither (`Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.`) an ask; spec-fidelity's first MODE 4 round of 2026-11-25 found the earlier bound, any sentence-opening `waiting` with no colon, let that last form through. `OFFER` gains `if you agree` and a sentence opening `Say if`, the brief's named offers that fired only when another phrase stood beside them. The `?` rule is unchanged, still per line, and the kept-id check still reads the whole line.
  - **Measured on the corpus.** Each message ran through the real guard (`tests/hooks/escalation-hooks.sh stop`, a fixture clone whose transcript holds one GM message and no filter). Before, 112 of 112 fired, precision 66.1% (T only) and 73.2% (T and B), measured 2026-11-25 (the corpus through HEAD's guard). After, 82 fired, precision 90.2% (T only) and 100% (T and B), with all 74 T and all 8 B still firing and all 30 F passing, measured 2026-11-25 (the corpus through the fixed guard). The corpus holds only firings, so it cannot show new ones. The two added offer forms were run over the 6,374 end-of-turn messages of the same transcripts that the old rule passed, and fire on 28 lines, each an offer on reading (`If you agree, I'll file it as a 451 task.`, `Say if you meant otherwise; otherwise the question is moot.`), measured 2026-11-25 (the two patterns over every `end_turn` record the old rule passed). Every other change only narrows.
  - **Recall, beyond the corpus.** Feature 429 FR-002's own case, the 2026-10-25 feature 417 message (two choices put to the GM), is the suite's case 9 and is still refused, measured 2026-11-25 (`tests/hooks/test-escalation-hooks.sh`, 53 passed). The exemptions are bounded so a decision put to him still fires: the negation needs a `nothing`-like subject in the same clause, or `not` within two words, with no exceptive between or after (`It is not landed, and it is waiting on your go-ahead.`, `This can't land without your call.`, `Nothing is left but your call on the split.` and `Nothing else needs your decision except the budget.` fire; spec-fidelity's MODE 4 round of 2026-11-25 found the last three let through by the first bound), and the measure's-name form needs `waiting` to open its sentence as the subject of `is`/`was`/`were` or as a table row's first cell with no `:` (`**Waiting on you:** the removal command ...`, `Waiting on your go-ahead to land it.`, `| T22 | Waiting on you: the budget's words |` and `| T26 | Waiting on your budget answer |` fire); each is pinned by the new test's asks.
  - **The 8 borderline firings stay as they were.** Two point to a question already put to him (`Still waiting for your decision: the three questions ... (374#90, 385#107, 397#11)`, `T26 is still waiting on your budget answer`); feature 432 already exempts a line naming a kept question by its id, read from the clone's `gm-review.jsonl`, so the first fires only where those rows were not kept. Three defer a decision to him (`a candidate fix for you to decide on`, a budget overage brought at the port's end, a proposal sent after the filter). One pauses for his word (`When you want me to resume, ...`). Two invite him to look at a sheet (`If you'd like to look at the moved sheets`), and fire as offers, whose significance escalation-check judges (feature 429 amendment 1: it keeps the significant offers and cuts the routine). Each puts something to him, so none is information only, and none is a defect of this rule.
  - **The pre-filter, read two ways.** The GM's words (request.md, 2026-11-25) ask whether there are more efficient ways to run the check; the pre-filter is the session's answer to him, relayed by the coordinating session's brief as his request. As that reply sketched it (`the hook could send the agent only messages that put something to you: a sentence ending in "?" addressed to you, or an offer`), it is this rule: plain status no longer reaches the agent. A narrower prompt (only the flagged sentences sent to escalation-check, not the draft) would change that agent's contract and its refusal texts, which no words of his ask for; it is not built here. A strictly "?"-or-offer rule (any sentence ending in "?" with `you`, `your` or `I`, or an offer) was priced on the corpus: it fires on 50 of the 74 T and drops 24, measured 2026-11-25 (that rule over the labeled corpus), the asks with no "?" (`whether to keep it is your call`, `**Waiting on you:** the removal command ...`, `It needs your words`, `Say the word and I'll carry on`).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `which` only as the interrogative | `a_statement_that_nothing_waits_on_the_gm_is_no_ask` (`which one clone holds`, `which would mean`), red on HEAD; suite case 12 | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a stated decision negated, a measure, or a measure's name | the same test's `Nothing is waiting on you.` and its siblings, red on HEAD; its asks (`**Waiting on you:** ...`, `waiting on your go-ahead`, `your call`) green both sides | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| `if you agree` and `Say if` as offers | the same test's offers, red on HEAD; suite case 12 "an offer on the GM's agreement", red on HEAD | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T235 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A final message that only reports, including one saying nothing waits on the GM, ends its turn with no escalation-check run. A message that puts a question, a decision or an offer to him is still refused until the filter has read it.
2. **The constraints.** Feature 429 FR-002 and amendment 1: a question or an offer with no review behind it owes the filter. Feature 432: a kept question named by its id is no new ask. The T235 task line and its 2026-11-25 amendment: the recorded statements are its cases.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task line, its amendment, and the GM's 2026-11-25 words on the check's cost (request.md, "the escalation check's cost and the Stop hook's false questions"), with the session's pre-filter reply beside them. O: the corpus measurement above. The offer half is feature 429 amendment 1 (the suite's case 10 heading names it; the hook's OFFER UNFILTERED refusal is its build).
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: the corpus of 112 real firings ran through the real guard before and after, measured 2026-11-25 (`tests/hooks/escalation-hooks.sh stop` on each message).
5. **The order.** No dependency. T242, built beside it, touches no file of this task.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T235 F=451`. Red: what failed is recorded and the task set down, and a claim that it cannot be done is ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25. On HEAD's code the new Rust test failed (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`: 509 passed, 1 failed, on `Nothing is waiting on you.`), and `tests/hooks/test-escalation-hooks.sh` gave 45 passed, 8 failed (the seven statements refused, the `If you agree` offer passed). After the fix: 510 passed, and the suite 53 passed, 0 failed. The asks MODE 4 named were added red too: on the first bound the test failed on `This can't land without your call.` (509 passed, 1 failed), and passed once the exceptives were read, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`). The corpus's precision rose from 66.1% to 90.2% with no T lost, measured 2026-11-25 (the corpus through the guard, before and after).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: the hook refused turns that asked the GM nothing, each an escalation-check run and a turn. No map changes.

**Found and left?** none.

**Performance work?** no: it removes false refusals of a Stop hook; nothing runs faster.

### T245 (the GM 2026-11-25; measured 2026-11-25 (`du`, `df`, `make cache-clean DRY=1`): the disk at 88-90%, the build cache 190 GB against its own 100 GB budget, the cleanup freeing 27 MB)

- **Approach**: Four parts in `rust/guard/src/guards/scratch_sweep_hooks/`, each a `--scratch-sweep` mode or a rule under the existing ones.
  - **The audit** (`disk/audit.rs`, `make disk-audit`): every place this container writes, each with its size, its largest entries with their owner (a tree, a session, a project) and age, and a budget (each a GUESS): the build cache by tree (100 GB, `L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB`), `/tmp/claude-<uid>` by session (20), the transcripts `~/.claude/projects` (20), the guard log (1), `/tmp/l7r-*` (5), the rest of this user's `/tmp` (10), the clones (25), the mirror outside the clones (25), the rest of `~/.cache` (5). Each budget is a GUESS, set from the 2026-11-25 measurement (`du` of each, `df`), recorded beside the constants. Then the total against the disk, the unaccounted remainder (the overlay's `df` counts the host's disk), and what the low-disk eviction would free now. Read-only.
  - **The budget held** (`sweep/evict.rs`, called from `cargo::plan` with a `Budget`): past the budget, whole profiles of live trees' build directories go (`debug/`, `cover-gate/`, `tool/`, each a child directory, never the build directory's own files). Least recently built goes first, and only until the cache is back within the budget. A profile goes only when it is idle past `L7R_CACHE_IDLE_HOURS` (12), its build directory is not in use (`cargo::in_use`), and the build directory is not the mirror's. An idle tree's profiles rank first: one whose trees are gone, or whose HEAD log has not moved in the knob with no live process cwd in it. An active tree's idle profiles rank after. Then the old variants, as before. The unit is the profile, not the tree: measured 2026-11-25 (`find -printf '%T@'` over each profile), `diagram-backlog-land/tool` was written at 13:28 while its 25 GB `cover-gate` was last built at 07:34, so a per-tree age would keep what is idle.
  - **The trigger** (`disk/low.rs`): a prompt reads the disk (`Config::disk`: `SCRATCH_SWEEP_DF`, else one `df`). Below `L7R_DISK_FREE_PCT` (GUESS 20) free, with no eviction in the hour, it starts `--scratch-sweep evict` detached. The eviction frees what the budget asks or the disk's shortfall, whichever is more, and writes one line that the next prompt says (an `additionalContext` notice) and removes. A "found nothing it may take" line is said once until an eviction frees something again. A build running holds it, and the stamp is removed so the next prompt tries again.
  - **A removed worktree's build directory with it**: T158's proven-dead rule loses its idle wait (`cargo::dead`; a build running in one is `in_use`). The day's sweep removes the clean scratch worktrees first, then plans, so their build directories go in the same sweep. `make land`'s `landed` removes each cleaned tree's build directory (`sweep::gone_targets`). A hand `git worktree remove` is caught at the next sweep (a session's first prompt, the day's, `make cache-clean`, the trigger).
  - **Never under a running build**: T158's global hold stays (no cache work while a cargo, rustc or clippy process runs). Each removal of a cache entry re-checks it (`sweep::take`), because an eviction walks for seconds.
  - **The cost, and who chose it.** A profile taken is a cold rebuild of that profile at its tree's next build, one crate's coverage family taking minutes and the landing tree's whole set (46 GB, measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`)) making its next landing's gate cold. T158 kept every live tree's build directory whole under the GM's condition of no loss of performance. The GM's T245 words ask for something triggered automatically below a share of free space, and the coordinating session's build of them (request.md) asks for the budget made to hold by evicting idle trees' targets. A full disk is the 2026-11-22 failure, in which every builder's coverage run failed for want of space. Alternatives priced: a larger budget, which holds nothing as each parallel tree adds 13-14 GB (measured 2026-11-25 (`du` of a trial's build directory)), evicting only gone trees, which freed 27 MB (measured 2026-11-25 (`make cache-clean DRY=1`)), and evicting by tree rather than profile, which keeps the idle 25 GB set above (measured 2026-11-25 (`du`)). The T245 builder chose the profile as the unit under that build; the knobs are the budget, the idle hours and the free share.
  - **The audit register** (449 T437 item 13) gets the disk entry: noted here, not built (the brief).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the budget's eviction of live trees' idle profiles | `choose` returning nothing: `evict::tests` (2), `disk::tests::past_the_budget_...` and both `low::tests` red, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`, 507 passed, 8 failed with all four rules off) | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the low-disk trigger | `trigger` never starting: `low::tests::below_the_share_free_...` and `a_build_holds_...` red | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a removed worktree's build directory with it | the idle wait restored: `disk::tests::the_cleanup_takes_...` and the floor refusal's count red; `gone_targets` off: `a_landing_removes_...` red | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the audit | `audit::tests::the_audit_names_every_place_...` (new mode, red by absence) | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T245 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** One command shows what this container leaves on disk and whose it is. The build cache is brought back toward its budget by taking idle trees' targets first (the brief's words, request.md's T245 entry), and never what a running build or a tree in use within the knob holds (the brief's "never under a running build"). Where those working sets alone pass the budget, as measured in item 4, the cache stays over it, and the audit says by how much. Holding the budget (100 GB, `L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB`, GUESS) there would mean evicting a tree's working set mid-task, which neither the GM's words nor the brief ask. A disk under the free share (20%, GUESS, `L7R_DISK_FREE_PCT`) is acted on at the next prompt, which says in one line what was freed. A removed worktree's build directory goes with it.
2. **The constraints.** T158's: never a build directory in use, never while a build runs, never the mirror's (the guard's kept binary), never through a symlink. Tests never delete outside a temp root (every test's `Config` points at a `TempDir`; the sweep tests' `world` sets a disk well above the share).
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's three sentences (request.md, "2026-11-25: what this container leaves on disk"), with the coordinating session's build of them beside, not as his words. O: the measurements of 2026-11-25 below.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes, on the live disk, read-only. The disk held 432.5 GB used of 494.5 GB (df's bytes, 461 GiB), 62.0 GB free (12%), measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`, 60 s). The places the audit lists held 255.7 GB, with 176.7 GB unaccounted, outside the container's view, measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`). The build cache was 182.6 GB, OVER by 82.6 GB (diagram-backlog 84.4 GB, -land 46.1 GB, -research 20.5 GB, -review 19.1 GB), measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`). `/tmp/claude-1000` was 18.7 GB, 16.0 GB of it one session's still registered as running and so kept (d2dc8c63), measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`, `~/.claude/sessions`). The transcripts were 14.9 GB, the clones 13.8 GB, and the mirror outside the clones 17.6 GB (16.2 GB of it `.specify`, 13 GB of that the source archive), measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`, `du`). The eviction would free 30.5 GB in 76 entries, measured 2026-11-25 (`l7r-guard --scratch-sweep evict-dry`), in this order: the idle trees' profiles (`tree`, `clone`, both tooling landings' `tool`, every profile of diagram-research, 20.5 GB), then the active trees' idle coverage families (diagram-backlog-review's cover-guard, cover-embed, cover-browser, cover-mode_a, then diagram-backlog-land's cover-embed and cover-browser, then diagram-backlog's four idle side profiles), then 0.5 GB of variants. It touched nothing of the trees building then: none of diagram-backlog's debug, cover-gate or tool, nothing of diagram-backlog-t235 (a parallel builder's), nothing of this worktree's, nothing of the mirror's (the same dry run's listing). After it the cache would be about 152 GB, still past the 100 GB budget, measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit` less the dry run): what remains is the two working trees' live sets (diagram-backlog's 84 GB and the landing tree's 44 GB built that morning). The budget is a GUESS knob, and holding it would take an active tree's working set.
5. **The order.** No dependency. T158's floor and cleanup are extended, not replaced.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T245 F=451`. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`): with the four rules disabled (`choose` empty, `trigger` never starting, `gone_targets` empty, the dead rule's idle wait restored), 507 passed and 8 failed, the eight named in the table. Restored, 515 passed and 0 failed (the same 515 tests), measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`). The live dry-run figures are in item 4. Nothing was evicted for real on the live disk (DRY only).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a. New knobs: `L7R_DISK_FREE_PCT` (20, GUESS) and the audit's budgets (GUESS constants), each with its why beside it. The eviction reuses `L7R_CACHE_IDLE_HOURS` and `L7R_CACHE_BUDGET_GB`.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: the cache's budget held nothing (190 GB against 100 GB, measured 2026-11-25 (`du`)), and nothing acted on a disk at 90% (measured 2026-11-25 (`df`)). No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- The free share (GUESS, `L7R_DISK_FREE_PCT`) is read on the host's disk, of which 176.7 GB is not this container's, measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`). With every evictable profile taken, the disk would sit at about 18.7% free, measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit` and the dry run), so the trigger would keep finding nothing. Visible effect: an hourly "nothing it may take" line at a prompt. Fixed here: the line is said once until an eviction frees something again. Which disk the share is read on is the knob's question. The GM's words name "our disk space", and the host's disk is the one that fills, so it is read there.

**Performance work?** yes, for the builders' loop (451 FR-013): the disk kept clear of the 2026-11-22 failure, a full disk that failed every builder's coverage run. It is not engine speed, so the performance checklist does not apply. Its cost is a cold rebuild of an evicted profile, priced above.

### T229 (page session P7's cascade, 2026-11-24: impl-drift's `NOTED, NOT FILED` line and modal-research's OUTSIDE THE CHANGE note filed nothing, as T219 meant, but neither recording command echoed them, so "listed" meant only in the saved reply)

- **Approach**: the echo existed and missed both real forms. `Outside::said` (`rust/gate/crates/owed/src/record/owed/answers/cli.rs`, behind `make claims-checked` and `make record-checked REPLY=`) printed `listed, not filed - <line>` only for a `- <file> | <block> | <finding>` row under an `OUTSIDE THE CHANGE` heading naming no effect, and its reader stopped at the next `#` line. The two replies of P7's cascade, read 2026-11-24 (`/home/agent/.claude/jobs/c6fd72d1/tmp/cascade/impl-5.txt`, `modal-research-reply-1.txt`): impl-drift's note sat under a bare `NOTED, NOT FILED` heading, the heading the agent files give every no-effect note since T219 (impl-drift.md, the five record checks, modal-depiction.md), with no OUTSIDE heading in the reply, so nothing was read; modal-research's sat under `OUTSIDE THE CHANGE` as a prose line with no pipes, which the row form skipped. The reader now walks the reply's lines: a heading `OUTSIDE THE CHANGE` or `NOTED, NOT FILED` (each with or without `#`, bold or a colon) opens a section, which ends at any other `#` heading, a `---` rule, or a prose line after a blank line (a closing paragraph). In an OUTSIDE section a row naming its effect is filed as before; a row naming none, any other bullet, and the prose of the section's first paragraph are listed; a line saying the section is empty (`None.`, `none (every block and note is listed under THE CHANGE).`, never `None of the pages ...`) is no note and still ends its paragraph - the common form, the first line of 13 of the 23 such sections in the saved replies, observed 2026-11-25, method: the first non-blank line after each heading, over `/tmp/*.txt` and the cascade's replies. In a NOTED section every line is listed and none is filed, whatever it names: the check chose not to file it. Each listed note prints one line, `<cmd>: listed, not filed - <file> | <block> | <note>`; a note naming no file and block takes the reply's units instead - the bundle's claim keys for `claims-checked`, the units it answered for `record-checked` - so the line says which unit it was read with. **Where they are kept**: `specs/<active feature>/noted.jsonl`, beside `found.jsonl` and found the same way, one row a note (`check`, `file`, `block`, `note`, `utc`, house-styled as a found row is), a note already kept for the same check, file and block not written again (the tool tells a session to run a reply again after a refused line or a hold); the closing echo line names the file, and `make found-list` ends with how many notes the feature keeps there and its path, so the session listing a feature's findings meets them. Not `found.jsonl`: a row there is open work, which T219 took away from these notes, and `make found-list`'s count of open rows must not grow by them. The task line's "the round's report keeps them" read as this record, since no command keeps a round's report: the claims round's record is `dev/claims-index.json` (claims only) and a record check's is its answer store (units only), neither of which holds a note; `noted.jsonl` is added to `preflight.rs`'s feature records beside `found.jsonl`, as a record the round writes. What it costs: a tracked file per feature that grows by a few lines a round (P7's cascade had two notes, observed 2026-11-24, method: its record's 451 T219 line); priced and not taken, the gitignored `.git` (a later session in another clone would not find it) and the round's bundle directory under `/tmp` (pruned).

### T247 (451 T229's builder in a parallel worktree: the tool target's l7r-gate rebuilt inside a cover run's environment after a gate source edit, and 21 tests of clone-sync-hooks.sh and sync-with-main.sh then failed on 'uncommitted changes' from the default_*.profraw files in their fixture clones, observed 2026-11-25, method: T229's builder's hook-suite run; seen by T235's, T231's and T229's builders)

- **Approach**: `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh` builds a stale tool with the coverage environment cleared, and removes a binary that comes out instrumented anyway rather than run it.
  - **The cause, measured.** A crate's coverage tests run with `rustc/cover.rs`' environment (`cover_env`, then the run's own `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`): `cargo llvm-cov show-env`'s five variables (RUSTFLAGS, LLVM_PROFILE_FILE, CARGO_LLVM_COV, CARGO_LLVM_COV_SHOW_ENV, CARGO_LLVM_COV_TARGET_DIR; its output in this tree, 2026-11-25), with `workspace_only` moving `-C instrument-coverage` out of RUSTFLAGS into a RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER script. A test that calls the launcher inherits it, and the launcher's cargo built the tool in `~/.cache/l7r-cargo-target/<tree>/tool/` under it. The builder's workaround (`env -u RUSTFLAGS -u CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`) does not clear the flag, measured 2026-11-25 (a toy two-crate workspace in the scratchpad, real cargo): a release build under that wrapper alone gave a binary holding `__llvm_prf_cnts` that wrote `default_<id>_0_<pid>.profraw` into the directory it ran in, and the plain rebuild after it (0.05 s, the plain artifacts at their own metadata hash) put back a binary without the section.
  - **The fix: the build's environment.** `build()` runs cargo under `env -u` of every variable show-env sets, every flag channel cargo reads (RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS, RUSTDOCFLAGS, CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTDOCFLAGS), both wrapper channels (RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER, RUSTC_WRAPPER: no config or script of this tree sets one, `grep -rn RUSTC_WRAPPER` 2026-11-25) and CARGO_LLVM_COV_BUILD_DIR. The tool's flags then come from `.cargo/config.toml` (rust-lld, T96), as at every build outside a cover run.
  - **The fix: never left as the tool.** After a successful build and before the `touch` and the build id, a binary holding `__llvm_prf_cnts` is removed with its `build.json`, and the launcher exits 1 with "l7r-gate: <bin> came out instrumented for coverage, so it is removed and nothing runs on it ..." and where to look (a config's rustflags or rustc-wrapper). `L7R_GATE_PRINT_FRESH` names no binary then. The scan runs only at a build: 0.038 s over the 33 MB l7r-gate, measured 2026-11-25 (`time grep -qaF`), per call it would cost that on every one of a suite's hundreds of calls. The detector was checked for false positives: 0 of the 19 tool binaries in every clone's target hold the section (2026-11-25, `grep -caF` over each `tool/` program), so no plain build is refused.
  - **A binary instrumented before this fix**: none exists (the same scan). One that did would run until a source newer than it rebuilds it, which the toy shows comes out plain. Accepted, the GM not asked (no cost to a map or a verdict; the scan is the evidence): the alternative priced was a `<bin>.plain` stamp the launcher requires as fresh - one stat a call, a rebuild of every program in every clone on the first call after landing, and the stamp in three suite fixtures (FT, HT, BT), observed 2026-11-25, method: `grep -n L7R_GATE_TARGET` over the suites - for a state the scan finds nowhere.
  - **The guards' wrapper is left**: `scripts/hooks/l7r-guard.sh` builds the same way into the same target, but nothing runs it inside a cover environment - Claude Code's hooks and `make hooks-test` start it, and no Rust test does (`grep -rn l7r-guard.sh rust/`, 2026-11-25: three mentions in text and a fixture string). Its build also writes `l7r-guard`, not the gate's programs.
