### T246 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** Every leftover a clone keeps has a place and a budget in `make disk-audit`, and goes when its task lands or by the sweep's age; no snapshot a review still reads is taken; the build targets are smaller at no cost in build or test time.
2. **The constraints.** T245's audit and sweep (its rules unchanged: the cache's budget, the proven-dead rule, the low-disk share), T158's same-number rule at a landing, 451 T164's review tree (its snapshot keys the unit). On the live disk dry runs only; real removal only in fixtures under a temp root.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words and the host session's five points, passed on at his request, in request.md's "the per-clone leftovers (451 T246)" section. O: the measurements above. R: none (tooling).
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes: each was measured on this container's disk the day the task was filed, and the dry runs below are the live disk's.
5. **The order.** After T245 (its modules); no dependency on T232.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T246 F=451`. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25 (`scratchpad/trial/t246-redfirst.sh`: this task's code copied to scratch, each rule switched off alone, its test run): the unchanged copy passed, and each of the eight switches failed its test (the table's rows). The crate's suite passed, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/guard`: 521 passed). THE LIVE DISK, dry, measured 2026-11-25 (`make scratch-sweep DRY=1` about 16:50, a build running, its lines summed by reason): 23.6 GB in all - 16.07 GB of scratchpad entries, every one of the finished session `d2dc8c63`, 6.57 GB of dead `.gencache` stores, 0.93 GB of review snapshots without `tree.json` idle past a week, and the task outputs, idle sessions and `/tmp` entries each near 0, the coordinator's scratchpad untouched. The audit's new lines were measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`): `.git/t<N>*` 0.0 of 1.0 GB, handoffs 0.2 of 0.5 GB, review snapshots 1.7 of 1.5 GB OVER and `.gencache` 6.6 of 1.0 GB OVER (each over only until the sweep runs), this project's transcripts 7.2 of 10 GB, and the host's podman line printed. Its last line called the disk under the trigger while it stood above it, measured 2026-11-25 (`make disk-audit`: 29% free against the 20% share), and named the build cache for what are now mostly the age shares; both fixed here.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a: the new knobs (`SCRATCH_SWEEP_SNAPSHOT_DAYS`, the place budgets) are GUESSes labeled at their definitions; `debug` moves with the measurement above.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: about a twentieth of the disk was kept by no rule and freed by none, measured 2026-11-25 (the dry run above: 23.6 GB), and a landed task's handoff scratch outlived it. No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- `make disk-audit` counted every project's transcripts as this container's, measured 2026-11-25 (`du -sch`: 14 GB against 6.8 GB). Effect: the audit overstated this project's share. Fixed here.
- `--scratch-sweep`'s usage line lacked `landed`. Effect: a wrong invocation was not told the mode exists. Fixed here.
- `make disk-audit`'s last line (the eviction's dry run) said "disk under" the share whatever the disk's free share. Effect: the audit told its reader the disk was under the trigger when it was not (measured 2026-11-25, `make disk-audit`, at 29% free). Fixed here.

**Performance work?** yes (451 FR-013, the builders' loop): `debug = 0` makes every dev, test and coverage target smaller at the same build and test times (measured 2026-11-25, above). It is not engine speed, so no performance checklist applies.

### T233 (`docs/gm-rulings.md`, section 'NOT a ruling', 2026-11-24: 0006's comment calling dry plots against the canal a ruling of his was never his; the audit of that day found 74 of 180 such comments with no recorded words behind them)

- **Approach**: a static text check, `l7r-gate check gm-attributions` (`rust/gate/crates/checks/src/checks/gm_attributions.rs`), run in `make quick` (`_quick`, after partial-citations) and as a row of the push's checks (`cohort/src/push.rs`, `CHECKS` 23 -> 24), registered in `scripts/tool-registry.json`.
  - **What it reads.** Every HTML comment of `research/questions/*.html`, and every CANON claim line (` - CANON`) in the Rust under `rust/` (the tooling trees `gate`, `guard`, `browser`, `embed` and `target` left out, as `claims::units::walked` leaves them; `rust/parked` kept in, its 3 claims come back when it is unparked) and in the two procedure docs (`docs/buildings.md`, `docs/building-programs.md`, `claims::units::PROCEDURES`). A claim is one line by the claims grammar, so a line scan reads it whole; the check does not build on the claims crate.
  - **What names a ruling.** The task's three forms, case-insensitive: "the GM's ruling|catch|word|decision" (plural too), "the GM ruled", "GM <date>", the date also after a comma ("the GM, 2026-08", 109 of the comments). It also matches the audit's near-twins ("the GM's rule|doctrine|correction"), which the brief puts in the baseline.
  - **What backs it.** A path in the same comment or line that exists in the tree: `specs/<NNN-slug>/request.md` (or `gm-request.md`, which holds his request verbatim: 152's opens "The GM's request, verbatim"; the audit counted it as his words), `docs/gm-rulings.md`, or `specs/<NNN-slug>/gm-review.jsonl` (the file `make gm-reviewed` writes its `gm_words` rows to, `reviews::gm_review`). A bare "request.md" or "feature 280" is no pointer. A path that does not exist is named in the refusal.
  - **What is not checked: that the record holds those words.** The comments paraphrase rather than quote, so matching their words against the record would refuse most correct pointers. The cost is that a pointer to the wrong record passes, and whoever builds on the comment reads the record it names. A verbatim-quote rule was priced and turned down, because it would refuse most correct pointers. His words for this task (request.md, "2026-11-24: a ruling attributed to the GM names his recorded words") say what was wrong, not how a tool checks it. The sentence "checked against his recorded words before anything is built on it" is the session's in `docs/gm-rulings.md`, and it puts the reading on whoever builds; the check makes sure there is a record to read. The builder chose the pointer's existence under his 2026-10-25 words, quoted in the same request.md section: "we can just do whatever is algorithmically easier".
  - **The baseline, `dev/gm-attribution-baseline.jsonl`.** Every attribution with no pointer at landing, one JSON line each (`file`, `key`, `kind`, `says`, `excerpt`). The key is the first 16 hex of the sha256 of its whitespace-normalized text, not its line, so an edit elsewhere on the page leaves it listed and an edit of its own text owes its pointer. Three refusals keep the list shrinking:
    - an attribution not listed;
    - an entry no longer found, with the fix `scripts/gates/l7r-gate.sh check gm-attributions --prune`, which only drops entries;
    - an entry the merge base's copy lacks.
    `--seed` writes the list only where none exists, so deleting it and seeding again is refused at the push by the third rule.
  - **Why a check and not a guard on Edit.** A check is the easier and cheaper route. It is one module beside `partial_citations.rs`, about 0.5 s per run with the launcher, partial-citations 0.35 s, measured 2026-11-25 (`time` on each check over this tree). It also sees a page however it was written: a page session's `make` targets, a Write, or a Bash. An Edit guard would see only the Edit and Write tools, needs a hooks-test suite, and runs on every edit.
  - **The baseline's counts**, 2026-11-25. Method: `check gm-attributions --seed` at this worktree's HEAD (c9d2cac85c), counted with `jq`/python over the file, then `--prune` after the three parked claims below were given their pointers.
    - 351 entries: 341 page comments on 172 pages, and 10 CANON claims (`docs/buildings.md` 4, `docs/building-programs.md` 1, `rust/phases` 3, `rust/mode_a` 2), observed 2026-11-25, method: the file counted by kind and file. 13 claims were seeded. The 3 in `rust/parked`, which no claims round reads, are fixed here, because each one's words are in a request.md: `homesteads/gap_ways.rs` and `homesteads/place.rs` in `specs/318-grow-outward-no-restart/request.md` (lines 61 and 47), and `law/meet.rs` in `specs/417-all-seeds-pass/request.md` (line 42).
    - Of the comments, 176 carry the four words. That is the audit's 180, less the 3 that already cite a request.md path (0029, 0094, 0246) and the edits since c693e6ddcb, among them 0006's disowned comment, removed by 9207459906. The 176 include the audit's 74 unbacked. They also include its BACKED rows, which name no record by path ("269 B32", "feature 280") and so are no pointer to the check.
    - The other 165 comments are the near-twins: "GM, <date>" 109, "GM <date>" 29, "the GM's rule" 15, "the GM ruled" 5, "doctrine" 5, "correction" 5. These are more than the audit's "about 60", which did not count the comma form.
  - **Not fixed here: the 341 page comments** (observed 2026-11-25, method: the baseline counted by kind). Giving each its pointer, or saying whose rule it is, is an edit of a research page. Page edits run as page sessions under the research switch, which his words of 2026-11-25 deferred (request.md, quoted in T233's section; `dev/switches.json`). T233's task line asks for the baseline "shrinking as pages are edited".
  - **Not fixed here: the 10 walked claims** (observed 2026-11-25, method: the baseline counted by kind). A pointer is found for some of them, but each of the others needs either a relabel from CANON to what backs it, or a GM question. A relabel is a MISLABELED for the claims round to judge (impl-drift), and this builder's brief forbids dispatching it (`scripts/container/builder-brief.md`, 451 T237). Four of them share their rule with a baseline page comment: the tub (0100), true size (0039), the dedication (0222) and the reed fringe (0058). Their fix and the page's must agree.

| the baseline lists, prunes and only shrinks | `the_baseline_lists_the_old_ones_and_only_shrinks`, `an_entry_the_merge_base_lacks_is_refused` | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| on the real tree | 0006's remaining entry ("the GM's catch, 2026-07", key acf9608739fd2b6b) dropped from the baseline: refused, `0006-dry-fields-and-their-crops-hatake.drawing.html:38`, rc 1; restored: green, 2026-11-25 | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T233 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A research page's comment or a CANON claim that calls something the GM's ruling names where his words are recorded. A new one without a pointer is refused. The ones written before are listed and can only go down.
2. **The constraints.** `docs/gm-rulings.md` "NOT a ruling" (a comment naming his ruling is checked against his recorded words before anything is built on it). The research switch deferred (`dev/switches.json`), so no page is edited. The root CLAUDE.md: tips live in error output (each refusal prints its fix), and new Rust owes 100% line coverage.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM 2026-11-24 in `docs/gm-rulings.md` and `specs/449-rust-codebase/request.md:212`. R: the audit (`/home/agent/.claude/jobs/c6fd72d1/tmp/gm-attributions-audit.md`). O: the seed's counts and the real-tree fires-proof above, 2026-11-25.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. The four-word scan over `research/questions` finds 179 comments on 113 pages (case-insensitive) against the audit's 180 on 112, measured 2026-11-25 with the same comment regex at this HEAD, 40 commits to the pages after the audit's.
5. **The order.** No dependency. T246, built beside it, touches none of its files.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T233 F=451`. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** The 4 tests red with the check emptied and green with it, and the real tree green with the baseline and red with one of its entries dropped, measured 2026-11-25 (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/gate/crates/checks`, then the check over this tree).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** No map changes. The finding: attributions with no recorded words became rules that code enforced (0006 and `field/dry.rs`). Observed 2026-11-24, method: the audit's full table.

**Found and left?**
- The baseline's 341 page comments (observed 2026-11-25, method: the baseline counted by kind) still name a ruling of the GM's with no pointer to his words. Any one of them can carry a rule the GM never made, as 0006's did into the dry-field stage. Not fixed here: a research page's edit waits for the research switch to reopen (his words of 2026-11-25, request.md). Filed as T<n> by the coordinating session (a builder in a parallel worktree may not `make task-add`), titled "the gm-attributions baseline's page comments: each points at the GM's recorded words or says whose rule it is, the audit's 74 unbacked first (451 T233)"; the first page work to land once the research switch reopens.
- The baseline's 10 walked CANON claims (observed 2026-11-25, method: the baseline counted by kind) carry the same risk in the engine and the procedure docs. Not fixed here: a relabel is the claims round's to judge. Filed as T<n> by the coordinating session, titled "the gm-attributions baseline's 10 CANON claims: each points at the GM's recorded words, or is relabeled to what backs it through the claims round (451 T233)"; lands beside the first item's pages it shares (0039, 0058, 0100, 0222), the others first.

**Performance work?** no: a new check; nothing runs faster.

### T151 (make ledger-owed traced no check-wave unit to the session that ran it: 35 impl-drift passes of 449 T249's re-check stayed owed after the session's write and refused every landing)

- **Approach**: measured first, then the trace and the reply of a Workflow agent taught to `reviews`' `ledger_passes/rows.rs`:
  - HOW A PASS IS TIED TO A SESSION, measured 2026-11-22 (reading `ledger_passes.rs`, `rows.rs`, `settle.rs`, `trace.rs` and the
    guard's `ledger/cost.rs`): `make ledger-owed WRITE=` passes `--session $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and `write_owed` keeps a pass
    where `rows::session_of` names that session - the agent's transcript's parent's parent. The transcript is found by
    `cost::transcript`, which lists `<project>/<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl` only. A check-wave unit's transcript sits at
    `<session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-<id>.jsonl`, measured 2026-11-22 (`ls` of the session's directory: 13 runs under
    `subagents/workflows/wf_*`), so it was never found: `session_of` gave "", and the pass was "not traced to it". Had it been found,
    its parent's parent is `workflows`, not the session.
  - WHERE A UNIT'S REPLY STANDS, measured 2026-11-22 (`tail` of a unit's transcript and its run's `journal.jsonl`): the transcript
    ends in the StructuredOutput call's tool result, no text; the run's `journal.jsonl` holds one `{"type":"result","agentId":...,
    "result":{label, verdict, text}}` line per unit, `text` the unit's reply and `label` its bundle's name (`claims-rust-...`, the
    same name as the `/tmp/l7r-check/<name>/` its prompt reads, checked on one unit's first user message).
  - THE FIX (`rows.rs`): `wave_transcript` finds `<project>/<session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/agent-<id>.jsonl`; `session_of`
    names a hand-dispatched agent's session as before and a wave unit's as the directory above `subagents/workflows/<run>/`;
    `filled_row` takes a wave unit's reply and place from its run's journal (`journal_reply`: the last result line naming the agent,
    its `text` and `label`, or the result itself where it is text), and fills the same cells a hand-dispatched pass gets - the
    verdict by `verdict_of` on the reply, its first line, `nothing` or `judgment`, the acted-on cell from `WRITE=`.
  - THE VERDICT CELL, a decision, labeled (parity): read from the reply as a hand-dispatched pass's is, not from the journal's
    `verdict` field, so an all-IN-STEP impl-drift reply reads `findings` as the session's hand-dispatched impl-drift rows already do.
  - THE COST CELLS, a decision, labeled (an accepted limitation): the costing (`settle::settled`, through `cost::subagent_files`) is
    left looking where it looked, so a wave pass keeps its logged cells. Cost: a wave unit's cells are the hook's, not recomputed from
    its finished transcript (how far they differ was not measured). The alternative priced: teaching the costing the wave directory
    recomputes the cells of the ~342 wave passes already answered (377 in the log, 35 owed, measured 2026-11-22 by `grep -c` of the
    clone's `check-passes.jsonl`), and a row answers a pass by its cost cells, so those rows would answer nothing and the passes
    would be owed again. Chosen by the T151 builder.
  - THE WRITE, measured 2026-11-22 (`make ledger-owed WRITE=` in the clone, the new binary): 41 rows written for c6fd72d1 - the 35
    impl-drift units, each with its bundle's label and its reply's first line, and 6 passes launched after the brief (a
    building-review, a glyph-check and a size-audit of 449 T265, two escalation-checks, one spec-fidelity `ARBITER_OK` dispatch); 40
    plan reviews refused as their landings' own (451 T105). `WRITE=` was the session's earlier rows' full text, which begins with the
    brief's ("each pass's verdict recorded by its tool: make claims-checked into dev/claims-index.json") and names where the other
    checks' verdicts are recorded, so the 6 later rows' acted-on cells are true. After, `make ledger-owed` lists 40 passes, every
    one a MODE 4 plan review, measured 2026-11-22 (its listing, `grep -vc "MODE 4"` = 0).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### T248 (451 T227's builder, 2026-11-25: record-format's 2026-11-24 rounds on 0097 spanned two `origin/main` batches, and the batch rule restarts a unit's count on any move of `origin/main`, so with several sessions landing the cap seldom fires)

- **Approach**: The batch rule lives in `new_cause` (`rust/guard/shared/src/checks/rounds.rs`), which `cap_refusal` asks before it holds a repeat round. It is narrowed. A later batch restarts the count only where the subject itself moved upstream, never through the landing of the round's own edits.
  - **The ruling it changes.** c5db336fd3 (2026-10-12, feature 374 batch 11) rests on the round arbiter's `continue` on `round:modal-depiction|modal:hamlet/woodland-commons@3` (`specs/374-match-the-research-continued/arbiter.jsonl`). Rounds 1 and 2 had converged; a new, material cause then arrived, a 0077 bullet added in batch 9. The arbiter asked that a fresh count start "when a later batch owes the unit for a page change that no earlier counted round saw". c5db336fd3 built that as "a later batch, another `origin/main`", because the first build (by fingerprint) restarted on every edit and the cap never tripped.
  - **What was measured, 2026-11-25** (method: the coordinating clone's `.git/checks-open.json` dispatch times against its `origin/main` reflog and `git diff --name-only` of each move over `research/questions/0097-*`). Rounds 1 and 2 ran at 05:15 and 05:25Z, under `origin/main` ab26e3eebd. Ten moves followed before 17:15Z. One of them, c7dac385dd at 06:02Z, changed three 0097 files, measured 2026-11-25 (`git show --stat 7fc9f06512`): it was this clone's push of its own 7fc9f06512, the round's own edits. The other nine changed no 0097 file. The would-be next round came after the 18:08Z fetch (39dcee3d4a, 36 commits of features 453 and 454, measured 2026-11-25 with `git log f7c105b4a0..39dcee3d4a`), which also changed no 0097 file. So the page moved between the batches only by the round's own landing, and every restart was from moves elsewhere.
  - **Telling our landing from another session's.** The reflog of `refs/remotes/origin/main` lives in the clone's common git directory, so every worktree of the clone (the land, review and builder worktrees) writes to it. This clone's landing is an `update by push` entry. Another session's work arrives by a fetch or a pull entry. Measured 2026-11-25 on the coordinating clone's last 150 entries (21 to 25 November): 147 pushes and 3 fetches. Every commit in a push step was made in this clone (in a HEAD, branch or worktree reflog as a commit, merge or revert), except the `land-tooling` commits made in the land worktree, which are this session's too. HEAD-reflog authorship was tried first and rejected: f7c105b4a0 (land-tooling) is in no reflog, and a local merge or revert is not a `commit:` line.
  - **The rule as built.** `new_cause` holds only when three things are true: the unit's last counted round was under another `origin/main`; no round of the subject is open; and `moved_upstream` says the subject moved. `moved_upstream` walks the origin/main reflog from the last entry that reached the stored batch. A non-push entry whose `git diff --name-only old new` names a file of the subject (`subject_of_path`) moves it. Each failure direction is chosen. Where the reflog does not reach the stored batch (expired, or no tracking log), any change of the subject between the two batches moves it, whoever made it. That keeps the arbiter's intent where authorship cannot be read. A stored batch git cannot read (or a diff git refuses) moves nothing. The cap then holds and the round arbiter rules: the tripwire fails toward its ruling, not past it. An unrecognized reflog message counts as another session's.
  - **How the narrower rule keeps the ruling's intent.** The ruling's case is a later page change that no counted round saw, which owes a fresh count. Another session's change to the subject is still that case, and it still starts fresh. What no longer restarts is a batch whose only change to the subject is the round's own edits landing, which c5db336fd3 itself excluded ("never on a batch's own edits"), or a batch with no change to the subject at all. **The cost, accepted:** the ruling's own trigger was the session's own later change, to a page the pop-up reads (0077) and not the pop-up's file. A cause like that now trips the cap, and one `make arbiter-bundle` ruling stands where the restart stood. The root CLAUDE.md's tripwire ("a check's third round on one subject") is exactly that ruling. The alternative priced was counting the pages a unit reads as its subject. It was not built: the task's words are "the subject itself", and a page a pop-up reads moving owes the pop-up a triage (`make modal-triage`), not a fresh count. Chosen by this builder under the task's text; the spec-fidelity review rules.
  - **The split.** `rounds.rs` passed the 1,000-line bar with the new rule (1,029 lines, measured 2026-11-25 by `check file-scale`), so the cap's code moved unchanged into `rounds/cap.rs`: `home_dir`, `batch_of` (re-exported), `new_cause`, `moved_upstream`, `moved_since_answer`, `record_store`, `quoted`, `answered` and `cap_refusal`. Measured 2026-11-25 (`wc -l`): `rounds.rs` is now 843 lines and `cap.rs` 198.
  - **Other readers.** None: `round_batch`, `new_cause` and "later batch" appear in no gate crate, doc or agent file (grep of `rust`, `docs`, `.claude/agents`, `scripts`, 2026-11-25).

### T252 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** `tests/hooks/test-closing-checks.sh` gives one verdict for one code, however loaded the machine: a row its output shows is a row it finds.
2. **The constraints.** The task's text: find the race or shared read, reproduce it red on a forced interleaving, make it deterministic, say what was shared. The suite keeps `set -uo pipefail`.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task line of tasks.md (T252). O: the measurements of item 4.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. WHAT WAS SHARED: nothing on disk - every path the suite's case 1 reads (the stub make, its events, `CLOSING_CHECKS_DIR`, the gate stub) is under the suite's own `mktemp -d`, measured 2026-11-25 (reading the suite and `scripts/gates/closing-checks.sh`), and the run id's directory is made with a plain `mkdir`, so the brief's candidates (a fixed /tmp path, the run directory under the common .git, a timestamp collision, the stamp file) were ruled out by reading `scripts/gates/closing-checks.sh` and the suite. What two side-by-side runs share is the CPU. THE RACE: the check is `printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^  static +GREEN ...'` under pipefail. Bash writes the printf builtin's stdout a line at a time (6 write calls for an 8-line text, measured 2026-11-25 (`/proc/<pid>/io`'s `syscw` read before and after one printf into a pipe)); grep -q exits at its first match; a printf still writing when grep has exited dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns 141, and the check reports FAIL with `$OUT`, which shows the row, beside it. The static row is the first row, so it has the most text behind it - the row that failed. Unloaded, 0 of 2,000 runs on a 461-byte copy of case 1's output failed; pinned to one CPU 1 of 3,000 did, measured 2026-11-25 (a bash loop of the check's own pipeline, the second under `taskset -c 0`). The forced interleaving: the row first, then 1.3 MB (`seq 200000`), more than a pipe holds, so the writer is always still writing at grep's exit: the old form 50 of 50 red, its negation (`! printf | grep -q`) a false pass 50 of 50, the here-string form 0 of 50 red, measured 2026-11-25 (one bash loop of 50 over each form).
5. **The order.** No dependency.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T252 F=451`. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.

After `seen` replaced the 47 pipes (`$OUT`, `$A`, `$B`; the forcing line keeps the old form on purpose), 64 passed, 0 failed.

### T253 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A guard suite or a gate script gives one verdict for one text, however loaded the machine: a line its text holds is a line its grep finds, and a negated check never passes on a line that is there.
2. **The constraints.** The task's text: recount the pattern across `tests/hooks/` and outside it (`tests/`, `scripts/`) in every early-exit form, fix every one with one shared helper, move T252's self-check to where every suite is run (`make hooks-test`), red-first by the forced race on one representative of each form, and answer whether T139's no-poll flake is this race. The suites keep their `set` lines.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task line of tasks.md (T253) and its brief. O: the measurements of items 4 and 9.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. THE DECISIONS:
   - T253-D1 THE SCOPE IS EVERY SHELL FILE, PIPEFAIL OR NOT: every tracked file under `tests/` and `scripts/` that ends `.sh` or opens with a sh or bash shebang (149, measured 2026-11-25, `git ls-files`). A sourced file runs under its caller's pipefail without saying so (`scripts/hooks/lib/failed-open-log.sh:121`, sourced by `l7r-guard.sh`, which sets it), and a suite that gains pipefail later would arm the race silently; the 4 files without it hold 24 of the sites, measured 2026-11-25 (a grep of the refused form over those files), which change form at no cost.
   - T253-D2 THE REFUSED FORM: a pipe into `grep` with an early-exit flag (`-q`, `-l`, `-m`, or `--quiet`, `--silent`, `--max-count`, `--files-with-matches`), whatever the writer - the flag is what exits early, and its status is the point of the call. `head`, `sed q` and `awk exit` readers are not refused: the 149 files hold 31 `| head` pipes, none whose status is read, and no pipe into a `sed` that quits nor an `awk` that exits, measured 2026-11-25 (a grep over the 149 files of `| head`, of `| sed` with a `q` command - `1q`, `/q`, `;q`, a bare `q` - and of `| awk` with `exit`, then of the head lines an `&&`, `||`, `if` or `set -e` would read), so no verdict moves (not a defect, constitution XIV).
   - T253-D3 THE FIX, BY FORM: a variable printed into grep (`printf '%s' "$V"`, `echo "$V"`) becomes `seen V <args>`; a command or a list of arguments into grep is captured first, `o=$(cmd) && seen o <args>`, the `&&` keeping what pipefail demanded of the writer (its success) on 14 lines (finished-run 9, make-only, measure, no-poll, set-down, `install-chromium.sh`), measured 2026-11-25 (the diff). Where the writer's status is dropped, a writer that fails gives empty text, which answers as the failed pipe did - no match, and a negated check true - so no verdict moves; a writer that prints the line and then fails would now match where pipefail answered no, and the one writer that can (`grep -rl`, exit 2 after its matches on a file it cannot read) now counts the matches it printed, the right answer, while `tr`, `tail`, `git log`, `head`, `ls`, `git diff` and `jq` print nothing to stdout on the failures these sites meet (a missing file, an empty repository, text that is not JSON), measured 2026-11-25 (reading each site): 14 lines under pipefail (`tr` of a process's cmdline 3, `tail` and `git log` 3, `head` 1, `ls` 3 as `[ -n "$(ls ...)" ]`, `grep -rl | xargs grep -l` 1, `review-gate.sh` 2 and `failed-open-log.sh` 1 through `< <(...)`) and the 10 command lines (12 pipes) of `test-pair-hooks.sh`, a suite without pipefail, whose pipe status was grep's alone, measured 2026-11-25 (the diff); `scripts/` cannot source `tests/`, so a script greps `<<< "$x"` inline. `seen` is defined once, in `tests/hooks/seen.sh`, and sourced by each suite that greps; T252's own definition in `test-closing-checks.sh` moves there. A here-string adds a newline: no converted suite site greps with `-v` or `-c`, measured 2026-11-25 (the flags of every `seen` call in the diff); of the scripts, `review-gate.sh`'s `grep -qv '^specs/' <<< ""` replaced a `printf '%s\n'` that wrote the same newline, and its `grep -qv '^A$'` reads `< <(...)`, which adds none, so empty text still answers no line.
   - T253-D4 THE CHECK: `l7r-gate check pipe-race --root <tree>` (Rust, `rust/gate/crates/checks/src/checks/pipe_race.rs`), run in `make hooks-test`'s unconditional tail beside `check rust-tooling` (a suite is skipped when its key is unchanged; the tail runs at every hooks-test, measured 2026-11-25 (reading the recipe)), names each line with its fix and exits 1. A line continued with a trailing `|` is read with the next. The escape is a `# pipe-ok: <reason>` comment on the line, of two words or more, for text that is never run as a pipe (a command a suite feeds a guard as payload, the forcing line). T252's self-grep in `test-closing-checks.sh` goes, the check doing its job over all 149 files measured 2026-11-25 (`git ls-files`); its section 0 stays.
   - T253-D5 RED FIRST BY THE FORCED RACE, per form: the matching line, then 1.3 MB (`seq 200000`), more than a pipe holds, so the writer is always still writing at grep's exit, measured 2026-11-25 (the loop below). Of 50 runs each, measured 2026-11-25 (a bash loop under `set -uo pipefail`): `printf '%s' "$V" | grep -q` red 50, `echo "$V" | grep -q` red 50, `printf '%s\n' "$@" | grep -qx` red 50, a command `| grep -q` red 50, the negated printf form a false pass 50; `seen V -q` red 0, `o=$(cmd) && seen o -q` red 0. The check's tests run each form through bash once on the forced text.

### T256 (the parallel trials, 2026-11-25: every carry-over of a worktree's task into the session clone conflicted on specs/451-time-retro-and-efficiency/plan-review.json and was merged by hand as JSON, both sides' entries kept)

- **Approach**: a git merge driver for `specs/*/plan-review.json`, registered in `.gitattributes` (`merge=plan-review`) and defined in the clone's git config by `scripts/sync-with-main.sh`'s `ensure_git_config` on every sync-in, runs `l7r-gate plan merge-record %O %A %B`: a three-way merge of the record's JSON that keeps both sides' entries, written through the recorder's own `pretty`. Measured 2026-11-25 (a scratch repo holding the real record, two branches each adding a task's verdict, `git cherry-pick`).

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the merge driver | the merge's tests: two sides each adding a task's verdict merge with both kept; a cherry-pick through the registered driver merges clean where git's text merge left 3 conflict hunks (measured 2026-11-25) | n/a: no engine code | none | n/a |

### T256 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** Two builders in two worktrees each record their task's plan review; carrying both tasks into the session clone (a cherry-pick or a merge) takes both verdicts with no hand merge, and every reader of `plan-review.json` reads it as before.
2. **The constraints.** The task line (tasks.md T256): each task's verdicts in their own file, or the record merged by a git merge driver; `make plan-verdict` and every reader unchanged in what they read; red-first on two branches each adding a task's verdict, then merging; before the first port batch at three builders.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task line and its brief (the cheaper sound route, measured). O: the measurements of item 4 and item 9.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. THE DECISIONS:
   - T256-D1 THE ROUTE IS THE MERGE DRIVER: it touches 4 files where per-task files touch about 39, measured 2026-11-25 (a grep of `plan-review.json` and the plan crate's `RECORD` over `rust/` and `scripts/`): per-task files move 10 reading files outside the plan crate (the arbiter's bundle, research pointers, the landing's ready check, the feature report, stale terms, the ledger's plan rows, the review-round guard, `plan-gate.sh`, `land-alone.sh` with 6 sites) and 5 plan-crate modules, about 24 test files that write the record, and a migration of 173 records; and `land/ready.rs` and `land-alone.sh` are the push refusal the T254 builder is editing in parallel. Per-task files would still leave the plan's shared blocks (`## Summary`, `## Decisions`) and the `block_reviews` log in one file, so their merges would still conflict. The driver is a new module and its tests, its verb in `plan.rs`, a `.gitattributes` line and `ensure_git_config`'s registration, and no reader changes.
   - T256-D2 THE MERGE IS THREE-WAY AND AN ENTRY IS WHOLE: the record's top level and its `blocks` and `tasks` maps are merged key by key against the base. A key one side changed and the other left is that side's. A key both sides removed, or only one side removed while the other left it, is removed. A key one side removed and the other changed keeps the changed entry. An entry (a block's or a task's verdict) is never merged field by field: a mix of one side's digest and the other's verdict could read CLEAR on a text nobody cleared. Where both sides changed one key to different entries, the one with the later `reviewed` day wins, and on a tie the incoming side's (`%B`). Each entry carries its own digest, so a wrong pick leaves a block owed a review again and never a false CLEAR: the gate compares the digest with the merged plan's text.
   - T256-D3 `block_reviews` KEEPS EVERY ROW: it is an append-only log (no writer removes a row, measured 2026-11-25, a read of `record.rs`, `history.rs` and `task.rs`). The merge is our side's rows, then each of the incoming side's rows that the base does not hold and our side does not already hold. The review-round guard counts a task's trailing non-CLEAR rows (`review_round_hooks.rs`'s `rev().take_while`), so each side's rows keep their order.
   - T256-D4 REGISTRATION IS TOOLING: a merge driver's command is local git config, which no clone carries. `ensure_git_config` sets `merge.plan-review.driver` on the session clone (its worktrees share the clone's config) at every sync-in, idempotently, saying so the first time. The command runs the gate with `L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1`: mid-pick, a Rust source may hold conflict markers, and a rebuild then would fail the merge; the stale binary merges as well as a fresh one. Unregistered, or with a binary older than the verb, git falls back to its text merge: today's conflict, no worse.
   - T256-D5 A RECORD THAT DOES NOT PARSE IS LEFT TO THE HAND MERGE: a side that is not JSON fails the merge with our side untouched, and the message names the file and says to merge it by hand as JSON, both sides' entries kept.
5. **The order.** Beside T257 (same builder); before the first port batch at three builders; T254's carry-over into the session clone is the first pick it serves, so the clone's sync-in must have run first.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T256`. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.** RED FIRST, measured 2026-11-25 (a scratch repo with the real 2.8 MB record as base, branches `a` and `b` each adding a task's entry, a block's entry and a `block_reviews` row, `git cherry-pick b` onto `a`): git's text merge left the file unmerged with 3 conflict hunks, one per map and one in the log. With the driver registered and the pick run from a linked worktree of that repo, measured 2026-11-25: the pick merged clean, both tasks', both blocks' and both rows kept (303 rows to 305), and the picked commit's diff is its own 21 lines, the record's form unchanged. `tests/hooks/test-sync-with-main.sh` case Z2 pins it: sync-in defines the driver once, and a pick of another task's verdict in the fixture clone merges clean with both kept. The merge's unit tests (`plan/merge/tests.rs`) cover each rule of D2, D3 and D5.
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** The finding: every carry-over of a worktree's task stopped on a conflict that a session merged by hand. No map changes.

**Found and left?** none.

**Performance work?** no: it removes a hand step from the builders' loop, and runs only at a merge.

### T254 (the parallel trials of 2026-11-25, `specs/449-rust-codebase/port-talk-agenda.md` item 1: one `active-task` mark in the shared .git, a second worktree's start overwrote the first's, and a push of one task was refused while the other was started)

- **Approach**: A mark per task; this tree's started task holds its push as before, another tree's only by the files the push carries.
  - **The marks** (`rust/guard/shared/src/speckit/marks.rs`). `make task-start` writes `<git common dir>/task-marks/<feature>/<task>.json`: feature, task, a bundle's `tasks`, the tree that started it, and the time. No start overwrites another task's mark. A tree's own task (`marks::of_tree`) is the newest mark that tree wrote. The main worktree also reads the old one-mark file, `active-task`, as its oldest mark, so a start made before this change still counts. That tree's next start removes the old file. A mark is removed when its task lands (`make land`'s sweep, `--scratch-sweep landed`) or when its feature is set down in its own tree (`marks::clear`). Another tree's marks stay. A ticked task's mark that is left behind holds nothing, because every reader asks for an open box. Each `task-starts.jsonl` row now names its tree too.
  - **The hold** (`speckit::holding_with`, which the push, `make land` and the CI merge ask). A started task of the feature holds only while its box is open (or an open box is nested under it) and the landing does not tick it. A task THIS tree started (its mark names this tree, or names none, so the hold fails closed) then holds the push whatever the push carries, as feature 405 T32's D4 had it, with its old message ("the active task (make task-start), open"). A task ANOTHER tree started holds it only where, as well, the push's delta carries one of its edits. "Carries an edit" is 451 T101's rule, moved to `speckit/touch.rs` so the push and `land/ready.rs` share one reader: a delta file, other than the feature's sectioned files and the review ledger, holds a write of the task's on the event log, made after the file last landed and before the delta's last commit of it. A landing that rules its tasks ready (`L7R_LAND_READY`) is still not held. If a mark this tree reads is not an object, the hold fails closed, as before.
  - **The prefix fault, fixed here.** T101's rule stripped only the clone's path from an edit line, so every edit a worktree's builder made was passed over. The edit lines are now read against every tree: the worktrees git lists, the trees the marks and starts name, and the clone, longest first. A worktree nested inside the tree is read as its own.
  - **The readers, by what they ask.**
    - Changed to this tree's mark (`marks::of_tree`): `speckit::active_task`, and through it the reviews' declared placement (`reviews/owed/declared.rs`); and the plan crate's `task::active_task`, and through it decide's refusal, the approach tripwire (`approach.rs`) and the review-round guard's `plan door active-task`.
    - Changed to read a tree's own starts, a row naming another tree passed over and a row naming none read as before: the event log's booking of a line by the task in force (`event_log_hooks/filed.rs::starts`), the context cap's in-force fallback (`context_cap_hooks.rs`), and the task `make land-tooling`'s log line names (`rust/gate/crates/core/src/logs.rs::land_tooling`, its tree git's top of the directory it runs in; outside a repository every row, as before).
    - Changed to every mark: the stall check (`set_down_hooks/stalls.rs`) and the hold.
    - Changed in what it removes: `make set-down` (`set_down.rs` through `marks::clear`) and the landed sweep (`scratch_sweep_hooks/disk.rs`).
    - Already read the task from their own argument or a per-task row, so unchanged: `land/ready.rs`'s `started_tasks`, `builder_stop_hooks::started_and_open`, `static_runs_hooks` (the task its filing names), `closing-checks.sh` (`CLOSING_TASK`), `wording.rs`, the Makefile's landed sweep, `check_bundle_hooks/own.rs` (the check's own task since 449 T258), `approach.rs::in_flight` (every in-flight task of the feature, the GM's 2026-10-21 rule), and the ledger's `whose.rs`.
    - Read clone-wide on purpose, unchanged: the Stop hook's started features and idle check (`set_down_hooks.rs::started`, `idle.rs`), which serve the coordinating session over every tree; `make events-refile` (`every_start`, its reading kept as it was); and the measure crates' reports (`task_time`, `where_time`, `feature_report`).

### T255 (the parallel trials of 2026-11-25: builders in two worktrees each ran `make task-add` and filed T247, then T248, twice; renumbered by hand)

- **Approach**: `make task-add` (`rust/gate/crates/task/src/task_add.rs`) already held a filing lock per feature in the git common directory (451 T84), which every worktree shares. What clashed was the number: `next_id` read only its own tree's tasks.md, tasks-done.md, plan.md and plan-done.md. The number is now one past the highest id of these sources: those files in this tree; the same files on `main` and on `origin/main` as last fetched (`git show <ref>:./<file>`, with no fetch under the lock); and the reservation file `<git common dir>/task-ids.txt`, which holds one `<feature> T<n>` line per id handed out. The id is written to the reservation file under the lock, before the box goes in. A filing that `make quick` withdraws gives its id back, so the next filing takes that id, as before. A tree that git does not know has no other worktree, and keeps no reservation.

### T259 (the GM 2026-11-25, `specs/449-rust-codebase/port-talk-agenda.md` item 13 and its "Order" paragraph: "should we move that item up to or near the front, so it can apply to all of the other optimizations we're building at the moment?")

- **Approach**: a register of one Markdown file per entry under `dev/audits/`, a lister, and a check at `make static` and the push that refuses a delta adding a mechanism no entry names.
  - **The register** (`dev/audits/<slug>.md`). Each entry opens with a front matter of `key: value` lines between `---` lines: `kind` (`adopted`, a mechanism in force, or `declined`, an option weighed and not built, whose falsifier is what would reopen it - T259-D11), `title`, `for` (what it is for, in outcomes), `measured` (the date of the measurement that justified it, or `unmeasured`, which then names its first audit in `first-audit:`), `measurement` (the figures, with their method), `command` (what reproduces it), `falsifier`, `threshold`, `cost` (its cost source in `make task-time`), `last-audited` (a date, or `never`), `cadence-days`, and any number of `covers:` lines naming the mechanisms it answers for. The reasoning is the prose below. Markdown, not JSON: an entry is mostly prose the GM reads, and the front matter is split line by line on its first colon by `parse` (about thirty lines, observed 2026-11-26, method: the function as written), so no new parser or dependency enters the crate (JSON would hold the reasoning as escaped strings).
  - **`make audits`** (`l7r-gate check audit-register --list`): every entry, the never-audited first, then the overdue by how far, then by the day each falls due; each with its `[kind]`, title, file, last audit, cadence, measured date, falsifier and threshold, and a MALFORMED line for any field wrong; then a BACKFILL section: the five detectors run over the whole tree against git's empty tree, less the mechanisms the entries' `covers:` lines name - the mechanisms in force that no entry answers for yet (T260's list).
  - **The check** (`rust/gate/crates/checks/src/checks/audit_register.rs`, its detection `audit_register/detect.rs`; `l7r-gate check audit-register --delta ROOT`, in `make static` after the spec lint and in the push's checks table after it, each with its self-test). It refuses when any entry is malformed (a field of the eleven missing or empty, a `kind` other than `adopted` or `declined`, a date or cadence that does not read, `unmeasured` without `first-audit`), or when the delta against the merge base (`merge-base HEAD origin/main`, HEAD where there is none; the working tree's dirty and untracked files counted, as the push's own delta counts them) adds one of these five with no entry's `covers:` line naming it:
    - **a guard module**: a file `rust/guard/src/guards/<name>_hooks.rs` or `<name>_gate.rs`, or the same under `rust/guard/shared/src/guards/`, that `git diff -M --name-status` lists `A` (a rename is `R`, so it adds nothing; a guard's own submodule, `<name>_hooks/x.rs`, is not a module);
    - **a numeric threshold constant**: a module-level line (at column 0: a constant inside a function, an `impl` or an inline test module is not read) `[pub[(...)]] const NAME: <an integer or float type, or Duration> =`, in a non-test file (not `tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`, `testkit`, or under `tests/`) of the tooling - `rust/guard/`, every gate crate under `rust/gate/`, `rust/browser/` and `rust/embed/` (`detect::CONST_SCOPE`, T259-D2), whose NAME has a part (split on `_`) among the threshold words (`CAP`, `MAX`, `MIN`, `LIMIT`, `CEILING`, `FLOOR`, `BUDGET`, `THRESHOLD`, `PCT`, `PERCENT`, `RATIO`, `SLACK`, `LEEWAY`, `TIMEOUT`, `WAIT`, `IDLE`, `STALE`, `STALL`, `AGE`, `FRESH`, `EVERY`, `RETRIES`, `TRIES`, `ROUNDS`, `ROUND`, `S`, `MS`, `SECS`, `SECONDS`, `MINUTES`, `HOURS`, `DAYS`, `GB`, `MB`, `BYTES`, `TOKENS`, `KEEP`, `KEPT`, `CHARS`, `WORDS`, `RUNS`, `N`, `BAR`) and is not made of unit words alone (`GB`, `DAY_MICROS`, `SECONDS_A_DAY`), and which no such line anywhere in the scope held at the base - so a constant moved between files, or a file split by the 1,000-line bar, adds nothing;
    - **a make target in the gate and landing chain**: a target the Makefile reaches from the roots `done`, `quick`, `static`, `hooks-test`, `closing-checks`, `land`, `land-batch` and `land-tooling` (`detect::CHAIN`), transitively, through prerequisites and `$(MAKE) <target>` calls in recipes, that the base's Makefile did not reach - a new target, or an old one newly wired in;
    - **an agent file**: `.claude/agents/<name>.md` listed `A`;
    - **a landing step** (`detect::STEPS`): a name new against the base's text of the same file in one of three places - a row of the push's checks table (`Row("<name>"` in `rust/gate/crates/cohort/src/push.rs`), a phase of `make land` (`self.phase("<name>"` in `rust/gate/crates/land/src/land.rs`), or a gate script its first pass runs (the quoted names on the `const GATES` line of `land/cheap.rs`); and a landing refusal (`detect::REFUSALS`): `make land`'s first pass refuses through `stops.push(` calls in `land/cheap.rs` that carry no name, so they are counted, the k-th the item `landing refusal land/cheap.rs #k`, and a delta that raises the count adds the new numbers.
  - **The refusal** names each item with its kind, then prints the entry to write (the eleven fields with a hint each, and a `covers:` line per item), and the escape: `AUDIT_ENTRY_OK="<reason>"` (a reason of two words and eight characters, `l7r_shared::escape::enough`) passes it, the would-be refusal printed and the firing recorded in the guard log (`escaped`; each refusal `blocked`).
  - **The replay** (`--range BASE HEAD [--root R] [--empty-register]`): the same detection over a past delta, the register read from HEAD (or none), which measures the false fires.
  - **The first entries** (`dev/audits/`): `builders-context-cap.md`, `delegating-to-builders.md`, `disk-budget.md`, `blocking-definition.md`, `research-switch.md`, `started-task-mark-per-tree.md`, `task-numbers-one-writer.md`, `plan-review-merge-driver.md`, `review-tree.md`, and `audit-register.md` for the check itself (its two push rows, `audit-register` and its self-test, are landing steps the check detects, so the entry covers them); and three `kind: declined` entries, `declined-context-cap-600k.md`, `declined-terse-output-style.md` and `declined-shallow-clones.md`, the three options `docs/process-decisions.md`'s "Decisions NOT to do something" section lists (observed 2026-11-26, method: a read of that section after the merge of main 0c0ae9d878), with its figures and its reopening conditions as their falsifiers. Each figure is the agenda's (items 1, 12 and 13), `plan-done.md`'s (T244-T246, T254-T257) or `docs/process-decisions.md`'s, with its date; each threshold no record states is labeled GUESS; where no make target reproduces a measurement (the transcript pass of item 12, measured 2026-11-25 by a read-only pass over the builder transcripts since 2026-11-18, its method in the agenda), the entry says so and names the method's record.
  - **Recorded beside it**: a row in `docs/guards.md`, a paragraph in `docs/process-decisions.md` (beside its "Decisions NOT to do something" section, whose declined options are the register's `kind: declined` entries), a `scripts/tool-registry.json` entry, the Makefile's `audits` help line, `docs/make-targets.html`.

### T259 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** Every optimization or procedure that costs time or tokens has one entry saying what it buys, the dated measurement that justified it and how to repeat it, and the measurement and number that would show it costs more than it saves; `make audits` says which are due; and a landing that adds a guard, a threshold, a gate-chain step, a landing step or an agent arrives with its entry, or is told which entry to write; and an option weighed and declined is recorded the same way, with what would reopen it.
2. **The constraints.** The T259 line of tasks.md (one file per entry under dev/; the six fields; `make audits` lists the overdue; a landing that adds a guard, a cap or threshold, a gate or landing step, a mandatory check or a standing procedure without its entry is refused, the way a guard is refused without its test companion, naming the entry to write; the first entries). Agenda item 13 (what an entry holds, what warrants one - "not pure corrections that cost nothing" - and the backfill's sources). The brief: narrow and measurable, a guard firing on correct work worse than none, proven not to fire on the last 20 landings.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the GM's words of 2026-11-25 in agenda item 13 and its "Order" paragraph, quoted in the T259 line, and on declined options ("We should also make sure our processes record decisions about what NOT to implement for future reference in the same way we record decisions about the processes and tooling we DO implement.", request.md's T259 section). O: the replay of item 9 and the measurements each entry cites.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. THE DECISIONS:
   - T259-D1 FIVE DETECTORS, ON PATHS AND NAMES ONLY: the task line's six kinds map to what a delta can show without reading prose. A guard is a guard module; a cap or threshold is a threshold constant; a gate step is a make target newly in the chain; a landing step is a push check, a land phase or a landing gate script newly named (plan review round 1's D1b), or a landing refusal by count (round 2's D1-stops: the `stops.push(` calls of `land/cheap.rs` carry no name, but their count is a form a delta shows - measured 2026-11-26 (`git show <landing>:rust/gate/crates/land/src/land/cheap.rs | grep -c stops.push` at each of the 21 landings of the replay list): 6 at every one, so the count moves only when a refusal is added or removed, and counting cannot fire on a refactor that keeps them); a mandatory check is, for the review checks, an agent file. NOT DETECTED, on purpose: a rule line in a CLAUDE.md or `docs/` file telling a session to wait, serialize or always do a step, a new mandatory round of an existing agent, a standing order added to the builder brief - none has a form a check can tell from correct work, and a check firing on correct work teaches a session to escape every check (the brief; the root CLAUDE.md's "What is enforced"). Those agenda item 13 names as backfill sources (the rule lines, the agent files' standing orders and the builder brief, the review rounds, the escape log) enter the INITIAL backfill by their own enumeration, each with its method (T260, Found and left); only what that misses is added as found later, the route the GM gave ("after the initial backfill, we can backfill as we go, as we find things that we missed"), and `dev/audits/audit-register.md` names the gap.
   - T259-D2 THE CONSTANT SCOPE IS THE TOOLING, NOT THE ENGINE: `rust/guard/`, every gate crate under `rust/gate/`, `rust/browser/` and `rust/embed/` - every crate whose constants are a session's waits, caps, retries or bundle sizes, so cost time or tokens (the goal line's words). Widened twice by the plan reviews: round 1 (its D2) past the checks crate to the land and cohort crates - measured 2026-11-26 (a grep of their non-test files' module-level numeric names, the same word filter), 10 of their 17 names pass, each a knob (`CLAIMS_WAIT_S`, `COMMIT_TRIES`, `HANDOFF_FRESH_S`, ...) - and round 2 (its D2-rest) to the rest of the gate - measured 2026-11-26 (the same grep over the gate's other crates), 68 more names pass, among them the run lock's `CEILING_S` and `MUTEX_S`, `LOCK_WAIT_S`, `IDLE_S`, `IDLE_CAP_S`, `BUNDLE_TOKENS`, `TRIAGE_SKIP_MAX`, `GROWTH_CAP` - and the browser's 4 (`BODY_WAIT`, `CLOSE_WAIT`, `READY_WAIT`, `KEPT_EVENTS`; the embedder has none). `Duration` joins the numeric types (round 1's aside). LEFT OUT, the engine's crates (`rust/mode_a`, `rust/phases`, `rust/parked`): measured 2026-11-26 (the same grep over `rust/` outside the tooling), 64 names pass the filter there, every one a drawing rule (`MIN_TURN_DEG`, `GATE_MAX_FT`, `POND_PCT`, `SETBACK_LIMIT`), which costs a map's look, not a session's time, and is held already by the research labels and claims (`make claims-report`), `make tunables` and the stages' work budgets (`make work-budget`).
   - T259-D3 NEW IS BY NAME OVER THE WHOLE SCOPE, NOT BY FILE: a name absent from every such line of the scope at the base. A per-file comparison would fire on every file the file-scale bar splits and every constant moved. The known miss: a new threshold whose name the scope already holds elsewhere (a second `CAP`) is not seen - cheaper than a false fire. Its size, measured 2026-11-26 (the D4 grep, `uniq -d` over the kept names' lines): 14 of the 136 kept names stand on more than one line (151 lines), `CAP`, `LIMIT`, `LEEWAY`, `KEPT`, `ROUND_CAP`, `WAVE_N` and `WINDOW_S` among them; a new constant of one of those 14 names is the miss.
   - T259-D4 THE NAME FILTER: measured 2026-11-26 over the tooling scope (a grep of the 228 module-level numeric constant names of its non-test files, the detector's word lists applied), the threshold words keep 136, drop 90 and the unit-words rule drops 2 (`GB`, `SECONDS_A_DAY`). Measured 2026-11-25 over the first scope's 84 names, the threshold words kept 55, among them every knob the agenda names (`CAP_TOKENS`, `POLL_CHECK_S`, the round caps `PLAN_ROUND_CAP`, `SPEC_ROUND_CAP`, the static-run limit `STATIC_RUNS_A_TASK` through `RUNS`) and drop display sizes and fixed facts (27, among them `LARGEST`, `SHOWN`, `CHUNK`, `SIGTERM`, `DAY`, `MICROS`); names of unit words alone are dropped (2: `GB`, `SECONDS_A_DAY`). Before the filter, measured 2026-11-25 (the replay of item 9, `--empty-register`), the check fired on T245's `GB` (a unit, `1_000_000_000`) and `LARGEST` (how many of a place's largest entries the disk audit names, 4) - neither costs time or refuses anything.
   - T259-D5 THE CHAIN IS TRANSITIVE FROM FIXED ROOTS: `detect::CHAIN` names the eight roots every landing or builder's close runs; a target they reach through prerequisites or `$(MAKE)` calls (direct or through others) is in the chain. A target-specific variable line (`done: export X := ...`) is no rule. Measured 2026-11-25 over the 1,000 first-parent commits back to 2026-11-20 (`--range ... --empty-register`): the chain detector named `make closing-checks` and `make _quick`, both gate steps added in that span.
   - T259-D6 AN ENTRY COUNTS ONLY WHOLE: a stub with a `covers:` line would silence the check, so every entry's eleven fields are checked at every run, whatever the delta adds, and a malformed one refuses. `unmeasured` is allowed only with `first-audit:` naming the measurement that will be its first (the delegation to builders at all, never measured).
   - T259-D7 THE FORM IS MARKDOWN WITH A KEY-VALUE FRONT MATTER: one file per entry, as the agenda's proposal asks; why, in the Approach.
   - T259-D8 IN `make static` AS WELL AS THE PUSH: a builder's `make closing-checks` runs `make static`, so a missing entry is refused before the gate runs, not after it at the push. The push row needs `dev/audits` (the row's `needs`), so a fixture push in a tree with no register stays silent; the real tree holds it. 0.10 s a run with the four detectors (measured 2026-11-25, three runs of `--delta` in this clone after the build: 0.10, 0.11 s); 0.17 to 0.18 s with the five and the tooling scope (measured 2026-11-26, three runs of `--delta` under `/usr/bin/time` after the build: 0.18, 0.17, 0.17 s).
   - T259-D9 THE ESCAPE: `AUDIT_ENTRY_OK="<reason>"`, read by the check from the environment, so the one form serves `make static` and the push; recorded `escaped` with its reason in the guard log, each refusal `blocked`, so `make guard-log GUARD=audit-register` audits the check against its own falsifier (`audit-register.md`).
   - T259-D10 CADENCES AND UNSTATED THRESHOLDS ARE GUESS KNOBS: each entry's cadence, and every falsifier threshold no record states, is a knob labeled GUESS in its entry, the never-audited entries given the shortest cadence so `make audits` asks for them soonest.
   - T259-D11 A DECLINED OPTION IS AN ENTRY OF ITS OWN KIND: the GM's words of 2026-11-25 ("record decisions about what NOT to implement ... in the same way"). An entry's `kind:` is `adopted` or `declined`; a declined one carries the same fields, its `measured` and `measurement` the evidence that declined it, its `falsifier` and `threshold` what would reopen it, its `cost` `none: not built`, and it is audited on its cadence like any other, so `make audits` asks again whether the reopening condition holds. One register, not a second list: the lister, the form check and the cadences serve both. `docs/process-decisions.md` keeps the prose ("Decisions NOT to do something"); the entries carry its figures, and its three options today are the three declined entries.

### T227 (page session P7's cascade, 2026-11-24: record-format was dispatched on 0097 four times across features and the counter held 0 rounds; 2026-11-25: modal-form ran three rounds on sheet/barracks in four minutes and `make arbiter-bundle BATCH=1` said no round trigger was owed)

- **Approach**: The round cap (`rounds::cap_refusal`, `ROUND_CAP` 2) was sound. Two things kept it from being reached, and one more kept its ruling from being read.
  - **Cause 1, the feature reset.** `handle::handle_locked` replaced the whole check state with `{feature, dispatches}` whenever the active feature changed. That wiped every unit's `rounds`, `seen`, `own_edits`, `notes_read`, `rebased` and `round_batch`. Observed 2026-11-25, method: the source, and `.git/checks-open.json` of the coordinating clone. Its `feature` was 451 and it held no `record-format|q:0097` count, although its `dispatches` kept 13 record-format rows on q:0097, 4 of them dated 2026-11-24.
  - **Cause 2, a hand fix read as a first look.** `first_look` (374 wave 120, the arbiter on 0190) let a round go uncounted when its unread sentences were none of the check's own EDITs. Its stated rule is "text OTHER checks' edits added", but it tested the opposite: anything not its own. It also asked whether the own-EDIT text contained the whole sentence, and an EDIT that replaces a span inside a sentence never does. Observed 2026-11-25, method: the barracks rows of the same state (dispatch toolu_01QzUrB5 `counted` [barracks]; toolu_01HDWmSu `counted` [marsh] only; toolu_01TWD7L7 `counted` []), the three kept replies (round 1's EDIT "and a gate rowhouse was tiled; ...", rounds 2 and 3 with `EDIT: none`), and `git diff 32d0d88c55 6557ee05b7` of `sheet/barracks.md` (the EDIT applied inside a longer sentence, a Guesses bullet added and then taken out by hand). Each of rounds 2 and 3 was read as a first look, so `rounds` stayed at 1 and no third round was held.
  - **The fix: what survives a feature change.** Nothing is wiped. Every key of the state is keyed by unit or subject, not by feature, so a count follows its unit. A unit's HOME is the feature its count began in (`round_home`, written when its first round is counted, and for a unit counted before this change, the state's old `feature` at the switch). Its triggers are filed under its home (`arbiter::trip_under`), and its `continue` and `accept` are read from there (`arbiter::rulings_of`, `continues_of`, `closed_of`), as 451 T240 reads a plan round's rulings from its trigger's feature. `arbiter-ruled` already files a ruling where the owed row names it (`home.rs`). An owed record round (`round:<record check>|q:NNNN@N` or `|modal:...@N`) is every feature's to hold and batch (`arbiter::record_round` in `mine`). So `make arbiter-bundle BATCH=1` lists it under any feature, and `blocking` holds only that unit's dispatch. Why a home and not every feature's log: counts restarted with each feature, so the same trigger is ruled in two features 10 times today, for example `round:record-format|q:0047@3`. Reading every log would let an old `continue` lift a new cap, and would make a new trigger "already ruled".
  - **The fix: what counts as a first look.** A round is a first look only when every unread sentence carries another check's EDIT words on that subject and none carries its own. Matching is sentence by sentence, an EDIT's sentence inside the page's or the page's inside it. Text the session wrote between rounds, a finding fixed by hand, is the fix loop and is counted.
  - **The gate's readers.** The arbiter bundle's `counted` returned 0 unless the state's feature was the active one. It now reads the count whatever feature is active. Its counter section and the rounds line no longer say "in this feature".
  - **The refusal** reads "round N of `<check>` on <subject> passes its cap of C - ...". "in this feature" is cut, because it is no longer true.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no state wiped on a feature change; a unit's home filed, ruled and batched | `a_record_round_follows_its_unit_across_features` (handle) red on HEAD: the third round under the next feature let through (""); `a_new_feature_keeps_the_counts_their_home_and_the_dispatches` restated; arbiter `a_held_gate_and_a_batch_are_told_apart`'s record-round case | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| a first look only for other checks' EDIT text | `a_session_s_own_fixes_between_rounds_count_the_next_round` (rounds) red on HEAD: round 2 `counted` [] where [barracks] was wanted; `first_looks_and_fresh_readings_are_no_repeat`'s hand-written case | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |
| the arbiter bundle's count read under any feature | `the_round_counters` restated (sections) | n/a: tooling | none | n/a |

### T258 (the GM 2026-11-25: "I created https://github.com/EliAndrewC/diagram-tooling-state for the tooling state" - a clone's check answers and event logs live only in its .git, so a lost container loses them)

- **Approach**: `scripts/state-sync.sh`, with a push and a restore. `push` commits the common .git's `record-checks/` and `l7r-events/` into a bare git mirror at `<common .git>/tooling-state.git` and pushes the branch named for the clone to the private repository; `make land` and `make land-tooling` run it detached (`push --detach`) after their own push succeeded, and exit with their own code. `restore` (`make state-restore [FROM=<clone>]`, and from `sync-with-main.sh sync-in` for a clone that has no mirror yet) fetches a branch and merges it in: the answers by `l7r-gate record merge-answers` (each record's utc, the newer kept), a log by appending the lines the local log lacks. The audit entry is `dev/audits/tooling-state.md`. Every figure is in item 9.

| step | alone off: fixed and pinned | fresh block vs HEAD | pool manifests moved | the last resort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the push and the restore | `tests/hooks/test-state-sync.sh` on a local bare fixture remote, red before the script existed (item 9) | n/a: no engine code | none | n/a |

### T258 Approach (checklist part A)

1. **The goal, in the world.** A container is lost. Its replacement's clone, at its next sync-in, has the check answers and the event logs the lost container had pushed at its last landing, and no landing waited or was refused for it.
2. **The constraints.** The task line (tasks.md T258): both directories pushed at each landing (`make land` and `make land-tooling`, after the main push, never refusing it) and restored into a fresh clone or a replacement container (a make target, and the session-clone setup). The project's token, never printed, never on a command line, never in a config. The repository private, never linked or copied anywhere public. Handoffs and caches stay out. An audit-register entry with a falsifier. The brief: the mechanism chosen by measuring. A restore never overwrites a newer local answer, merged by each record's utc as `record merge-answers` does. Tests on a local bare fixture, never the real remote. A real push by hand at the end.
3. **Where each comes from.** G: the task line and `request.md` ("2026-11-25: before three parallel builders ... and the tooling-state repository"). O: the measurements of item 9.
4. **Do they describe the world here?** Yes. THE DECISIONS (their measurements are item 9's):
   - T258-D1 A GIT MIRROR, NOT TAR SNAPSHOTS: a tar snapshot re-sends everything at every landing, a mirror committed into sends everything at its branch's opening push and afterwards what changed. The mirror is `<common .git>/tooling-state.git`, bare. The answers are added from where they lie (`--work-tree=<common .git>`), with no copy made.
   - T258-D2 THE LOGS GO IN AS SEGMENTS of whole lines (`split -C`, the size `SEGMENT` in the script, a GUESS knob: any size under GitHub's per-file limit works). A log committed whole stored a new blob of its full size each landing, and the largest log was on its way to GitHub's per-file limit, past which every push would fail for good. An append-only file's segments never change, the last excepted. The mirror is repacked at each run so it stays small.
   - T258-D3 DETACHED, SO NO LANDING WAITS (the task line: "never refusing it", the brief: "never refusing or delaying"). `push --detach` starts the push in its own session and returns. What it costs, accepted by this builder: a detached push's failure cannot be said by the landing that started it, so it is logged (`<common .git>/tooling-state.log`, a JSON line a run) and said in a single line at the NEXT landing (`the last push FAILED ...`). The alternative priced: a foreground push says its failure at once and delays every landing by the push's seconds. `make state-push` by hand is the foreground form. A lock (flock) lets a single run work the mirror, and a push that meets a running push is skipped, the next landing's carrying its state.
   - T258-D4 A BRANCH A CLONE, named for the clone the common .git belongs to, so a worktree's state is its clone's (the suite's worktree case). "Per-clone" is the task line's word. A replacement container's clone of the same name takes that branch.
   - T258-D5 NEVER A FORCE PUSH, AND A FRESH MIRROR TAKES THE BRANCH IN BEFORE IT COMMITS. A mirror that has never seen its branch (a fresh clone, a replacement container) fetches and merges the remote's state before it commits, so the commit removes nothing and its push is a fast-forward (the suite's replacement and fresh-clone cases). A push the remote refuses because another container moved the branch is fetched, merged in and pushed on top, as a merge commit (the suite's shared-branch case).
   - T258-D6 THE RESTORE MERGES, NEVER OVERWRITES. Answers: `l7r-gate record merge-answers`, the answer store's other writer, unchanged - a unit only the branch holds is copied, a unit both hold keeps every fingerprint either answered and the record of the later utc (the suite's newer-here case). Logs: the branch's segments joined, and the lines the local log lacks appended (`O_APPEND`, as the hooks write, and both readers sort by `t`, per `refile.rs`'s header). A local line is never removed. A `.tmp` file (a half-written answer or log) is not pushed.
   - T258-D7 THE SESSION-CLONE SETUP IS `sync-in`: a clone is made by a bare `git clone`, and `sync-with-main.sh sync-in` is where its config is set (`ensure_git_config`), so `sync_in` runs `state-sync.sh restore --if-fresh`. With no mirror yet it makes the mirror and restores in the background. A clone that has a mirror does nothing (the suite's setup case). A CONVENTION for where "the session-clone setup" is. `make state-restore` is the door by hand.
   - T258-D8 A CLONE WHOSE ORIGIN IS NOT GITHUB MAIN'S DOES NOTHING unless `STATE_REMOTE` names a remote (the suite's skipped case): the other suites' fixture clones run `sync-with-main.sh` and must never reach the real repository. The landings call the script from the Makefile's recipes, which no suite runs. The suite itself holds git to the file transport (`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`) and its answers and log lines are made up.
   - T258-D9 THE TOKEN as `sync-with-main.sh` hands it: `l7r-gate github-token` into `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `scripts/git-askpass-token.sh` as git's askpass, `credential.helper` emptied for the mirror's calls. The remote is passed by URL at each call and never stored, so the mirror's config holds no remote (the suite reads it).
   - T258-D10 A SHELL SCRIPT, NOT A GATE CRATE: it is git plumbing end to end, beside `sync-with-main.sh` and `land-tooling.sh`, which are shell for the same reason. Its only logic with rules, the answers' merge, is the gate's and is reused. The easier route where nothing rules.
   - T258-D11 HANDOFFS AND CACHES STAY OUT: only `record-checks` and `l7r-events` are added to the mirror's index.
5. **The order.** Alone; before a container is next replaced.
6. **The exits.** Green: `make closing-checks T=T258`, and the real push. Red: what failed recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be done ruled through `make arbiter-ask`.
7. **The search smell.** none.
8. **The budget.** One landing.
9. **Done, measured.**
   - THE STATE: 2,837 answer files in 71 MB and 31 logs in 122 MB, the largest log 38.6 MB, measured 2026-11-25 (`find | wc -l`, `du -sh` and `ls -l` on diagram-backlog's common .git).
   - RED FIRST: 36 of the suite's 41 checks failed with no script and 5 passed (each asserts an absence), then 41 of 41 passed with it, measured 2026-11-25 (`bash tests/hooks/test-state-sync.sh`, before and after `scripts/state-sync.sh` was written).
   - D1's CHOICE: a tar.gz of both directories was 33.8 MB and took 4.7 s, owed at every landing, measured 2026-11-25 (`time tar -czf` on that state). The mirror sent 29 MB at its opening push and then 0.72 MB in 9.7 s and 0.13 MB in 2.6 s at the next 2 pushes, measured 2026-11-25 (`state-sync.sh push` to a local bare remote, the seconds and bytes of its log lines, the machine at load 24 to 28).
   - D2's GROWTH: with logs committed whole the mirror grew 9 MB a commit, measured 2026-11-25 (`du -sh` of a scratch mirror before and after a commit of 15 appended lines), and with segments and the repack it stayed at 29 MB across 3 pushes, measured 2026-11-25 (`du -sh` after each push).
   - D3's WAIT: `push --detach` returned in 0.03 s, measured 2026-11-25 (`time bash scripts/state-sync.sh push --detach`).
   - THE REAL PUSH, by hand: the branch `diagram-backlog` went up as 29.3 MB in 8.7 s, measured 2026-11-25 (`make state-push` in this worktree at load 26, its own line), and `git ls-remote` read the remote's tip back equal to the mirror's. The next push sent 0.13 MB in 7.0 s, measured 2026-11-25 (`make state-push`, its own line). `make state-restore` over the full state took 15.9 s and brought 0 answers and 0 lines, everything being here already, measured 2026-11-25 (its own line).
10. **Before moving a constant.** n/a.
11. **Before fitting things into room.** n/a.
12. **Before any fix.** Nothing is fixed: a new operation. No map changes.

**Found and left?**
- not a defect (constitution XIV): a landing's push sends each grown log's last segment whole where the appended lines are far smaller, because git's thin pack found no delta base for the segment - 28 appended lines, a 7 KB diff, packed to 125 KB at `pack.window` 10 and at 50, measured 2026-11-25 (`git diff | wc -c` and `git pack-objects --thin --revs --stdout | wc -c` between the mirror's last 2 commits). No visible effect and no finding broken, the push being detached and under the audit entry's threshold. Recorded in the audit entry's known limits.
- not a defect (constitution XIV): `l7r-gate check audit-register` does not see this landing step, a script a recipe calls being none of the kinds its detectors read (`audit_register/detect.rs`'s header), observed 2026-11-25, method: `l7r-gate check audit-register --delta` on this delta named 0 mechanisms. Its header calls a miss cheaper than a false fire. The entry is written all the same, with no `covers:` line. A title for the coordinating session, since this builder files no task: "audit-register: a script newly called from make land's or land-tooling's recipe is a landing step no detector sees (451 T258's state-sync.sh)".

### T262 (451 T261's builder, 2026-11-26: PLAN_REVIEW_OK rode pushes where the plan gate owed nothing in 7 of 12 escape records replayed at their commits, and 155 of 160 records name a cause the gate never had)

- **Approach**: the gate is asked before the escape is read, at the tick and at the push, and an honored escape's record says what was held.
  - **The tick** (`tick_gate`, `rust/gate/crates/plan/src/plan.rs`). Where the gate owes nothing for the task and `PLAN_REVIEW_OK` is set, the tick proceeds and prints one line, `tick: the plan gate owes nothing - drop PLAN_REVIEW_OK`. No bypass record and no guard-log event is written (before: nothing was said). `make land` runs this tick, so it prints the line too.
  - **The push** (`scripts/gates/plan-gate.sh`, run by `sync-with-main.sh` and by `make land`'s cheap refusals). It honored the escape BEFORE asking the gate, which is how a clean push got a record. It now asks `l7r-gate plan push` first; where that lists nothing and the escape is set it prints `plan-gate: the plan gate owes nothing - drop PLAN_REVIEW_OK` and exits 0, with no record and no guard-log event.
  - **A bare token on a clean gate** (`PLAN_REVIEW_OK=x`) is told the same line and is not asked for a reason: no escape is being taken, so there is nothing for a reason to explain.
  - **The record** (`bypass_record`). Where the escape is honored, the record in `dev/bypass-log/` gains `held`: a list of `{feature, rule, blocks}`, one row per feature the gate held. `blocks` is every block key the judgment listed, whole (a block's key is its heading line; `(removed) <heading>` for a recorded block the plan no longer has; `preamble` for the text above the first heading): the keys owed a review under `plan-review-stale`, the BLOCKED keys under `plan-review-blocked`, and none under `plan-review-missing` and `plan-missing`, where the gate lists no block. The refusal's own text shows only its first keys, each cut short (`judge_held`'s `take(5)` and `take(60)`, observed 2026-11-26, method: `plan/status.rs` read); the record takes the full list from `status::judge_held`, which `judge_in`, `owed_for` and `push_owed` now wrap. The push's record is written by `l7r-gate plan door bypass-record <root> push <why> <range>`, which computes what is held over the range itself.
  - **"Checked against what the gate held"** (the task's title) is built as the task's body says it: the record carries what was held beside the reason, so a reader compares them. The reason's wording is not parsed or refused: no word list decides whether a sentence names a block.
  - **`make audit` is not changed.** Its Bypasses listing still prints each record's reason. The task's line says the record carries the blocks "so make audit and the measurements classify escapes by what was held"; this task builds the record they will read, and no listing or measurement over `held` (the brief scopes the build to the rule and the record; a count by `held` is a title in the builder's report, not filed here).
